e.en: She {circumnavigated} Britain solo in a small yacht.
e.zh: 她独自驾驶小型游艇环绕英国航行了一周。

circumnavigates.t: v. 环航（第三人称单数）

e.en: The satellite {circumnavigates} the earth every ninety minutes.
e.zh: 这颗卫星每九十分钟绕地球一圈。

e.en: He {circumnavigates} the lake on his morning run.
e.zh: 他晨跑时会绕湖跑一圈。

circumnavigating.t: v. 正在环航（现在分词）

e.en: {Circumnavigating} the world solo is an extraordinary achievement.
e.zh: 独自环游世界是一项非凡的成就。

e.en: They spent two years {circumnavigating} the Pacific Ocean.
e.zh: 他们花了两年时间环绕太平洋航行。

e.en: His {circumnavigation} of the globe took nearly three years.
e.zh: 他环游地球的航行历时近三年。

e.en: The first solo {circumnavigation} was completed in 1898.
e.zh: 首次单人环球航行于1898年完成。

e.en: Multiple {circumnavigations} have made him a sailing legend.
e.zh: 多次环球航行让他成为帆船界的传奇。

e.en: Early {circumnavigations} mapped previously unknown coastlines.
e.zh: 早期的环球航行绘制了此前未知的海岸线。

circumpolar.t: adj. 绕极的；环绕极地的

e.en: Polar bears live in the {circumpolar} regions of the Arctic.
e.zh: 北极熊生活在北极的环极地区。

e.en: Several {circumpolar} stars never dip below the horizon.
e.zh: 有几颗拱极星从不会落到地平线以下。

e.en: New regulations {circumscribe} how companies handle user data.
e.zh: 新规对公司处理用户数据的方式作出了限制。

e.en: Geometry students learn to {circumscribe} a circle around a triangle.
e.zh: 几何学生要学会在三角形外接一个圆。

circumscribed.t:
adj. 受限制的
v. circumscribe 的过去式

e.en: Her authority is sharply {circumscribed} by company policy.
e.zh: 她的权力受到公司政策的严格限制。

e.en: The teacher {circumscribed} a circle around the square.
e.zh: 老师在正方形外画了一个外接圆。

e.en: The law placed strict {circumscription} on press freedom.
e.zh: 该法律对新闻自由施加了严格的限制。

e.en: The {circumscription} of the species's range concerns biologists.
e.zh: 该物种分布范围的缩减让生物学家感到担忧。

circumspect.t: adj. 谨慎的；考虑周到的

e.en: Be {circumspect} when sharing personal details online.
e.zh: 在网上分享个人信息时要谨慎小心。

e.en: The CEO was {circumspect} about future hiring plans.
e.zh: 这位 CEO 对未来的招聘计划态度谨慎。

e.en: Handle the negotiation with great {circumspection} and patience.
e.zh: 处理这次谈判要非常谨慎且有耐心。

e.en: Her {circumspection} prevented many costly business mistakes.
e.zh: 她的谨慎避免了许多代价高昂的商业失误。

circumspectly.t: adv. 谨慎地；小心翼翼地

e.en: The diplomat answered each question {circumspectly} and briefly.
e.zh: 这位外交官谨慎而简短地回答了每个问题。

e.en: Invest {circumspectly} during periods of market uncertainty.
e.zh: 在市场不确定时期要谨慎投资。

e.en: Under no {circumstance} should you share your password.
e.zh: 在任何情况下都不应该分享你的密码。

e.en: This unusual {circumstance} requires a creative solution.
e.zh: 这种特殊情况需要一个有创意的解决方案。

e.en: Given the {circumstances}, postponing the wedding seems wise.
e.zh: 考虑到目前的情况,推迟婚礼似乎是明智的。

e.en: The accident occurred under suspicious {circumstances}.
e.zh: 这起事故发生在可疑的情况下。

circumstantial.t: adj. 间接的（证据）；视情况而定的

e.en: The prosecution relied entirely on {circumstantial} evidence.
e.zh: 控方完全依赖间接证据。

e.en: Their meeting was purely {circumstantial}, not planned beforehand.
e.zh: 他们的相遇纯属偶然,并非事先安排。

circumstantially.t: adv. 间接地；根据情况地

e.en: The defendant was only {circumstantially} linked to the crime.
e.zh: 被告与该罪行仅有间接的关联。

e.en: She described the events {circumstantially} and in great detail.
e.zh: 她详细而具体地描述了整个事件经过。

e.en: Astronomers detected dust in the {circumstellar} disk.
e.zh: 天文学家在恒星周围的尘埃盘中检测到尘埃。

e.en: Planets typically form within {circumstellar} regions of young stars.
e.zh: 行星通常在年轻恒星周围的区域形成。

circumvent.t: v. 规避；绕开（规则、限制）

e.en: Hackers found ways to {circumvent} the new security measures.
e.zh: 黑客找到了绕过新安全措施的方法。

e.en: The company tried to {circumvent} environmental regulations.
e.zh: 该公司试图规避环保法规。

e.en: The {circumvention} of copyright protection is illegal.
e.zh: 规避版权保护是违法的。

e.en: VPNs are often used for {circumvention} of regional blocks.
e.zh: VPN 常被用来绕过地区限制。

e.en: The kids loved the acrobats at the {circus} last night.
e.zh: 孩子们昨晚很喜欢马戏团的杂技演员。

e.en: The press conference turned into a complete {circus}.
e.zh: 这场新闻发布会完全变成了一场闹剧。

e.en: Modern {circuses} have largely stopped using wild animals.
e.zh: 现代马戏团基本上已经不再使用野生动物。

e.en: Traveling {circuses} were once a major form of entertainment.
e.zh: 巡回马戏团曾是主要的娱乐形式之一。

cirencester.t: n. 赛伦塞斯特（英国城镇名）

e.en: {Cirencester} is a charming market town in the Cotswolds.
e.zh: 赛伦塞斯特是科茨沃尔德地区一座迷人的集镇。

e.en: Roman ruins can still be seen around {Cirencester} today.
e.zh: 如今在赛伦塞斯特周围仍能看到罗马遗迹。

e.en: The hikers camped beside a glacial {cirque} high in the Alps.
e.zh: 徒步者在阿尔卑斯山高处的一个冰斗旁扎营。

e.en: A small lake had formed inside the mountain {cirque}.
e.zh: 山间的冰斗里形成了一个小湖。

e.en: Heavy drinking over decades can cause liver {cirrhosis}.
e.zh: 长达几十年的酗酒会导致肝硬化。

e.en: The doctor diagnosed him with advanced {cirrhosis}.
e.zh: 医生诊断他患有晚期肝硬化。

e.en: Wispy {cirrus} clouds drifted high across the morning sky.
e.zh: 丝缕状的卷云在清晨高空中飘浮。

e.en: {Cirrus} clouds often signal a change in the weather.
e.zh: 卷云通常预示着天气即将变化。

cis.t: adj. 顺式的（化学）；顺性别的

e.en: She identifies as a {cis} woman and a feminist.
e.zh: 她认为自己是一名顺性别女性和女权主义者。

e.en: The chemistry exam asked us to identify the {cis} isomer.
e.zh: 化学考试要求我们辨认出顺式异构体。

cisapride.t: n. 西沙必利（一种胃动力药）

e.en: Doctors stopped prescribing {cisapride} due to heart risks.
e.zh: 由于心脏风险,医生已停止开西沙必利。

e.en: {Cisapride} was once used to treat severe heartburn.
e.zh: 西沙必利曾被用于治疗严重的胃灼热。

cisco.t: n. 思科（网络设备公司）

e.en: Our company uses {Cisco} routers throughout the office network.
e.zh: 我们公司在整个办公网络中都使用思科路由器。

e.en: She passed the {Cisco} networking certification exam last month.
e.zh: 她上个月通过了思科网络认证考试。

e.en: The oncologist prescribed {cisplatin} for her ovarian cancer.
e.zh: 肿瘤科医生为她的卵巢癌开了顺铂。

e.en: {Cisplatin} is a widely used chemotherapy drug.
e.zh: 顺铂是一种广泛使用的化疗药物。

cissy.t: n. 娘娘腔；胆小的男孩

e.en: The bullies called him a {cissy} for crying at the movie.
e.zh: 那些恶霸因为他看电影哭了就叫他娘娘腔。

e.en: Don't be such a {cissy} about a little cold water.
e.zh: 别因为一点凉水就这么娇气。

cistercian.t: n./adj. 熙笃会修士；熙笃会的

e.en: The {cistercian} monks lived a quiet life of prayer.
e.zh: 熙笃会修士过着安静的祈祷生活。

e.en: We toured an old {cistercian} abbey in France.
e.zh: 我们参观了法国一座古老的熙笃会修道院。

e.en: The toilet {cistern} keeps refilling on its own.
e.zh: 马桶水箱总是自己不停地注水。

e.en: Rainwater is collected in a large {cistern} outside.
e.zh: 雨水被收集到屋外的一个大蓄水池里。

e.en: In old slang, a {cit} meant a city dweller.
e.zh: 在旧时俚语中,cit 指的是城里人。

e.en: The novel mocks the wealthy London {cit} of that era.
e.zh: 小说嘲讽了那个时代富有的伦敦市民。

e.en: Tourists climbed up to the ancient {citadel} at sunset.
e.zh: 游客们在日落时分爬上了那座古老的城堡。

e.en: The library is a {citadel} of free thought.
e.zh: 图书馆是自由思想的堡垒。

e.en: Please add a {citation} for that statistic in your essay.
e.zh: 请为论文里的那个数据加上引用出处。

e.en: The officer issued a {citation} for illegal parking.
e.zh: 警察因违章停车开了一张罚单。

e.en: Her paper has thousands of {citations} on Google Scholar.
e.zh: 她的论文在谷歌学术上有数千次引用。

e.en: Drivers received several {citations} during the holiday weekend.
e.zh: 司机们在假日周末收到了好几张罚单。

cite.t:
v. 引用；援引
v. 表彰

e.en: Always {cite} your sources when writing a research paper.
e.zh: 写研究论文时务必标明引用来源。

e.en: Critics often {cite} cost as the main issue.
e.zh: 批评者常把成本列为主要问题。

cited.t: v. 引用（cite 的过去式）

e.en: The study is widely {cited} in climate research.
e.zh: 这项研究在气候研究中被广泛引用。

e.en: He {cited} family reasons for leaving the job.
e.zh: 他以家庭原因为由辞去了工作。

cites.t: v. 引用（cite 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The article {cites} three independent expert sources.
e.zh: 这篇文章引用了三位独立专家的来源。

e.en: She often {cites} her grandmother's advice in conversation.
e.zh: 她聊天时常常引用奶奶的建议。

e.en: I opened a savings account at {citibank} last week.
e.zh: 我上周在花旗银行开了一个储蓄账户。

e.en: The {citibank} branch downtown closes at six.
e.zh: 市中心那家花旗银行分行六点关门。

e.en: {Citicorp} merged with Travelers Group back in 1998.
e.zh: 花旗公司在1998年与旅行者集团合并。

e.en: The old {citicorp} tower still dominates the Manhattan skyline.
e.zh: 老花旗公司大楼依旧是曼哈顿天际线的主角。

e.en: Many {cities} are investing in better public transit.
e.zh: 许多城市正在投资改善公共交通。

e.en: She has visited over thirty {cities} in Europe.
e.zh: 她已经去过欧洲三十多个城市了。

citified.t: adj. 都市化的；城市气派的

e.en: His {citified} accent surprised his country relatives.
e.zh: 他那带城市味的口音让乡下亲戚很惊讶。

e.en: The small town has become noticeably {citified} recently.
e.zh: 这个小镇最近明显变得城市化了。

citing.t: v. 引用（cite 的现在分词）

e.en: She declined the offer, {citing} health reasons.
e.zh: 她以健康原因为由拒绝了这个邀请。

e.en: The professor warned students against {citing} unreliable websites.
e.zh: 教授提醒学生不要引用不可靠的网站。

e.en: Every {citizen} has the right to vote in elections.
e.zh: 每位公民都有在选举中投票的权利。

e.en: He became a Canadian {citizen} after living there ten years.
e.zh: 他在加拿大住了十年后成为该国公民。

citizenry.t: n. 全体公民；市民（总称）

e.en: The mayor addressed the {citizenry} during the town hall.
e.zh: 市长在市政厅向全体市民发表讲话。

e.en: An informed {citizenry} is essential to democracy.
e.zh: 知情的公民群体对民主至关重要。

e.en: Concerned {citizens} gathered to protest the new law.
e.zh: 忧心的市民们聚集起来抗议这项新法律。

e.en: All {citizens} must carry a valid ID card.
e.zh: 所有公民都必须随身携带有效身份证。

e.en: She applied for British {citizenship} after her marriage.
e.zh: 她婚后申请了英国国籍。

e.en: Good {citizenship} means caring about your community.
e.zh: 好公民意识意味着关心自己的社区。

citizenships.t: n. 公民身份（citizenship 的复数）

e.en: He holds dual {citizenships} in Japan and Brazil.
e.zh: 他拥有日本和巴西的双重国籍。

e.en: Some countries do not allow multiple {citizenships}.
e.zh: 有些国家不允许拥有多重国籍。

e.en: Magnesium {citrate} is often used to relieve constipation.
e.zh: 柠檬酸镁常被用来缓解便秘。

e.en: The lab added sodium {citrate} to the blood sample.
e.zh: 实验室在血样中加入了柠檬酸钠。

e.en: Lemons contain a lot of {citric} acid.
e.zh: 柠檬里含有大量柠檬酸。

e.en: The candy has a sharp {citric} flavor.
e.zh: 这种糖果带有强烈的柠檬酸味。

e.en: She wore a ring set with a yellow {citrine}.
e.zh: 她戴着一枚镶有黄色黄水晶的戒指。

e.en: {Citrine} is the traditional birthstone for November.
e.zh: 黄水晶是十一月的传统诞生石。

e.en: He drives a small blue {citroen} around Paris.
e.zh: 他开着一辆蓝色的小雪铁龙在巴黎四处转。

e.en: The classic {citroen} 2CV is beloved in France.
e.zh: 经典的雪铁龙2CV在法国深受喜爱。

e.en: Candied {citron} peel is a key fruitcake ingredient.
e.zh: 蜜饯香橼皮是水果蛋糕的关键原料。

e.en: The {citron} fruit looks like a giant lemon.
e.zh: 香橼果实看起来像一颗巨大的柠檬。

e.en: We lit {citronella} candles to keep mosquitoes away.
e.zh: 我们点了香茅蜡烛来驱蚊。

e.en: This soap has a fresh {citronella} scent.
e.zh: 这款肥皂带有清新的香茅香味。

citrus.t:
n. 柑橘类水果
adj. 柑橘的

e.en: Florida is famous for its sweet {citrus} fruits.
e.zh: 佛罗里达以其甜美的柑橘水果而闻名。

e.en: The perfume has a bright {citrus} top note.
e.zh: 这款香水有清新的柑橘前调。

e.en: Tokyo is the largest {city} in Japan.
e.zh: 东京是日本最大的城市。

e.en: I love walking around the {city} at night.
e.zh: 我喜欢晚上在城市里散步。

cityscape.t: n. 城市景观；都市风光

e.en: The hotel offers a stunning {cityscape} view at night.
e.zh: 酒店夜晚可以欣赏到迷人的城市景观。

e.en: He paints {cityscape} scenes of old Shanghai.
e.zh: 他画的是老上海的城市风景。

citywide.t:
adj. 全市范围的
adv. 遍及全市

e.en: The mayor announced a {citywide} recycling program.
e.zh: 市长宣布了一项全市范围的回收计划。

e.en: There was a {citywide} blackout last night.
e.zh: 昨晚发生了全市范围的停电。

e.en: We spent a weekend exploring {ciudad} de México.
e.zh: 我们花了一个周末探索墨西哥城。

e.en: The Spanish word {ciudad} simply means city.
e.zh: 西班牙语单词 ciudad 就是城市的意思。

e.en: The rare {civet} was spotted near the rainforest stream.
e.zh: 那只罕见的麝香猫出现在雨林溪边。

e.en: Some coffee is made from beans eaten by a {civet}.
e.zh: 有些咖啡是由麝香猫吃过的咖啡豆制成的。

civic.t: adj. 城市的；市民的；公民的

e.en: Voting is an important {civic} duty.
e.zh: 投票是一项重要的公民义务。

e.en: The new {civic} center opens to the public tomorrow.
e.zh: 新的市民中心明天向公众开放。

e.en: Schools should teach {civics} so kids understand government.
e.zh: 学校应该教公民课,让孩子们了解政府。

e.en: My {civics} teacher made politics genuinely interesting.
e.zh: 我的公民课老师让政治变得真正有趣。

civil.t:
adj. 民事的；公民的
adj. 有礼貌的

e.en: Please keep the discussion {civil} and respectful.
e.zh: 请保持讨论文明而有礼。

e.en: They had a small {civil} ceremony at city hall.
e.zh: 他们在市政厅举行了一场小型的世俗婚礼。

civilian.t:
n. 平民；百姓
adj. 民用的

e.en: The soldier returned to {civilian} life after the war.
e.zh: 那位士兵战后回归了平民生活。

e.en: No {civilian} casualties were reported in the incident.
e.zh: 事件中没有平民伤亡的报告。

e.en: The {civilianization} of police roles has reduced costs.
e.zh: 警察岗位的文职化降低了成本。

e.en: Many countries pursued {civilianization} of military support jobs.
e.zh: 许多国家推动军事辅助岗位的文职化。

e.en: The army was ordered to protect innocent {civilians}.
e.zh: 军队奉命保护无辜的平民。

e.en: Hundreds of {civilians} fled the conflict zone overnight.
e.zh: 数百名平民在一夜之间逃离了冲突地区。

civilisation.t: n. 文明（civilization 的英式拼写）

e.en: Ancient Egyptian {civilisation} flourished along the Nile river.
e.zh: 古埃及文明在尼罗河沿岸繁荣兴盛。

e.en: After hiking for days, we welcomed signs of {civilisation}.
e.zh: 徒步好几天后,看到文明社会的迹象真令人欣慰。

civilisations.t: n. 文明（复数，英式拼写）

e.en: The museum showcases artifacts from many ancient {civilisations}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了许多古代文明的文物。

e.en: Lost {civilisations} continue to fascinate archaeologists today.
e.zh: 失落的文明至今仍令考古学家着迷。

civilise.t: v. 教化；使文明（英式拼写）

e.en: Education can {civilise} even the roughest of behaviors.
e.zh: 教育能让最粗野的行为也变得文明。

e.en: Colonial powers claimed they wanted to {civilise} other lands.
e.zh: 殖民列强声称他们想要开化其他地方。

e.en: Let's discuss this in a {civilised} manner over tea.
e.zh: 我们边喝茶边以文明的方式讨论这件事吧。

e.en: Modern medicine is a hallmark of {civilised} society.
e.zh: 现代医学是文明社会的一个标志。

civilising.t: v. 教化（现在分词，英式拼写）

e.en: Music has a {civilising} effect on restless children.
e.zh: 音乐对躁动的孩子有教化作用。

e.en: The empire spoke of its supposed {civilising} mission.
e.zh: 那个帝国宣扬其所谓的开化使命。

e.en: Online discussions often lack basic {civility} these days.
e.zh: 如今网上讨论常常缺乏基本的礼貌。

e.en: He greeted his rival with cold {civility}.
e.zh: 他冷冷而有礼地向对手打了招呼。

e.en: The fall of Roman {civilization} took several centuries.
e.zh: 罗马文明的衰落花了好几个世纪。

e.en: Smartphones are arguably a marvel of modern {civilization}.
e.zh: 智能手机可以说是现代文明的奇迹。

civilizational.t: adj. 文明的；与文明相关的

e.en: Climate change presents a {civilizational} challenge for humanity.
e.zh: 气候变化对人类构成了文明层面的挑战。

e.en: The two regions have deep {civilizational} differences.
e.zh: 这两个地区存在深层的文明差异。

e.en: Several great {civilizations} once thrived in Mesopotamia.
e.zh: 几个伟大的文明曾在美索不达米亚兴盛。

e.en: Sci-fi often imagines contact with alien {civilizations}.
e.zh: 科幻作品常常想象与外星文明的接触。

e.en: Good manners help {civilize} our daily interactions.
e.zh: 良好的礼仪有助于让日常交往更文明。

e.en: Critics argue that prisons rarely {civilize} their inmates.
e.zh: 批评者认为监狱很少能教化在押人员。

e.en: In a {civilized} society, everyone deserves basic rights.
e.zh: 在文明社会中,每个人都应享有基本权利。

e.en: They had a {civilized} divorce without any drama.
e.zh: 他们文明地分手,没有任何闹剧。

civilizing.t: v. 教化（civilize 的现在分词）

e.en: Public libraries play a {civilizing} role in any neighborhood.
e.zh: 公共图书馆在任何社区都起到教化作用。

e.en: She spent years {civilizing} her unruly garden into order.
e.zh: 她花了好几年把杂乱的花园整理得井井有条。

e.en: The neighbors greeted each other {civilly} despite past disputes.
e.zh: 尽管以往有过争执,邻居们仍然礼貌地互相打招呼。

e.en: He responded {civilly} to the harsh criticism.
e.zh: 面对严厉的批评,他礼貌地作出了回应。

civita.t: n. 奇维塔（地名，意大利语 città）

e.en: The scholar referenced {Civita} in his medieval history lecture.
e.zh: 那位学者在中世纪史讲座中提到了奇维塔。

e.en: We visited {Civita} di Bagnoregio during our trip to Italy.
e.zh: 我们在意大利旅行时参观了白露里治奥的奇维塔小镇。

e.en: The soldier changed into {civvy} clothes after his shift.
e.zh: 那名士兵下班后换上了便服。

e.en: He missed wearing {civvy} attire during deployment.
e.zh: 派驻期间他很怀念穿便装的日子。

clack.t:
n. 咔哒声
v. 发出咔哒声

e.en: I could hear the {clack} of her heels on the floor.
e.zh: 我能听见她高跟鞋在地板上发出的咔嗒声。

e.en: The keyboard keys {clack} loudly in the quiet office.
e.zh: 键盘按键在安静的办公室里发出响亮的咔嗒声。

clacking.t: v. 发出咔哒声（clack 的现在分词）

e.en: The {clacking} of knitting needles filled the room.
e.zh: 编织针的咔嗒声充满了整个房间。

e.en: She kept {clacking} her pen against the desk nervously.
e.zh: 她紧张地用钢笔不停地敲击桌子。

clacton.t: n. 克拉克顿（英国地名）

e.en: We spent the weekend at the seaside in {Clacton}.
e.zh: 我们在克拉克顿海边度过了周末。

e.en: {Clacton}-on-Sea is a popular British holiday destination.
e.zh: 滨海克拉克顿是英国一个热门的度假胜地。

clad.t:
adj. 穿着…的
v. 覆盖（clothe 的过去式）

e.en: The hikers were {clad} in waterproof jackets.
e.zh: 徒步者们都穿着防水夹克。

e.en: The building is {clad} in shiny metal panels.
e.zh: 这栋建筑外墙覆盖着闪亮的金属板。

e.en: The new {cladding} improves the building's insulation.
e.zh: 新的外墙覆层改善了建筑的保温效果。

e.en: They replaced the unsafe {cladding} after the fire.
e.zh: 火灾发生后他们更换了不安全的外墙板。

e.en: Birds form a {clade} that includes all their dinosaur ancestors.
e.zh: 鸟类构成的演化支包含了它们所有的恐龙祖先。

e.en: Scientists identified a new {clade} of ancient mammals.
e.zh: 科学家发现了古代哺乳动物的一个新分支。

claim.t:
v. 声称；索取
n. 主张；索赔

e.en: You can {claim} a refund if the product is defective.
e.zh: 如果产品有缺陷,你可以申请退款。

e.en: His {claim} that the data was fake turned out to be true.
e.zh: 他声称数据是伪造的,结果证明属实。

e.en: The {claimant} provided documents to support her case.
e.zh: 原告提供了文件来支持她的诉求。

e.en: Each {claimant} must fill out the insurance form online.
e.zh: 每位申请人必须在网上填写保险表格。

claimed.t: v. 声称（过去式）；已认领

e.en: She {claimed} she had never received the email.
e.zh: 她声称自己从未收到过那封邮件。

e.en: The lost wallet was finally {claimed} by its owner.
e.zh: 丢失的钱包最终被失主认领了。

claiming.t: v. 声称；索取（现在分词）

e.en: He is {claiming} ownership of the abandoned property.
e.zh: 他正在主张那处废弃房产的所有权。

e.en: Many users are {claiming} the new update is buggy.
e.zh: 很多用户都说新版本有很多漏洞。

claims.t:
n. 索赔；主张（复数）
v. 声称

e.en: The company {claims} its products are eco-friendly.
e.zh: 该公司声称其产品环保。

e.en: Insurance {claims} usually take a few weeks to process.
e.zh: 保险理赔通常需要几周时间处理。

e.en: She bought a box of {Clairol} hair dye at the drugstore.
e.zh: 她在药妆店买了一盒可丽柔染发剂。

e.en: {Clairol} has been a popular hair-care brand for decades.
e.zh: 可丽柔几十年来一直是热门的护发品牌。

e.en: She claims to have {clairvoyance} and can predict the future.
e.zh: 她自称拥有透视能力,能够预知未来。

e.en: His apparent {clairvoyance} about the market surprised investors.
e.zh: 他对市场看似神奇的预知能力让投资者们大为惊讶。

clairvoyant.t:
n. 通灵者
adj. 有预知能力的

e.en: She visited a {clairvoyant} hoping to contact her late father.
e.zh: 她拜访了一位通灵者,希望能联系到已故的父亲。

e.en: His {clairvoyant} prediction about the election proved correct.
e.zh: 他对选举做出的神奇预言后来被证实是对的。

e.en: We dug for {clam} shells along the beach at low tide.
e.zh: 退潮时我们沿着海滩挖蛤蜊壳。

e.en: This restaurant serves the best {clam} chowder in town.
e.zh: 这家餐厅供应全城最好喝的蛤蜊浓汤。

clambake.t: n. 海滩蛤蜊烧烤聚会

e.en: We're hosting a {clambake} on the beach this Saturday.
e.zh: 这周六我们要在海滩上办一场蒸蛤蜊聚会。

e.en: The annual {clambake} draws hundreds of seafood lovers.
e.zh: 一年一度的蛤蜊烤会吸引了数百位海鲜爱好者。

e.en: The kids {clamber} over the rocks at the playground.
e.zh: 孩子们在游乐场的岩石上爬来爬去。

e.en: She had to {clamber} through the window to get inside.
e.zh: 她不得不从窗户爬进去。

clammy.t: adj. 又湿又冷的；黏糊糊的

e.en: His {clammy} hands gave away how nervous he was.
e.zh: 他湿冷的双手暴露了他有多紧张。

e.en: The basement felt cold and {clammy} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后地下室感觉又冷又潮湿。

clamor.t:
n. 喧嚷；强烈要求
v. 吵闹要求

e.en: There was a public {clamor} for stricter gun laws.
e.zh: 民众强烈要求制定更严格的枪支法律。

e.en: Fans {clamor} for tickets to the sold-out concert.
e.zh: 歌迷们争相索要这场售罄演唱会的门票。

clamoring.t: v. 吵闹要求（现在分词）

e.en: Customers are {clamoring} for a refund after the outage.
e.zh: 停电之后顾客们纷纷要求退款。

e.en: Reporters were {clamoring} outside the courthouse for a statement.
e.zh: 记者们在法院外大声要求发表声明。

clamorous.t: adj. 喧闹的；大声要求的

e.en: The {clamorous} crowd cheered as the team scored.
e.zh: 球队进球时,喧闹的人群欢呼起来。

e.en: There were {clamorous} demands for the CEO to resign.
e.zh: 人们高声要求那位首席执行官辞职。

clamour.t:
n. 喧嚷（英式拼写）
v. 吵闹要求

e.en: Voters {clamour} for greater transparency in government.
e.zh: 选民们强烈要求政府提高透明度。

e.en: The {clamour} of the city kept her awake all night.
e.zh: 城市的喧嚣让她整夜未眠。

clamp.t:
n. 夹钳；夹具
v. 夹紧

e.en: Use a {clamp} to hold the wood while the glue dries.
e.zh: 用夹钳固定木头,等胶水干透。

e.en: Officials plan to {clamp} down on illegal parking downtown.
e.zh: 官员计划严厉打击市中心的违章停车。

e.en: The government announced a {clampdown} on tax evasion.
e.zh: 政府宣布对逃税行为进行严厉打击。

e.en: There has been a {clampdown} on social media misinformation.
e.zh: 对社交媒体上的虚假信息已经开始严打了。

e.en: Police are {clamping} down on speeding in school zones.
e.zh: 警方正在严厉打击学校区域的超速行为。

e.en: He was {clamping} the metal pieces together for welding.
e.zh: 他正把金属件夹紧准备焊接。

e.en: We bought fresh {clams} for tonight's pasta dish.
e.zh: 我们买了新鲜的蛤蜊准备做今晚的意面。

e.en: The {clams} opened up after a few minutes in the broth.
e.zh: 蛤蜊在汤里煮几分钟后就张开了壳。

clamshell.t: n. 翻盖式（手机/设备）；蛤壳

e.en: The phone has a sleek {clamshell} design that folds in half.
e.zh: 这款手机采用时尚的翻盖设计,可对折合上。

e.en: Salads are sold in plastic {clamshell} containers at the deli.
e.zh: 熟食店里的沙拉装在塑料翻盖盒里出售。

e.en: The whole {clan} gathers for dinner every Christmas Eve.
e.zh: 每年平安夜全家族都会聚在一起吃晚饭。

e.en: In the game, players can join a {clan} to fight together.
e.zh: 在游戏里,玩家可以加入一个战队一起作战。

e.en: They held {clandestine} meetings to plan the merger.
e.zh: 他们秘密召开会议策划合并事宜。

e.en: The spy operated a {clandestine} radio from the attic.
e.zh: 那名间谍在阁楼上操作一台秘密无线电。

e.en: The journalist {clandestinely} recorded the corrupt official.
e.zh: 那位记者秘密录下了那名贪官的言行。

e.en: They met {clandestinely} to discuss leaving the company.
e.zh: 他们秘密会面,商讨离开公司的事。

clang.t:
n. 铿锵声
v. 发出叮当声

e.en: The {clang} of the metal gate echoed across the yard.
e.zh: 金属大门的当啷声回荡在院子里。

e.en: Church bells {clang} loudly every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 每周日早晨教堂的钟声都会响亮地敲响。

e.en: He dropped a real {clanger} when he forgot the boss's name.
e.zh: 他忘了老板的名字,真是闹了大笑话。

e.en: The reporter made a {clanger} by misquoting the senator.
e.zh: 那位记者错引参议员的话,犯了大错。

clanging.t: v. 发出叮当声（现在分词）

e.en: The {clanging} of construction work woke her at dawn.
e.zh: 施工的叮当声在黎明时分把她吵醒了。

e.en: Bells were {clanging} to announce the start of school.
e.zh: 钟声叮当作响,宣告上学时间到了。

e.en: The {clangor} of swords filled the battlefield.
e.zh: 刀剑相击的铿锵声响彻战场。

e.en: She covered her ears against the {clangor} of the factory.
e.zh: 她捂住耳朵,挡住工厂里的喧闹声。

clank.t:
n. 当啷声
v. 发出当啷声

e.en: The chains {clank} as the ship's anchor is lowered.
e.zh: 船锚下放时铁链发出当啷声。

e.en: I heard a loud {clank} from the engine compartment.
e.zh: 我听见发动机舱传来一声响亮的金属撞击声。

clanking.t: v. 当啷作响（现在分词）

e.en: The old radiator kept {clanking} all through the night.
e.zh: 那台旧暖气片整夜都在叮当作响。

e.en: You could hear the {clanking} of dishes from the kitchen.
e.zh: 从厨房传来碗盘碰撞的叮当声。

e.en: The neighborhood is friendly but a bit {clannish} to outsiders.
e.zh: 这个社区很友好,但对外人有点排外。

e.en: Office cliques can become {clannish} and exclude new hires.
e.zh: 办公室小团体会变得排外,把新员工排斥在外。

e.en: Highland {clans} once fought fiercely over territory.
e.zh: 高地的氏族曾为领土激烈争斗。

e.en: The top {clans} in the game compete in weekly tournaments.
e.zh: 游戏中顶级战队每周都会参加锦标赛。

e.en: Every {clansman} swore loyalty to the chief.
e.zh: 每位族人都向首领宣誓效忠。

e.en: He greeted his fellow {clansman} warmly at the gathering.
e.zh: 他在聚会上热情地问候同族的兄弟。

clap.t:
v. 鼓掌；拍手
n. 掌声

e.en: The audience began to {clap} as soon as she finished singing.
e.zh: 她一唱完,观众就开始鼓掌。

e.en: A loud {clap} of thunder startled the dog.
e.zh: 一声响亮的雷鸣把狗吓了一跳。

e.en: The cottage was painted white with {clapboard} siding.
e.zh: 那间小屋外墙铺着白色的护墙板。

e.en: The director snapped the {clapboard} before each take.
e.zh: 导演在每个镜头开拍前都会打一下场记板。

clapham.t: n. 克拉珀姆（伦敦地名）

e.en: She rents a small flat near {Clapham} Common in London.
e.zh: 她在伦敦克拉珀姆公地附近租了一间小公寓。

e.en: {Clapham} Junction is one of the busiest stations in Europe.
e.zh: 克拉珀姆枢纽站是欧洲最繁忙的车站之一。

e.en: The crowd {clapped} loudly when the band came on stage.
e.zh: 乐队登台时,观众报以热烈的掌声。

e.en: She {clapped} her hands to get the children's attention.
e.zh: 她拍了拍手,以引起孩子们的注意。

e.en: The bell's {clapper} broke off after years of use.
e.zh: 用了多年后,钟里的钟舌断掉了。

e.en: The film crew used a {clapper} board to mark each scene.
e.zh: 摄制组用场记板来标记每个场景。

clapping.t:
v. 鼓掌（现在分词）
n. 掌声

e.en: Everyone started {clapping} when the speech ended.
e.zh: 演讲结束时大家都开始鼓掌。

e.en: The {clapping} grew louder as the dancer took her bow.
e.zh: 舞者鞠躬谢幕时掌声越来越响亮。

claps.t:
n. 掌声
v. 鼓掌（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {claps} along to the beat of every song she hears.
e.zh: 她听到每首歌都会跟着节拍拍手。

e.en: Two {claps} of thunder echoed across the valley.
e.zh: 两声雷鸣在山谷里回荡。

e.en: Eric {Clapton} is regarded as one of the greatest guitarists ever.
e.zh: 埃里克·克莱普顿被誉为有史以来最伟大的吉他手之一。

e.en: She listens to {Clapton}'s blues albums while she works.
e.zh: 她工作时会听克莱普顿的蓝调专辑。

claptrap.t: n. 废话；哗众取宠的言论

e.en: His speech was full of {claptrap} and empty promises.
e.zh: 他的演讲充满了空话和虚假的承诺。

e.en: Don't believe that {claptrap} you read on social media.
e.zh: 别相信你在社交媒体上看到的那些废话。

claque.t: n. 捧场队；雇来喝彩的人

e.en: The politician hired a {claque} to cheer at every speech.
e.zh: 那位政客雇了一群捧场客在每次演讲时喝彩。

e.en: Critics dismissed the loud applause as a paid {claque}.
e.zh: 评论家将那阵热烈掌声视为花钱雇来的捧场队。

e.en: She studied economics at {Claremont} McKenna College.
e.zh: 她在克莱蒙特麦肯纳学院学习经济学。

e.en: The conference will be held in {Claremont}, California next spring.
e.zh: 会议将于明年春天在加州克莱蒙特举行。

clarendon.t: n. 克拉伦登（地名/人名）

e.en: The headline was set in bold {Clarendon} type.
e.zh: 标题采用了粗体克拉伦登字体。

e.en: They visited the historic {Clarendon} Hotel during their trip.
e.zh: 他们旅途中参观了历史悠久的克拉伦登酒店。

claret.t:
n. 波尔多红葡萄酒
adj. 酒红色的

e.en: He poured a glass of {claret} with dinner.
e.zh: 他在晚餐时倒了一杯波尔多红葡萄酒。

e.en: The rugby team wore {claret} and blue jerseys.
e.zh: 那支橄榄球队穿着深红与蓝色相间的球衣。

e.en: They booked afternoon tea at {Claridge}'s in London.
e.zh: 他们预订了伦敦克拉里奇酒店的下午茶。

e.en: Mr. {Claridge} will chair tomorrow's board meeting.
e.zh: 克拉里奇先生将主持明天的董事会会议。

e.en: Could you provide some {clarification} on the new policy?
e.zh: 你能就新政策做一些说明吗?

e.en: The lawyer asked the witness for further {clarification}.
e.zh: 律师要求证人作进一步澄清。

clarified.t:
v. 澄清（过去式）
adj. 已提纯的

e.en: The teacher {clarified} the instructions for the confused students.
e.zh: 老师为困惑的学生澄清了说明。

e.en: Many recipes call for {clarified} butter instead of regular butter.
e.zh: 许多食谱要求使用澄清黄油而不是普通黄油。

e.en: The water treatment plant uses a large {clarifier} to remove sediment.
e.zh: 水处理厂使用大型澄清池来去除沉淀物。

e.en: This skincare {clarifier} helps unclog pores overnight.
e.zh: 这款护肤净化液能在一夜间帮助疏通毛孔。

clarifies.t: v. 澄清；阐明（第三人称单数）

e.en: The new manual {clarifies} how to install the software.
e.zh: 新手册说明了如何安装这款软件。

e.en: A good diagram often {clarifies} complex relationships.
e.zh: 一张好的图表往往能厘清复杂的关系。

e.en: Let me {clarify} what I meant in the previous email.
e.zh: 让我澄清一下我在上封邮件中的意思。

e.en: Can you {clarify} which option you prefer?
e.zh: 你能说清楚你更喜欢哪个选项吗?

clarifying.t:
v. 正在澄清
adj. 起澄清作用的

e.en: She asked a {clarifying} question before answering.
e.zh: 她在回答之前先问了一个澄清性的问题。

e.en: This toner has a {clarifying} effect on oily skin.
e.zh: 这款爽肤水对油性皮肤有清洁净化的效果。

e.en: He plays the {clarinet} in the school orchestra.
e.zh: 他在学校管弦乐队里吹单簧管。

e.en: The {clarinet} solo opens the second movement beautifully.
e.zh: 单簧管独奏优美地开启了第二乐章。

e.en: The young {clarinetist} won first prize at the competition.
e.zh: 那位年轻的单簧管演奏家在比赛中获得了一等奖。

e.en: She trained for years to become a professional {clarinetist}.
e.zh: 她苦练多年才成为一名专业的单簧管演奏家。

e.en: The {clarinettist} performed a stunning jazz improvisation.
e.zh: 那位单簧管演奏家表演了一段精彩的爵士即兴演奏。

e.en: He's the principal {clarinettist} of the symphony.
e.zh: 他是这个交响乐团的首席单簧管演奏者。

clarion.t:
n. 号角声
adj. 响亮的

e.en: Her speech was a {clarion} call for climate action.
e.zh: 她的演讲是对气候行动的响亮号召。

e.en: The morning began with the {clarion} sound of trumpets.
e.zh: 清晨在号角般嘹亮的小号声中开始。

e.en: Diamonds are graded by their different {clarities} and cuts.
e.zh: 钻石按其不同的净度和切工分级。

e.en: The lake's varying {clarities} change with the seasons.
e.zh: 这片湖泊的清澈度随季节而变化。

e.en: The new screen offers amazing image {clarity}.
e.zh: 这款新屏幕提供了惊人的画面清晰度。

e.en: I appreciate the {clarity} of your explanation.
e.zh: 我很欣赏你解释得如此清晰。

e.en: {Clark} Kent is the alter ego of Superman.
e.zh: 克拉克·肯特是超人的另一身份。

e.en: Mr. {Clark} will lead the new product team.
e.zh: 克拉克先生将带领新的产品团队。

clarks.t: n. 其乐（英国鞋履品牌）

e.en: She bought a pair of {Clarks} desert boots online.
e.zh: 她在网上买了一双其乐沙漠靴。

e.en: The {Clarks} family invited us for dinner on Sunday.
e.zh: 克拉克一家邀请我们周日去吃晚餐。

e.en: He prefers a mild {claro} cigar after dinner.
e.zh: 他喜欢饭后抽一支温和的浅色雪茄。

e.en: The shop sells handmade {claro} cigars from Honduras.
e.zh: 这家店出售来自洪都拉斯的手工浅色雪茄。

clary.t: n. 南欧丹参；快乐鼠尾草

e.en: {Clary} sage oil is popular in aromatherapy.
e.zh: 南欧丹参精油在芳香疗法中很受欢迎。

e.en: She added fresh {clary} leaves to the herbal tea.
e.zh: 她在草本茶中加入了新鲜的南欧丹参叶。

clash.t:
n. 冲突；抵触
v. 冲突；不协调

e.en: Protesters and police {clash} in the city center.
e.zh: 抗议者与警察在市中心发生冲突。

e.en: That bright pink will {clash} with your red dress.
e.zh: 那种亮粉色会和你的红裙子很不搭。

e.en: The report documents violent {clashes} along the border.
e.zh: 该报告记录了边境上发生的暴力冲突。

e.en: Her style {clashes} completely with the office dress code.
e.zh: 她的穿搭与办公室着装要求完全不搭。

e.en: The room had {clashing} colors that hurt my eyes.
e.zh: 房间里的颜色相冲,看得我眼睛都疼。

e.en: Their {clashing} opinions made the meeting tense.
e.zh: 他们针锋相对的意见让会议气氛紧张。

clasp.t:
n. 搭扣；紧握
v. 扣紧；紧抱

e.en: The {clasp} on my necklace broke yesterday.
e.zh: 我项链上的搭扣昨天坏了。

e.en: She reached out to {clasp} his hand tightly.
e.zh: 她伸手紧紧握住了他的手。

e.en: The child {clasped} her mother's hand at the crossing.
e.zh: 孩子在路口紧紧握着妈妈的手。

e.en: He sat with his hands {clasped} in his lap.
e.zh: 他坐着,双手交握放在膝上。

e.en: Male sharks use a {clasper} during reproduction.
e.zh: 雄性鲨鱼在繁殖时使用鳍脚。

e.en: The mechanic replaced the broken {clasper} on the device.
e.zh: 机械师更换了设备上损坏的夹紧器。

e.en: I have a math {class} at nine tomorrow morning.
e.zh: 我明天早上九点有一节数学课。

e.en: This restaurant attracts a wealthy {class} of customers.
e.zh: 这家餐厅吸引着富裕阶层的顾客。

e.en: The movie was {classed} as a romantic comedy.
e.zh: 这部电影被归类为浪漫喜剧。

e.en: Penguins are {classed} as birds despite not flying.
e.zh: 企鹅虽然不会飞,但仍被归为鸟类。

e.en: Online {classes} have become popular since the pandemic.
e.zh: 自疫情以来,网上课程变得越来越流行。

e.en: The yoga studio offers {classes} for all levels.
e.zh: 这家瑜伽馆提供适合各级别学员的课程。

classic.t:
adj. 经典的
n. 经典作品

e.en: Pride and Prejudice is a {classic} English novel.
e.zh: 《傲慢与偏见》是一部经典的英国小说。

e.en: That's a {classic} mistake every beginner makes.
e.zh: 那是每个初学者都会犯的典型错误。

e.en: She listens to {classical} music while studying.
e.zh: 她学习时会听古典音乐。

e.en: The museum specializes in ancient {classical} sculpture.
e.zh: 这座博物馆专门收藏古典时期的雕塑。

e.en: She is {classically} trained as a ballet dancer.
e.zh: 她接受过古典芭蕾舞蹈训练。

e.en: The dish is {classically} served with rice and beans.
e.zh: 这道菜按传统通常配米饭和豆子。

e.en: His paintings show a strong influence of French {classicism}.
e.zh: 他的画作明显受到法国古典主义的影响。

e.en: The architect rejected modernism in favor of {classicism}.
e.zh: 那位建筑师摒弃现代主义,转而推崇古典主义。

classicist.t: n. 古典主义者；古典学者

e.en: The {classicist} translated several plays by Sophocles.
e.zh: 这位古典学者翻译了几部索福克勒斯的剧作。

e.en: As a {classicist}, she reads Latin and Greek fluently.
e.zh: 作为古典学者,她能流利地阅读拉丁文和希腊文。

classicizing.t:
adj. 古典化的
v. 使古典化

e.en: The architect adopted a {classicizing} style for the new museum.
e.zh: 建筑师为新博物馆采用了仿古典的风格。

e.en: His {classicizing} sculptures echo ancient Greek ideals.
e.zh: 他仿古典风格的雕塑回应了古希腊的理想。

e.en: She majored in {classics} at Oxford University.
e.zh: 她在牛津大学主修古典学。

e.en: This bookstore sells all the great literary {classics}.
e.zh: 这家书店出售所有伟大的文学经典。

e.en: His unique style is not easily {classifiable}.
e.zh: 他独特的风格很难被归类。

e.en: These documents are {classifiable} into three main categories.
e.zh: 这些文件可以归为三大类。

e.en: The library uses the Dewey Decimal {classification} system.
e.zh: 图书馆使用杜威十进制分类系统。

e.en: Scientists debate the {classification} of this newly discovered species.
e.zh: 科学家们正在讨论这个新发现物种的分类。

e.en: The new tax law introduces several income {classifications}.
e.zh: 新税法引入了几种收入分类。

e.en: Different countries use different hotel star {classifications}.
e.zh: 不同国家采用不同的酒店星级分类。

e.en: The biologist proposed a new {classificatory} scheme for insects.
e.zh: 那位生物学家提出了一种新的昆虫分类方案。

e.en: His paper raised {classificatory} questions about modern art.
e.zh: 他的论文提出了有关现代艺术分类的问题。

classified.t:
adj. 机密的；已分类的
n. 分类广告

e.en: The documents are {classified} as top secret.
e.zh: 这些文件被列为绝密。

e.en: I found the apartment through a {classified} ad online.
e.zh: 我是通过网上的分类广告找到这套公寓的。

e.en: She browses the {classifieds} every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 她每个周日早上都会浏览分类广告。

e.en: He sold his old car through the newspaper {classifieds}.
e.zh: 他通过报纸分类广告卖掉了旧车。

e.en: The machine learning {classifier} sorts emails into spam and inbox.
e.zh: 机器学习分类器会把邮件分到垃圾邮件和收件箱。

e.en: Chinese uses a {classifier} before nouns when counting.
e.zh: 汉语在计数时会在名词前使用量词。

classifies.t: v. 分类（classify 的三单形式）

e.en: The app {classifies} photos automatically by location.
e.zh: 这款应用会自动按位置对照片进行分类。

e.en: The library {classifies} books by subject and author.
e.zh: 图书馆按主题和作者对图书进行分类。

e.en: Scientists {classify} animals based on shared traits.
e.zh: 科学家根据共同特征对动物进行分类。

e.en: It's hard to {classify} this song into one genre.
e.zh: 很难把这首歌归入某一种风格。

classifying.t: v. 分类（classify 的现在分词）

e.en: The intern spent the morning {classifying} customer feedback.
e.zh: 实习生花了一上午时间对客户反馈进行分类。

e.en: {Classifying} dreams into neat categories isn't really possible.
e.zh: 将梦境整齐地归类其实是不太可能的。

e.en: The judges are still {classing} the wool by quality.
e.zh: 评委们仍在按质量对羊毛进行分级。

e.en: He objected to {classing} jazz as background music.
e.zh: 他反对把爵士乐归类为背景音乐。

e.en: The novel exposes the {classism} hidden in elite schools.
e.zh: 这部小说揭露了精英学校中隐藏的阶级歧视。

e.en: She wrote an essay about {classism} in the workplace.
e.zh: 她写了一篇关于职场阶级歧视的文章。

classless.t: adj. 无阶级的；不分等级的

e.en: They dreamed of building a truly {classless} society.
e.zh: 他们梦想建立一个真正没有阶级之分的社会。

e.en: His rude comment was completely {classless}.
e.zh: 他那粗鲁的评论完全没有教养。

e.en: The country prides itself on its supposed {classlessness} and equal opportunity.
e.zh: 这个国家以其所谓的无阶级性和机会平等而自豪。

e.en: Critics argue that true {classlessness} has never existed in any society.
e.zh: 批评者认为真正的无阶级社会从未在任何社会中存在过。

e.en: My old {classmate} from high school messaged me on LinkedIn.
e.zh: 我高中时的老同学在领英上给我发了消息。

e.en: She married a {classmate} she met during freshman year.
e.zh: 她嫁给了一位大一时认识的同学。

e.en: Her {classmates} threw a surprise party for her birthday.
e.zh: 她的同学们为她办了一个惊喜生日派对。

e.en: Most of my college {classmates} now work in tech.
e.zh: 我大学的同学大多数现在都在科技行业工作。

e.en: The new {classroom} has smart whiteboards and adjustable desks.
e.zh: 新教室配有智能白板和可调节的课桌。

e.en: Students returned to the {classroom} after the long summer break.
e.zh: 学生们在漫长的暑假后回到了教室。

e.en: The school renovated all its {classrooms} during the summer.
e.zh: 学校在暑假期间翻新了所有教室。

e.en: Many {classrooms} now use tablets instead of textbooks.
e.zh: 许多教室现在用平板电脑代替课本。

e.en: Please finish your {classwork} before you start chatting.
e.zh: 请先完成课堂作业再开始聊天。

e.en: The teacher reviews all {classwork} at the end of each day.
e.zh: 老师每天放学前都会检查所有课堂作业。

classy.t: adj. 有品味的；上档次的

e.en: She wore a {classy} black dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了一条优雅的黑色礼服出席晚会。

e.en: That restaurant has a really {classy} atmosphere for dates.
e.zh: 那家餐厅的氛围很有格调,适合约会。

e.en: Methane {clathrate} deposits sit beneath the ocean floor in vast quantities.
e.zh: 海底蕴藏着大量的甲烷水合物。

e.en: Scientists are studying how {clathrate} structures trap gas molecules.
e.zh: 科学家正在研究笼形化合物如何捕获气体分子。

clatter.t:
n. 哐当声
v. 发出哐当声

e.en: The dishes fell with a loud {clatter} on the floor.
e.zh: 盘子哗啦一声掉在地上。

e.en: I could hear keyboards {clatter} across the open office.
e.zh: 我能听到键盘声在开放式办公室里此起彼伏。

clattering.t: v. 发出哐当声（现在分词）

e.en: Pots were {clattering} in the kitchen as dinner was prepared.
e.zh: 准备晚餐时锅碗瓢盆在厨房里叮当作响。

e.en: The {clattering} train kept me awake all night.
e.zh: 哐当作响的火车让我整夜没睡。

e.en: The patient complained of leg {claudication} after walking short distances.
e.zh: 患者诉说走一小段路后就出现腿部跛行。

e.en: Intermittent {claudication} is often a sign of poor circulation.
e.zh: 间歇性跛行通常是血液循环不良的征兆。

claus.t: n. 人名 Claus（圣诞老人 Santa Claus）

e.en: Children leave cookies out for Santa {Claus} on Christmas Eve.
e.zh: 孩子们在平安夜会为圣诞老人留下饼干。

e.en: The mall hired an actor to play Santa {Claus} this year.
e.zh: 今年商场雇了一位演员来扮演圣诞老人。

e.en: Read the confidentiality {clause} carefully before signing the contract.
e.zh: 签合同前请仔细阅读保密条款。

e.en: The grammar lesson focused on identifying the main {clause}.
e.zh: 这节语法课重点讲如何识别主句。

e.en: The lawyer flagged several risky {clauses} in the agreement.
e.zh: 律师指出了协议中几条有风险的条款。

e.en: Complex sentences often contain multiple subordinate {clauses}.
e.zh: 复杂句通常包含多个从句。

e.en: His {claustrophobia} made the long elevator ride unbearable.
e.zh: 他的幽闭恐惧症让漫长的电梯之旅难以忍受。

e.en: She avoids MRI scans because of severe {claustrophobia}.
e.zh: 她因严重的幽闭恐惧症而避免做核磁共振检查。

e.en: Different {claustrophobias} can be triggered by elevators, tunnels, or crowded rooms.
e.zh: 不同的幽闭恐惧症可能由电梯、隧道或拥挤房间引发。

e.en: Therapists treat various {claustrophobias} through gradual exposure techniques.
e.zh: 治疗师通过渐进暴露疗法治疗各种幽闭恐惧症。

claustrophobic.t: adj. 有幽闭恐惧症的；令人窒息的

e.en: The tiny bathroom felt incredibly {claustrophobic} after a few minutes.
e.zh: 那个小卫生间几分钟后就让人感到极度压抑。

e.en: I get {claustrophobic} in crowded subway cars during rush hour.
e.zh: 高峰时段拥挤的地铁车厢会让我感到幽闭恐惧。

e.en: The salsa rhythm is built around the {clave} pattern.
e.zh: 萨尔萨节奏是围绕克拉维节拍型构建的。

e.en: He tapped out the {clave} on the edge of the table.
e.zh: 他在桌沿上敲打着克拉维节奏。

e.en: Bach composed many pieces intended for the {clavichord}.
e.zh: 巴赫创作了许多专为击弦古钢琴而写的曲子。

e.en: The museum displays a beautifully preserved 17th-century {clavichord}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一台保存完好的十七世纪击弦古钢琴。

e.en: He fractured his {clavicle} during the cycling accident.
e.zh: 他在那次骑车事故中摔断了锁骨。

e.en: The doctor showed me the X-ray of my {clavicle}.
e.zh: 医生给我看了我锁骨的X光片。

e.en: Bach's Well-Tempered {Clavier} remains essential repertoire for pianists.
e.zh: 巴赫的《平均律键盘曲集》至今仍是钢琴家的必备曲目。

e.en: She practiced scales on the {clavier} every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上都在键盘乐器上练习音阶。

claw.t:
n. 爪子
v. 抓；挠

e.en: The cat tried to {claw} the new sofa.
e.zh: 猫想要抓挠新沙发。

e.en: A crab's {claw} can deliver a surprisingly painful pinch.
e.zh: 螃蟹的钳子夹起人来出乎意料地疼。

clawback.t: n. 追回款项；回扣条款

e.en: The contract includes a {clawback} provision for executive bonuses.
e.zh: 合同中包含针对高管奖金的追回条款。

e.en: Regulators issued a {clawback} order after the accounting fraud.
e.zh: 监管机构在会计欺诈事件后下达了追回令。

clawed.t:
adj. 有爪的
v. 抓挠（过去式）

e.en: The startup {clawed} its way back to profitability after two years.
e.zh: 这家初创公司花了两年才艰难地重新实现盈利。

e.en: The kitten {clawed} at the dangling string playfully.
e.zh: 小猫顽皮地抓挠着垂下的绳子。

e.en: The bathroom features a vintage {clawfoot} bathtub from the 1920s.
e.zh: 浴室里有一个1920年代的复古爪足浴缸。

e.en: She fell in love with the antique {clawfoot} table at the auction.
e.zh: 她在拍卖会上爱上了那张古董爪足桌子。

e.en: The puppy kept {clawing} at the door to come inside.
e.zh: 小狗不停地抓门想要进来。

e.en: She is {clawing} her way to the top of the company.
e.zh: 她正一步步艰难地往公司高层爬。

e.en: The artist shaped the {clay} into a delicate vase.
e.zh: 艺术家把陶土塑造成一个精致的花瓶。

e.en: Children love playing with modeling {clay} in art class.
e.zh: 孩子们很喜欢在美术课上玩橡皮泥。

e.en: The {clayey} soil makes drainage difficult in this garden.
e.zh: 这片黏土质土壤使花园的排水变得困难。

e.en: After the rain, the path turned thick and {clayey}.
e.zh: 雨后小路变得厚重而黏腻。

claymore.t: n. 苏格兰阔刃大剑；克莱莫地雷

e.en: The Highland warrior wielded a massive two-handed {claymore}.
e.zh: 那位高地战士挥舞着一把巨大的双手阔剑。

e.en: A {claymore} mine was hidden along the jungle trail.
e.zh: 丛林小径旁藏有一枚阔剑地雷。

e.en: Lawyers must complete annual {CLE} hours to keep their license.
e.zh: 律师每年必须完成持续法律教育学时以保留执照。

e.en: The airport code {CLE} refers to Cleveland, Ohio.
e.zh: 机场代码CLE指的是俄亥俄州的克利夫兰。

clean.t:
adj. 干净的
v. 清洁；打扫

e.en: Please {clean} the kitchen before our guests arrive.
e.zh: 客人来之前请把厨房打扫干净。

e.en: The app has a {clean} interface that's easy to navigate.
e.zh: 这款应用界面简洁,操作方便。

cleaned.t: v. 清洁（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: I {cleaned} my entire apartment over the weekend.
e.zh: 我周末把整个公寓都打扫了一遍。

e.en: The mechanic {cleaned} the engine and replaced the filter.
e.zh: 机械师清洗了发动机并更换了滤芯。

cleaner.t:
n. 清洁剂；清洁工
adj. 更干净的

e.en: Electric cars are generally {cleaner} than gasoline ones.
e.zh: 电动车通常比汽油车更环保。

e.en: I dropped off my suit at the dry {cleaner} yesterday.
e.zh: 我昨天把西装送到干洗店去了。

e.en: Most household {cleaners} contain harsh chemicals you should avoid inhaling.
e.zh: 大多数家用清洁剂含有应避免吸入的刺激性化学物质。

e.en: The office hires professional {cleaners} every Friday evening.
e.zh: 办公室每周五晚上都会雇专业清洁工。

cleaning.t:
n. 清洁；打扫
v. 清理（clean 的现在分词）

e.en: Spring {cleaning} always takes longer than I expect.
e.zh: 春季大扫除总是比我想象的要久。

e.en: She is {cleaning} the windows before her parents visit.
e.zh: 她在父母来访前正在擦窗户。

e.en: Hospitals enforce strict {cleanliness} standards to prevent infection.
e.zh: 医院执行严格的清洁标准以防止感染。

e.en: His obsession with {cleanliness} extends to disinfecting groceries.
e.zh: 他对清洁的执着甚至延伸到给食品消毒。

cleanly.t:
adv. 干净地；利落地
adj. 爱干净的

e.en: The knife sliced through the tomato {cleanly}.
e.zh: 刀干净利落地切开了番茄。

e.en: The merger went through {cleanly} without any legal complications.
e.zh: 这次合并顺利完成,没有任何法律纠纷。

e.en: The hotel is known for the {cleanness} of its rooms.
e.zh: 这家酒店以房间的洁净度而闻名。

e.en: Inspectors check restaurants for overall {cleanness} and food safety.
e.zh: 检查员会检查餐厅的整体清洁度和食品安全。

e.en: The garage {cleanout} took us the entire weekend.
e.zh: 车库大清理花了我们整个周末。

e.en: The plumber installed a {cleanout} for easier drain access.
e.zh: 水管工安装了一个清扫口以便更方便地疏通下水道。

cleans.t: v. 清洁（clean 的第三人称单数）

e.en: He {cleans} his glasses several times a day.
e.zh: 他一天要擦好几次眼镜。

e.en: This product {cleans} stubborn stains in just one wash.
e.zh: 这款产品只需洗一次就能去除顽固污渍。

e.en: Use a gentle {cleanse} for sensitive skin every morning.
e.zh: 敏感肌每天早上要用温和的方式清洁。

e.en: Many people try a juice {cleanse} after the holidays.
e.zh: 许多人在假期后会尝试果汁排毒。

e.en: This facial {cleanser} is gentle enough for daily use.
e.zh: 这款洁面乳很温和,适合每天使用。

e.en: Always test a new {cleanser} on a small skin area first.
e.zh: 使用新洁面产品前请先在小块皮肤上测试。

cleansing.t:
n. 清洁；净化
adj. 有清洁作用的

e.en: A double {cleansing} routine removes both makeup and sunscreen effectively.
e.zh: 双重清洁能有效去除彩妆和防晒霜。

e.en: The retreat offered a weeklong {cleansing} program for body and mind.
e.zh: 这个静修营提供为期一周的身心净化课程。

e.en: The post-party {cleanup} took us until midnight.
e.zh: 派对后的清理一直忙到了半夜。

e.en: Volunteers organized a beach {cleanup} this Saturday morning.
e.zh: 志愿者们组织了本周六上午的海滩清理活动。

clear.t:
adj. 清晰的；明确的
v. 清除；清空

e.en: The instructions are not very {clear} to beginners.
e.zh: 这些说明对初学者来说不太清楚。

e.en: Please {clear} your desk before leaving the office.
e.zh: 离开办公室前请清理一下你的桌子。

e.en: The jacket was on {clearance} for seventy percent off.
e.zh: 那件夹克在清仓打三折。

e.en: He needed security {clearance} to enter the server room.
e.zh: 他需要安全许可才能进入服务器机房。

e.en: The evidence in this case is far from {clearcut}.
e.zh: 这个案子的证据远不能算明确。

e.en: Loggers {clearcut} the entire hillside last summer.
e.zh: 伐木工去年夏天把整个山坡都皆伐了。

cleared.t: v. 已清除；已批准（clear 的过去式）

e.en: The fog finally {cleared} by mid-morning.
e.zh: 雾终于在上午快十点时散去了。

e.en: Customs {cleared} the shipment after a brief inspection.
e.zh: 海关经过简短检查后放行了这批货物。

clearing.t:
n. 空地；结算
v. 清理

e.en: They built a small cabin in the forest {clearing}.
e.zh: 他们在森林空地上建了一座小木屋。

e.en: The bank is still {clearing} my deposit from yesterday.
e.zh: 银行还在处理我昨天的存款。

clearinghouse.t: n. 票据交换所；信息交流中心

e.en: The website serves as a {clearinghouse} for job opportunities in tech.
e.zh: 该网站是科技行业招聘信息的汇总平台。

e.en: Stock trades pass through a central {clearinghouse} for settlement.
e.zh: 股票交易通过中央清算所进行结算。

e.en: She {clearly} explained the new refund policy to customers.
e.zh: 她向顾客清楚地解释了新的退款政策。

e.en: The signal is {clearly} stronger near the window.
e.zh: 信号在窗户附近明显更强。

e.en: The {clearness} of the lake amazed every visitor.
e.zh: 湖水的清澈让每位游客都感到惊叹。

e.en: I appreciated the {clearness} of her instructions.
e.zh: 我很欣赏她说明的清晰明了。

e.en: The report compared the {clearnesses} of several mountain streams.
e.zh: 报告比较了几条山间溪流的清澈程度。

e.en: Different {clearnesses} of glass affect how much light passes through.
e.zh: 不同清澈度的玻璃会影响透光量。

clears.t: v. 清除（clear 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The fog usually {clears} by mid-morning here.
e.zh: 这里的雾通常在上午中段就会散去。

e.en: He {clears} his inbox every Friday afternoon.
e.zh: 他每周五下午都会清空收件箱。

e.en: Tie the rope securely to the dock {cleat}.
e.zh: 把绳子牢牢地系在码头的系绳柱上。

e.en: One {cleat} on his soccer shoe came loose.
e.zh: 他足球鞋上的一颗鞋钉松了。

e.en: The {cleavage} between the two parties has deepened recently.
e.zh: 两党之间的分歧最近进一步加深。

e.en: Geologists studied the {cleavage} pattern in the mineral sample.
e.zh: 地质学家研究了矿物样本中的解理纹路。

e.en: A sharp axe can {cleave} the log in one stroke.
e.zh: 一把锋利的斧头一下就能把木头劈开。

e.en: Many traditions still {cleave} to the old calendar.
e.zh: 许多传统依然坚守旧历法。

e.en: The chef chopped the bones with a heavy {cleaver}.
e.zh: 厨师用一把沉重的剁刀切开骨头。

e.en: Hang the {cleaver} on the magnetic strip after washing.
e.zh: 洗完后把剁刀挂在磁条上。

e.en: We hiked up {Clee} Hill to watch the sunset.
e.zh: 我们徒步登上克利山去看日落。

e.en: The village near {Clee} is famous for its quiet trails.
e.zh: 克利附近的村庄以宁静的小径而闻名。

cleethorpes.t: n. 克利索普斯（英国地名）

e.en: Families flock to {Cleethorpes} beach every summer weekend.
e.zh: 每个夏季周末,许多家庭涌向克里索普斯海滩。

e.en: The train to {Cleethorpes} leaves from platform three.
e.zh: 开往克里索普斯的火车从三号站台发车。

e.en: Beginners usually learn the treble {clef} first.
e.zh: 初学者通常先学习高音谱号。

e.en: The bass {clef} sits at the start of the lower staff.
e.zh: 低音谱号位于下方五线谱的开头。

cleft.t:
n. 裂缝
adj. 裂开的

e.en: A narrow {cleft} in the rock hid a tiny stream.
e.zh: 岩石中一道狭窄的裂缝藏着一条小溪。

e.en: The charity funds surgery for children born with a {cleft} lip.
e.zh: 该慈善机构资助唇裂儿童的手术费用。

e.en: The purple {clematis} climbed gracefully up the trellis.
e.zh: 紫色的铁线莲优雅地攀上了花架。

e.en: She planted a white {clematis} beside the front porch.
e.zh: 她在门廊旁种了一株白色铁线莲。

e.en: The governor granted {clemency} to several nonviolent offenders.
e.zh: 州长对几名非暴力罪犯予以宽大处理。

e.en: His lawyers filed an urgent appeal for {clemency}.
e.zh: 他的律师紧急提出了减刑申请。

clement.t: adj. 仁慈的；（气候）温和的

e.en: We enjoyed unusually {clement} weather throughout October.
e.zh: 整个十月我们都享受着异常温和的天气。

e.en: The judge was known for being {clement} with first offenders.
e.zh: 这位法官以对初犯者宽容而闻名。

clementine.t: n. 小柑橘；克莱门汀（女名）

e.en: I packed a {clementine} in my lunch every day.
e.zh: 我每天午餐都会带一个小柑橘。

e.en: The {clementine} peels easily and tastes wonderfully sweet.
e.zh: 这种小柑橘很好剥皮,味道格外香甜。

e.en: He tends to {clench} his jaw when he's stressed.
e.zh: 他紧张时往往会咬紧牙关。

e.en: Try not to {clench} your fists during the interview.
e.zh: 面试时尽量不要握紧拳头。

clenched.t:
adj. 紧握的
v. 紧握（过去式）

e.en: She {clenched} the steering wheel as traffic worsened.
e.zh: 路况越来越糟,她紧紧地握住了方向盘。

e.en: His {clenched} fists showed how angry he really was.
e.zh: 他紧握的拳头显示出他到底有多生气。

clenches.t: v. 紧握（clench 的第三人称单数）

e.en: He always {clenches} his teeth before lifting a heavy weight.
e.zh: 举起重物前他总是会咬紧牙关。

e.en: The dog {clenches} the toy and refuses to let go.
e.zh: 那只狗紧紧咬住玩具不肯放开。

clenching.t: v. 紧握（clench 的现在分词）

e.en: I caught myself {clenching} my phone during the scary scene.
e.zh: 恐怖的镜头里我发觉自己正紧握着手机。

e.en: {Clenching} your jaw at night can cause headaches.
e.zh: 夜里紧咬牙关可能会导致头痛。

cleopatra.t: n. 克利奥帕特拉（埃及艳后）

e.en: {Cleopatra} ruled Egypt with remarkable political skill.
e.zh: 克利奥帕特拉以非凡的政治手腕统治着埃及。

e.en: The new film about {Cleopatra} drew mixed reviews.
e.zh: 这部关于克利奥帕特拉的新片评价褒贬不一。

clerestory.t: n. 高侧窗；教堂顶部采光窗

e.en: Light streamed through the {clerestory} windows of the cathedral.
e.zh: 阳光从大教堂的高侧窗倾泻而下。

e.en: The architect added a {clerestory} to brighten the loft.
e.zh: 建筑师加装了一排高侧窗,让阁楼更明亮。

e.en: Local {clergy} joined the march for affordable housing.
e.zh: 当地神职人员加入了争取保障性住房的游行。

e.en: Members of the {clergy} visited the hospital every week.
e.zh: 神职人员每周都会去医院探访。

e.en: A retired {clergyman} officiated the small garden wedding.
e.zh: 一位退休的牧师主持了这场小型的花园婚礼。

e.en: The village {clergyman} knew almost every family by name.
e.zh: 村里的牧师几乎能叫出每一户人家的名字。

e.en: A young {cleric} led the morning prayers at the mosque.
e.zh: 一位年轻的神职人员主持了清真寺的晨祷。

e.en: The {cleric} spoke calmly about forgiveness and community.
e.zh: 那位神职人员平静地谈论着宽恕与社区。

clerical.t:
adj. 文书的；办公室的
adj. 神职的

e.en: She handled the {clerical} work for the small law firm.
e.zh: 她负责这家小型律师事务所的文书工作。

e.en: A {clerical} error delayed the shipment by two weeks.
e.zh: 一个文书错误使发货延误了两周。

e.en: Reformers criticized the church's deep-rooted {clericalism}.
e.zh: 改革派批评教会根深蒂固的教权主义。

e.en: His book traces the decline of {clericalism} in modern Europe.
e.zh: 他的书追溯了教权主义在现代欧洲的衰落。

e.en: The hotel {clerk} handed me the room key with a smile.
e.zh: 酒店职员微笑着把房卡递给我。

e.en: She works as a court {clerk} in downtown Boston.
e.zh: 她在波士顿市中心的法院担任书记员。

clerkly.t: adj. 书记员的；文书式的

e.en: He kept neat, {clerkly} notes of every meeting.
e.zh: 他对每次会议都做了整洁、像书记员般的记录。

e.en: Her {clerkly} habits made the audit much easier.
e.zh: 她一丝不苟的文员习惯让审计轻松了许多。

e.en: Three {clerks} were busy stocking shelves before opening.
e.zh: 开门前有三名店员正忙着上架补货。

e.en: Court {clerks} processed hundreds of filings that morning.
e.zh: 那天上午法院书记员处理了数百份文件。

clerkship.t: n. 书记员职位；助理实习期

e.en: She landed a prestigious {clerkship} with a federal judge.
e.zh: 她获得了一份在联邦法官身边实习的高声望职位。

e.en: His {clerkship} taught him how courts really operate.
e.zh: 那段书记员经历让他了解了法院的真实运作。

e.en: We spent the weekend exploring {Clermont}-Ferrand's old town.
e.zh: 我们周末游览了克莱蒙费朗的老城区。

e.en: The conference will be held in {Clermont} next March.
e.zh: 会议将于明年三月在克莱蒙举行。

cleveland.t: n. 克利夫兰（美国城市）

e.en: The flight to {Cleveland} takes about two hours.
e.zh: 飞往克利夫兰的航班大约需要两个小时。

e.en: My cousin moved to {Cleveland} for a hospital job.
e.zh: 我表哥为了一份医院的工作搬到了克利夫兰。

e.en: That was a {clever} way to solve the puzzle.
e.zh: 这是一种解开这道谜题的巧妙方法。

e.en: She's a {clever} student who asks great questions.
e.zh: 她是个聪明的学生,提问总是切中要害。

e.en: He {cleverly} hid the spare key under a loose tile.
e.zh: 他巧妙地把备用钥匙藏在一块松动的瓷砖下。

e.en: The app {cleverly} reminds you to drink water hourly.
e.zh: 这款应用会巧妙地每小时提醒你喝水。

e.en: Her {cleverness} saved the team during the demo crash.
e.zh: 她的机智在演示崩溃时救了整个团队。

e.en: There's a quiet {cleverness} in how the show is written.
e.zh: 这部剧的剧本中藏着一种低调的聪慧。

e.en: The novel is full of small {clevernesses} that reward rereading.
e.zh: 这本小说充满值得反复回味的种种小巧思。

e.en: Critics admired the playwright's many {clevernesses} of dialogue.
e.zh: 评论家欣赏剧作家在对白上的诸多巧思。

e.en: The trailer attaches to the tractor with a heavy {clevis}.
e.zh: 拖车通过一个厚重的U形夹连接到拖拉机上。

e.en: Replace the worn {clevis} pin before towing anything.
e.zh: 拖运任何东西之前先更换磨损的U形夹销。

cli.t: n. 命令行界面（command-line interface 缩写）

e.en: Most developers prefer the {CLI} over the web dashboard.
e.zh: 大多数开发者更喜欢用命令行而不是网页控制台。

e.en: Run the deployment using the project's {CLI} tool.
e.zh: 使用项目的命令行工具来执行部署。

e.en: Avoid the {cliche} about chasing your dreams in your essay.
e.zh: 作文里要避免那种追逐梦想的老套说法。

e.en: That movie ending felt like a tired old {cliche}.
e.zh: 那部电影的结局给人一种老掉牙的陈词滥调感。

cliched.t: adj. 老套的；陈词滥调的

e.en: The dialogue felt {cliched} and totally predictable.
e.zh: 对白显得陈词滥调,毫无悬念。

e.en: She rewrote the {cliched} opening line of her novel.
e.zh: 她重写了小说中那句俗套的开篇语。

click.t:
v. 点击（鼠标、链接）
n. 咔哒声

e.en: Just {click} the blue button to confirm your order.
e.zh: 只需点击蓝色按钮即可确认订单。

e.en: I heard a soft {click} as the door locked.
e.zh: 门锁上时我听到一声轻微的咔哒声。

e.en: I {clicked} the link, but the page never loaded.
e.zh: 我点了链接,但页面始终没有加载出来。

e.en: We {clicked} immediately and talked for hours.
e.zh: 我们一见如故,聊了好几个小时。

e.en: Use a {clicker} to count people entering the venue.
e.zh: 用计数器来统计进入场地的人数。

e.en: Trainers reward the dog right after each {clicker} sound.
e.zh: 训犬师在每次响片声后立即奖励小狗。

clicking.t:
v. 正在点击
n. 咔哒声

e.en: Stop {clicking} that pen — it's driving me crazy.
e.zh: 别再按那支笔了——快把我逼疯了。

e.en: {Clicking} the icon will open the settings menu.
e.zh: 点击该图标即可打开设置菜单。

e.en: The ad got thousands of {clicks} on its first day.
e.zh: 这则广告上线第一天就获得了数千次点击。

e.en: Checkout takes only three {clicks} on our new site.
e.zh: 在我们的新网站上,结账只需三次点击。

e.en: They toasted the engagement with a chilled bottle of {Clicquot}.
e.zh: 他们用一瓶冰镇的凯歌香槟为订婚干杯。

e.en: A glass of {Clicquot} arrived with the dessert course.
e.zh: 甜点上桌时,一杯凯歌香槟也随之送上。

client.t:
n. 客户；委托人
n. 客户端（软件）

e.en: Our biggest {client} renewed the contract for another year.
e.zh: 我们最大的客户又续签了一年合同。

e.en: The email {client} keeps crashing on my old laptop.
e.zh: 这个邮件客户端在我那台旧笔记本上老是崩溃。

e.en: The boutique has a loyal {clientele} of fashion editors.
e.zh: 这家精品店拥有一批忠实的时尚编辑客户群。

e.en: He built his {clientele} mostly through word of mouth.
e.zh: 他的客户群主要是靠口碑积累起来的。

clientelistic.t: adj. 庇护主义的；依附关系的

e.en: Critics call the mayor's hiring practices openly {clientelistic}.
e.zh: 批评者称市长的用人方式公然带有恩庇主义色彩。

e.en: Reformers want to dismantle the party's {clientelistic} networks.
e.zh: 改革者希望瓦解该党的恩庇主义关系网。

e.en: Our law firm has hundreds of {clients} across Asia.
e.zh: 我们律所在亚洲有数百名客户。

e.en: Email {clients} like Outlook still dominate office workflows.
e.zh: 像 Outlook 这样的邮件客户端仍主导着办公流程。

e.en: She stood near the edge of the {cliff} taking photos.
e.zh: 她站在悬崖边上拍照。

e.en: The economy is heading toward a fiscal {cliff}.
e.zh: 经济正走向财政悬崖。

e.en: We hiked through the village of {Cliffe} in Kent.
e.zh: 我们徒步穿过了肯特郡的克利夫村。

e.en: Professor {Cliffe} published a paper on coastal erosion.
e.zh: 克利夫教授发表了一篇关于海岸侵蚀的论文。

cliffhanger.t: n. 悬念结尾；扣人心弦的情节

e.en: The season finale ended on a brutal {cliffhanger}.
e.zh: 本季大结局以一个残酷的悬念收尾。

e.en: Game seven was a real {cliffhanger} until the final second.
e.zh: 第七场比赛直到最后一秒都扣人心弦。

e.en: They booked a {cliffside} villa overlooking the ocean.
e.zh: 他们订了一栋俯瞰海洋的悬崖别墅。

e.en: A narrow path winds along the {cliffside} to the beach.
e.zh: 一条窄路沿着崖壁蜿蜒通往海滩。

e.en: We had dinner at a {clifftop} restaurant in Santorini.
e.zh: 我们在圣托里尼一家崖顶餐厅吃了晚餐。

e.en: The lighthouse sits on a windy {clifftop}.
e.zh: 灯塔矗立在多风的崖顶。

e.en: Montgomery {Clift} starred in several classic Hollywood films.
e.zh: 蒙哥马利·克利夫特出演了多部好莱坞经典影片。

e.en: The old {clift} above the river has eroded badly.
e.zh: 河上方那块老悬崖侵蚀得很厉害。

clifton.t: n. 克利夫顿（地名/人名）

e.en: The {Clifton} Suspension Bridge is a landmark of Bristol.
e.zh: 克利夫顿吊桥是布里斯托的地标。

e.en: My friend lives in a quiet neighborhood called {Clifton}.
e.zh: 我朋友住在一个叫克利夫顿的安静社区。

e.en: The old manuscript spelled the word as {clifves}.
e.zh: 那份古籍把这个词拼作 clifves。

e.en: Scholars debate whether {clifves} was an early plural of cliff.
e.zh: 学者们争论 clifves 是否是 cliff 的早期复数形式。

e.en: The {climactic} battle scene took six months to film.
e.zh: 那场高潮战斗戏拍了六个月。

e.en: Her speech reached a {climactic} moment near the end.
e.zh: 她的演讲在接近尾声时达到高潮。

climate.t:
n. 气候
n. 氛围；环境（政治气候）

e.en: Scientists warn that {climate} change is accelerating.
e.zh: 科学家警告说气候变化正在加速。

e.en: The startup struggled in a tough economic {climate}.
e.zh: 这家创业公司在严峻的经济环境中举步维艰。

e.en: Different crops thrive in different {climates}.
e.zh: 不同的作物在不同的气候下茁壮生长。

e.en: Political {climates} can shift overnight after an election.
e.zh: 政治气候在选举后可能一夜之间转变。

e.en: The region experiences extreme {climatic} conditions in winter.
e.zh: 该地区冬季气候条件极端。

e.en: Researchers study {climatic} patterns over thousands of years.
e.zh: 研究人员研究数千年来的气候规律。

e.en: The two regions are {climatically} very different.
e.zh: 这两个地区在气候上差异很大。

e.en: This crop is {climatically} suited to tropical zones.
e.zh: 这种作物在气候上适合热带地区。

e.en: The report uses {climatological} data from the past century.
e.zh: 该报告使用了过去一个世纪的气候学数据。

e.en: They built a {climatological} model of the Arctic.
e.zh: 他们建立了一个北极地区的气候学模型。

e.en: The {climatologist} predicted hotter summers ahead.
e.zh: 这位气候学家预测未来夏天会更热。

e.en: She trained as a {climatologist} at MIT.
e.zh: 她在麻省理工学院接受了气候学家的培训。

e.en: He earned a PhD in {climatology} last year.
e.zh: 他去年取得了气候学博士学位。

e.en: {Climatology} combines physics, chemistry, and earth science.
e.zh: 气候学融合了物理、化学和地球科学。

climax.t:
n. 高潮；顶点
v. 达到高潮

e.en: The film's {climax} left the entire audience speechless.
e.zh: 影片的高潮让全场观众无言以对。

e.en: The negotiations reached their {climax} at midnight.
e.zh: 谈判在午夜达到了高潮。

e.en: The novel {climaxes} with a courtroom showdown.
e.zh: 这部小说以一场法庭对决达到高潮。

e.en: Her career has had several memorable {climaxes}.
e.zh: 她的职业生涯有过几次难忘的高光时刻。

climb.t:
v. 攀爬；上升
n. 攀登

e.en: We plan to {climb} Mount Fuji this summer.
e.zh: 我们打算今年夏天去爬富士山。

e.en: Stock prices continued to {climb} after the earnings report.
e.zh: 财报公布后股价继续攀升。

e.en: The minister's apology was an embarrassing {climbdown}.
e.zh: 那位部长的道歉是一次尴尬的让步。

e.en: The company's {climbdown} on layoffs surprised investors.
e.zh: 公司在裁员问题上的退让让投资者意外。

climbed.t: v. climb 的过去式，攀登、上升

e.en: She {climbed} the corporate ladder in just five years.
e.zh: 她仅用五年就在公司里步步高升。

e.en: Temperatures {climbed} above forty degrees yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天气温攀升到了四十度以上。

climber.t:
n. 攀登者；登山者
n. 攀缘植物

e.en: The {climber} reached the summit just before sunset.
e.zh: 那位登山者在日落前抵达了顶峰。

e.en: Ivy is a fast-growing {climber} that covers walls.
e.zh: 常春藤是一种生长迅速、爬满墙面的攀缘植物。

climbers.t: n. 攀登者（复数）；登山者们

e.en: Several {climbers} were rescued from the icy ridge.
e.zh: 几名登山者从冰冷的山脊上获救。

e.en: Social {climbers} flock to these high-society parties.
e.zh: 攀附权贵者纷纷涌向这些上流社会派对。

climbing.t:
n. 攀登；登山运动
v. 正在攀登

e.en: Rock {climbing} has become hugely popular among teenagers.
e.zh: 攀岩在青少年中变得非常流行。

e.en: Inflation is {climbing} faster than wages.
e.zh: 通胀上升的速度超过了工资增长。

e.en: His many {climbings} of Everest made him a legend.
e.zh: 他多次登顶珠穆朗玛峰使他成为传奇。

e.en: The journal records all her {climbings} in the Alps.
e.zh: 日志记录了她在阿尔卑斯山的所有登山经历。

climbs.t:
v. 攀登；上升
n. 登山路线

e.en: He {climbs} every weekend at the local gym.
e.zh: 他每个周末都去本地的攀岩馆攀岩。

e.en: The trail includes several steep {climbs}.
e.zh: 这条小径包含几段陡峭的爬坡。

clime.t: n. 地带；气候（文学用法）

e.en: Retirees often move to a warmer {clime} for winter.
e.zh: 退休人员常在冬天搬到更温暖的地方。

e.en: Birds migrate to a sunnier {clime} every autumn.
e.zh: 鸟儿每年秋天迁徙到阳光更充足的地方。

clinch.t:
v. 确定；搞定（交易）
n. 拥抱；扭抱

e.en: A last-minute goal helped them {clinch} the championship.
e.zh: 最后一刻的进球帮他们锁定了冠军。

e.en: Her presentation should {clinch} the deal with investors.
e.zh: 她的演示应该能敲定与投资者的交易。

clinched.t: v. 已确定；已搞定（交易、胜利）

e.en: The team {clinched} a playoff spot with last night's win.
e.zh: 球队凭昨晚的胜利锁定了季后赛席位。

e.en: He {clinched} the contract after months of negotiation.
e.zh: 经过数月谈判,他终于敲定了合同。

clincher.t: n. 决定性论据；一锤定音的事

e.en: The free shipping was the {clincher} for me.
e.zh: 免运费是让我下单的关键因素。

e.en: His final argument turned out to be the {clincher}.
e.zh: 他最后的论点成了决定性的一招。

clinches.t: v. 确定；搞定（第三人称单数）

e.en: A strong demo often {clinches} a sale.
e.zh: 一次出色的演示往往能促成销售。

e.en: She always {clinches} negotiations at the last minute.
e.zh: 她总是在最后一刻搞定谈判。

clinching.t:
adj. 决定性的
v. 正在敲定

e.en: He scored the {clinching} goal in extra time.
e.zh: 他在加时赛中打入了制胜进球。

e.en: The CEO is focused on {clinching} the merger this week.
e.zh: CEO 这周专注于敲定这桩并购。

e.en: The dentist prescribed {clindamycin} for the tooth infection.
e.zh: 牙医开了克林霉素来治疗牙齿感染。

e.en: {Clindamycin} is sometimes used to treat severe acne.
e.zh: 克林霉素有时用于治疗严重的痤疮。

cline.t: n. 渐变群（生物学术语）

e.en: Biologists observed a clear {cline} in beak size across islands.
e.zh: 生物学家观察到各岛屿间喙的大小呈明显的渐变。

e.en: Dialects often vary along a geographic {cline}.
e.zh: 方言往往沿地理梯度逐渐变化。

cling.t: v. 紧贴；依附；抓紧不放

e.en: Wet leaves {cling} to the windshield after a storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨过后,湿叶子粘在挡风玻璃上。

e.en: Some people {cling} to outdated beliefs.
e.zh: 有些人执着于过时的观念。

e.en: Wrap the leftovers in {clingfilm} before refrigerating.
e.zh: 把剩饭用保鲜膜包好再放进冰箱。

e.en: She covered the bowl tightly with {clingfilm}.
e.zh: 她用保鲜膜把碗盖得严严实实。

clinging.t:
adj. 紧贴的；粘人的
v. 正紧贴着

e.en: The toddler was {clinging} to her mother's leg.
e.zh: 那个幼儿紧紧抱着妈妈的腿。

e.en: He's still {clinging} to hopes of a promotion.
e.zh: 他仍然抱着升职的希望不放。

clings.t: v. 紧贴；依附（第三人称单数）

e.en: The smell of smoke {clings} to your clothes for days.
e.zh: 烟味会在衣服上残留好几天。

e.en: She {clings} to the memory of her childhood home.
e.zh: 她紧紧守着对童年故居的记忆。

clingy.t: adj. 粘人的；依赖性强的

e.en: My new puppy is incredibly {clingy} after dinner.
e.zh: 我家小狗晚饭后特别黏人。

e.en: This shirt gets {clingy} when the weather is humid.
e.zh: 这件衬衫在潮湿天气里会变得贴身。

e.en: The {clinic} opens at eight every weekday morning.
e.zh: 诊所每个工作日早上八点开门。

e.en: She runs a free dental {clinic} for low-income families.
e.zh: 她为低收入家庭开办了一家免费牙科诊所。

clinical.t:
adj. 临床的
adj. 冷静客观的

e.en: The drug is now in {clinical} trials in three countries.
e.zh: 该药物正在三个国家进行临床试验。

e.en: His tone was cold and oddly {clinical}.
e.zh: 他的语气冷漠,带着一种奇怪的冷峻。

e.en: She was {clinically} diagnosed with depression last year.
e.zh: 她去年被临床诊断为抑郁症。

e.en: He described the accident {clinically}, without emotion.
e.zh: 他冷静客观地描述了那场事故,毫无情绪。

e.en: The {clinician} reviewed the patient's chart carefully.
e.zh: 那位临床医生仔细审阅了病人的病历。

e.en: She works as both a researcher and a {clinician}.
e.zh: 她既是研究人员,也是一名临床医生。

e.en: Free vaccination {clinics} opened across the city last week.
e.zh: 上周全市开设了多家免费疫苗接种诊所。

e.en: The hospital runs specialty {clinics} every Thursday.
e.zh: 这家医院每周四开设专科门诊。

e.en: She swears by {Clinique} moisturizer for sensitive skin.
e.zh: 她坚信倩碧的保湿霜对敏感肌特别有效。

e.en: {Clinique} launched a new lipstick line this fall.
e.zh: 倩碧今秋推出了一条新的口红系列。

clink.t:
v. 叮当作响（杯子碰撞声）
n. 叮当声

e.en: I heard the {clink} of glasses from the next table.
e.zh: 我听到隔壁桌传来酒杯碰撞的清脆声响。

e.en: They paused to {clink} their mugs in celebration.
e.zh: 他们停下来碰了碰杯子以示庆祝。

clinker.t: n. 熔渣；煤渣；水泥熟料

e.en: Cement is made by grinding {clinker} into fine powder.
e.zh: 水泥是通过将熟料磨成细粉制成的。

e.en: His latest movie was a total {clinker} at the box office.
e.zh: 他最新的电影在票房上彻底失败了。

e.en: Glasses kept {clinking} throughout the wedding toast.
e.zh: 婚礼祝酒时杯子一直叮当作响。

e.en: The {clinking} of coins filled the busy market.
e.zh: 硬币的叮当声充满了热闹的集市。

e.en: Hillary {Clinton} served as Secretary of State under Obama.
e.zh: 希拉里·克林顿曾在奥巴马任内担任国务卿。

e.en: We drove through {Clinton}, Iowa, on our road trip.
e.zh: 我们公路旅行时开车穿过了爱荷华州的克林顿市。

clintonian.t: adj. 克林顿式的；克林顿时代的

e.en: His speech had a {Clintonian} polish that charmed the donors.
e.zh: 他的演讲带着克林顿式的圆滑，让捐赠者们很受用。

e.en: Critics mocked her {Clintonian} habit of dodging direct questions.
e.zh: 批评者嘲讽她有种克林顿式的回避直接问题的习惯。

clio.t: n. 克利俄（希腊神话历史女神）

e.en: The agency won a {Clio} for its bold sneaker campaign.
e.zh: 该广告公司凭借大胆的运动鞋广告赢得了克里奥奖。

e.en: In Greek myth, {Clio} is the muse of history.
e.zh: 在希腊神话中，克利俄是历史的缪斯女神。

clip.t:
n. 短视频；剪辑；夹子
v. 剪；夹住

e.en: She watched a funny {clip} on TikTok during lunch.
e.zh: 她午饭时看了一段抖音上的搞笑视频。

e.en: Use a paper {clip} to keep the receipts together.
e.zh: 用回形针把这些收据夹在一起。

clipboard.t:
n. 剪贴板（电脑）
n. 写字夹板

e.en: Press Ctrl+C to copy the text to your {clipboard}.
e.zh: 按 Ctrl+C 把文字复制到剪贴板。

e.en: The nurse jotted notes on her {clipboard} during rounds.
e.zh: 查房时护士在写字夹板上做着记录。

clipped.t:
v. 剪下；夹住（过去式）
adj. 简短的

e.en: He spoke in a {clipped} British accent that sounded formal.
e.zh: 他说话带着干脆利落的英国口音，听起来很正式。

e.en: She {clipped} the article and saved it for later.
e.zh: 她把那篇文章剪下来留着以后看。

clipper.t:
n. 修剪器；推子
n. 快速帆船

e.en: The barber pulled out his {clipper} and started buzzing my hair.
e.zh: 理发师拿出推剪开始给我剃头发。

e.en: A tea {clipper} once raced from China to London in record time.
e.zh: 曾有一艘运茶快帆船以创纪录的速度从中国驶往伦敦。

clipping.t:
n. 剪报；剪辑片段
v. 正在剪

e.en: Grandma kept a newspaper {clipping} about my graduation.
e.zh: 奶奶留着一份关于我毕业的剪报。

e.en: The audio kept {clipping} because the mic gain was too high.
e.zh: 麦克风增益太高，导致音频一直爆音。

clips.t:
n. 短视频；夹子（复数）
v. 剪；夹

e.en: YouTube {clips} of the concert went viral overnight.
e.zh: 演唱会的YouTube片段一夜之间火遍全网。

e.en: She {clips} her bangs back with a tiny pearl barrette.
e.zh: 她用一个小珍珠发夹把刘海别到后面。

e.en: The popular {clique} sat at the same lunch table every day.
e.zh: 那群受欢迎的小团体每天都坐在同一张午餐桌。

e.en: It's hard to break into the engineering {clique} at this company.
e.zh: 想融入这家公司的工程师小圈子可不容易。

e.en: The article explained why the {clit} matters in sex education.
e.zh: 这篇文章解释了为什么阴蒂在性教育中很重要。

e.en: Many anatomy textbooks barely mention the {clit} at all.
e.zh: 许多解剖学教科书几乎根本不提阴蒂。

e.en: The study examined {clitoral} anatomy in surprising detail.
e.zh: 该研究以惊人的细节考察了阴蒂的解剖结构。

e.en: Doctors increasingly recognize {clitoral} health as part of women's wellness.
e.zh: 医生越来越将阴蒂健康视为女性健康的一部分。

e.en: Activists campaigned to end {clitoridectomy} in vulnerable communities.
e.zh: 活动人士致力于在弱势社区终结阴蒂切除手术。

e.en: The WHO classifies {clitoridectomy} as a form of female genital mutilation.
e.zh: 世卫组织将阴蒂切除归类为女性生殖器残割的一种。

e.en: The textbook finally included a full diagram of the {clitoris}.
e.zh: 这本教科书终于收录了阴蒂的完整图示。

e.en: Researchers say the {clitoris} is far larger than people assume.
e.zh: 研究者表示阴蒂远比人们想象的要大得多。

cliveden.t: n. 克莱夫登（英国庄园地名）

e.en: The Profumo affair famously began at {Cliveden} in 1961.
e.zh: 著名的普罗富莫事件于1961年始于克莱夫登庄园。

e.en: We toured {Cliveden} and admired its magnificent gardens.
e.zh: 我们参观了克莱夫登庄园，欣赏了那壮观的花园。

e.en: {Cllr} Thompson voted against the new housing development.
e.zh: 汤普森议员投票反对这个新住宅开发项目。

e.en: Local residents emailed their {Cllr} about the parking problem.
e.zh: 当地居民就停车问题给他们的市议员发了邮件。

clo.t: n. 克罗（服装保暖值单位）

e.en: Engineers measured insulation in {clo} units when designing the spacesuit.
e.zh: 工程师在设计宇航服时用克罗值来衡量保温性。

e.en: A heavy winter coat provides about three {clo} of insulation.
e.zh: 一件厚冬装提供大约三克罗的保暖值。

e.en: Birds excrete waste through a single opening called the {cloaca}.
e.zh: 鸟类通过一个叫做泄殖腔的单一开口排出废物。

e.en: In ancient Rome, the Cloaca Maxima drained the city's filthy {cloaca}.
e.zh: 古罗马的大下水道排走了城市污秽的下水。

cloak.t:
n. 斗篷；披风
v. 掩盖；遮蔽

e.en: She wrapped a velvet {cloak} around her shoulders before leaving.
e.zh: 她出门前把一件天鹅绒斗篷裹在肩上。

e.en: The deal was struck under a {cloak} of secrecy.
e.zh: 这笔交易是在重重保密的掩盖下达成的。

e.en: The mountain was {cloaked} in thick morning fog.
e.zh: 山峰笼罩在浓厚的晨雾之中。

e.en: Their plans were {cloaked} in vague corporate language.
e.zh: 他们的计划被含糊的企业辞令所掩饰。

cloaking.t:
n. 隐形；伪装
v. 遮盖

e.en: The starship activated its {cloaking} device and vanished.
e.zh: 那艘星舰启动了隐形装置，瞬间消失了。

e.en: Search engines penalize websites that use {cloaking} to trick crawlers.
e.zh: 搜索引擎会处罚那些用障眼法欺骗爬虫的网站。

e.en: Please leave your coat in the {cloakroom} before entering the gallery.
e.zh: 进画廊之前请把外套寄存在衣帽间。

e.en: They whispered political deals in the parliament's {cloakroom}.
e.zh: 他们在议会衣帽间里低声谈着政治交易。

cloaks.t:
n. 斗篷（复数）
v. 掩盖

e.en: The actors wore black {cloaks} for the witch scene.
e.zh: 演员们在女巫那一幕里穿着黑色斗篷。

e.en: Heavy fog {cloaks} the harbor every winter morning.
e.zh: 每个冬日清晨浓雾都笼罩着港口。

e.en: Rising fuel costs will {clobber} small airlines this quarter.
e.zh: 燃油成本飙升将在本季度重创小型航空公司。

e.en: Be careful—saving will {clobber} your unsaved changes.
e.zh: 小心，保存会覆盖掉你未保存的修改。

cloche.t: n. 钟形女帽；园艺钟形罩

e.en: She wore a 1920s {cloche} hat to the themed party.
e.zh: 她戴着一顶二十年代的钟形帽参加主题派对。

e.en: Cover the seedlings with a glass {cloche} until spring.
e.zh: 用玻璃罩盖住幼苗直到春天来临。

clock.t:
n. 时钟
v. 计时

e.en: The {clock} on the wall was twenty minutes fast.
e.zh: 墙上的钟快了二十分钟。

e.en: Top sprinters can {clock} under ten seconds in the hundred meters.
e.zh: 顶级短跑选手百米能跑进十秒。

clocking.t:
n. 计时
v. 打卡；测速

e.en: He's {clocking} sixty hours a week at the new startup.
e.zh: 他在那家新创业公司每周工作六十个小时。

e.en: The radar gun was {clocking} cars at over ninety mph.
e.zh: 测速枪测到车速超过每小时九十英里。

e.en: The old {clockmaker} repaired antique watches in his tiny shop.
e.zh: 那位老钟表匠在他狭小的店铺里修理古董表。

e.en: Her grandfather was a Swiss {clockmaker} famous for precision pieces.
e.zh: 她祖父是瑞士钟表匠，以精密作品闻名。

clocks.t:
n. 时钟（复数）
v. 记录时间

e.en: All the {clocks} in the house need new batteries.
e.zh: 家里所有的钟都需要换电池了。

e.en: He {clocks} in at seven every morning without fail.
e.zh: 他每天早上七点准时打卡上班，从不缺席。

clockwise.t:
adv. 顺时针地
adj. 顺时针方向的

e.en: Turn the screw {clockwise} until it feels tight.
e.zh: 顺时针转动螺丝直到拧紧。

e.en: The dancers moved {clockwise} around the maypole.
e.zh: 舞者们围着五月柱顺时针起舞。

clockwork.t: n. 发条装置；精密运转

e.en: The morning routine ran like {clockwork} after months of practice.
e.zh: 经过几个月的练习，早晨的流程进行得有条不紊。

e.en: He collects vintage {clockwork} toys from the 1950s.
e.zh: 他收藏五十年代的老式发条玩具。

e.en: The farmer kicked a {clod} of dirt off his boot.
e.zh: 农夫把靴子上的一块泥巴踢掉。

e.en: Don't be such a {clod}—apologize to her properly.
e.zh: 别这么蠢笨，好好向她道个歉。

clog.t:
v. 堵塞
n. 木底鞋

e.en: Grease can {clog} your kitchen drain in a matter of weeks.
e.zh: 油脂能在几周内堵塞你的厨房下水道。

e.en: She slipped off one wooden {clog} and rubbed her sore foot.
e.zh: 她脱下一只木屐，揉了揉酸痛的脚。

clogged.t:
adj. 阻塞的
v. 被堵住

e.en: The freeway was {clogged} with rush-hour traffic.
e.zh: 高速公路被高峰时段的车流堵得水泄不通。

e.en: My nose has been {clogged} since the pollen season started.
e.zh: 花粉季一开始我的鼻子就一直堵着。

e.en: She's a competitive {clogger} who performs at folk festivals.
e.zh: 她是一名木屐舞比赛选手，常在民俗节上表演。

e.en: Hair products are a notorious drain {clogger} in shared bathrooms.
e.zh: 在合用浴室里头发护理品是出了名的下水道杀手。

clogging.t:
v. 正在堵塞
n. 踢踏舞

e.en: Spam emails are {clogging} my inbox again this morning.
e.zh: 垃圾邮件今早又把我的收件箱塞满了。

e.en: Appalachian {clogging} mixes Irish step with African rhythms.
e.zh: 阿巴拉契亚木屐舞融合了爱尔兰踢踏与非洲节奏。

clogs.t:
n. 木底鞋（复数）
v. 堵塞

e.en: Dutch tourists posed for photos wearing wooden {clogs}.
e.zh: 荷兰游客穿着木屐摆姿势拍照。

e.en: Hair routinely {clogs} the shower drain in our apartment.
e.zh: 我们公寓的浴室下水道经常被头发堵住。

e.en: She bought a beautiful {cloisonne} vase at the Beijing antique market.
e.zh: 她在北京古玩市场买了一只精美的景泰蓝花瓶。

e.en: The museum displayed Ming dynasty {cloisonne} pieces in a glass case.
e.zh: 博物馆在玻璃柜里展出了明代景泰蓝作品。

cloister.t:
n. 修道院；回廊
v. 幽居

e.en: The monks walked silently through the medieval {cloister}.
e.zh: 修士们静静地穿行在中世纪的回廊里。

e.en: She tends to {cloister} herself in the library before exams.
e.zh: 她考试前总爱把自己关在图书馆里。

cloistered.t: adj. 隐居的；与世隔绝的

e.en: He led a {cloistered} life writing poetry in the countryside.
e.zh: 他过着与世隔绝的生活，在乡下写诗。

e.en: The nuns lived {cloistered} behind the convent walls.
e.zh: 修女们在修道院的高墙后过着隐修生活。

e.en: Tourists wandered the cathedral {cloisters} taking quiet photos.
e.zh: 游客们在大教堂的回廊里漫步，安静地拍着照。

e.en: Many famous philosophers spent years in monastic {cloisters}.
e.zh: 许多著名哲学家都在修道院的回廊里度过多年。

e.en: I could hear his heavy boots {clomp} up the stairs.
e.zh: 我能听见他穿着大靴子咚咚地走上楼梯。

e.en: The horses {clomp} across the cobblestone courtyard.
e.zh: 马匹哒哒地走过鹅卵石铺成的庭院。

e.en: Botanists use the term {clon} for genetically identical plants.
e.zh: 植物学家用 clon 一词指基因完全相同的植物群体。

e.en: Each {clon} of bamboo can spread across an entire hillside.
e.zh: 每一个竹子的克隆群都能蔓延整个山坡。

clonal.t: adj. 克隆的；无性繁殖的

e.en: Aspen groves are often a single {clonal} organism underground.
e.zh: 白杨林在地下往往是一个完整的克隆个体。

e.en: Researchers detected a {clonal} expansion of the cancer cells.
e.zh: 研究人员检测到癌细胞发生了克隆性扩增。

clone.t:
n. 克隆体；复制品
v. 克隆

e.en: Dolly the sheep was the first mammal {clone} in 1996.
e.zh: 绵羊多莉是1996年首个被克隆的哺乳动物。

e.en: Just {clone} the GitHub repo to get started.
e.zh: 只要把这个 GitHub 仓库克隆下来就能开始了。

cloned.t:
adj. 克隆出的
v. 已克隆

e.en: Scientists {cloned} the gene to study its function.
e.zh: 科学家克隆了这个基因以研究其功能。

e.en: He {cloned} the project and pushed his fix overnight.
e.zh: 他把项目克隆下来，连夜推送了修复代码。

clones.t:
n. 克隆体（复数）
v. 克隆

e.en: The market is flooded with cheap iPhone {clones}.
e.zh: 市场上充斥着廉价的iPhone山寨机。

e.en: Plant {clones} share identical DNA with the parent.
e.zh: 植物的克隆体与母本拥有完全相同的DNA。

e.en: The doctor prescribed {clonidine} to lower his blood pressure.
e.zh: 医生开了可乐定来降低他的血压。

e.en: {Clonidine} is sometimes used off-label for ADHD in children.
e.zh: 可乐定有时被超说明书用于治疗儿童多动症。

cloning.t:
n. 克隆技术
v. 正在复制

e.en: Human {cloning} remains banned in most countries.
e.zh: 人类克隆在大多数国家仍是被禁止的。

e.en: {Cloning} the database took about twenty minutes.
e.zh: 克隆这个数据库花了大约二十分钟。

clop.t:
n. 马蹄声
v. 嘚嘚作响

e.en: You could hear the {clop} of horse hooves on the cobblestones.
e.zh: 能听见马蹄在鹅卵石路上发出的哒哒声。

e.en: Her wooden sandals went {clop} down the wooden hallway.
e.zh: 她的木凉鞋踢踢踏踏地响过木地板走廊。

close.t:
v. 关闭；结束
adj. 接近的

e.en: Please {close} the door quietly when you leave.
e.zh: 你离开的时候请轻轻地关上门。

e.en: We're really {close} to finishing the project.
e.zh: 我们真的快完成这个项目了。

close-up.t:
n. 特写镜头
adj. 近距离的

e.en: The director shot a {close-up} of her trembling hands.
e.zh: 导演拍了她颤抖双手的特写镜头。

e.en: I want a {close-up} look at how the engine works.
e.zh: 我想近距离看看这台引擎是怎么运转的。

e.en: The shop is {closed} on Sundays and public holidays.
e.zh: 这家店周日和公共假期都不营业。

e.en: She kept her eyes {closed} during the meditation.
e.zh: 冥想时她一直闭着眼睛。

e.en: Don't be so {closed-minded} about new technology.
e.zh: 对新技术别这么固步自封。

e.en: His {closed-minded} attitude makes debate impossible.
e.zh: 他思想封闭的态度让辩论根本进行不下去。

e.en: The factory faces a permanent {closedown} next month.
e.zh: 这家工厂下个月将永久关闭。

e.en: The station's nightly {closedown} happens at midnight.
e.zh: 该电视台每晚午夜停播。

e.en: Investors are watching the stock price {closely} this week.
e.zh: 投资者本周正密切关注股价。

e.en: The two species are {closely} related genetically.
e.zh: 这两个物种在基因上密切相关。

e.en: I miss the {closeness} we had as roommates.
e.zh: 我怀念我们当室友时那种亲密感。

e.en: The {closeness} of the deadline made everyone anxious.
e.zh: 截止日期临近让大家都很焦虑。

e.en: The study measured {closenesses} between various dialects.
e.zh: 该研究衡量了不同方言之间的相近程度。

e.en: Different cultures define family {closenesses} differently.
e.zh: 不同文化对家庭亲密度的定义各不相同。

e.en: The store is having a {closeout} sale on winter coats.
e.zh: 那家店正在清仓甩卖冬季外套。

e.en: I grabbed these shoes at a {closeout} price.
e.zh: 我以清仓价抢到了这双鞋。

closer.t:
adj. 更近的
n. 终结者

e.en: Move a little {closer} so I can hear you.
e.zh: 靠近一点,这样我才能听见你说话。

e.en: The team's {closer} struck out the final batter.
e.zh: 球队的终结者三振了最后一名打者。

closes.t: v. 关闭（第三人称单数）

e.en: The library {closes} at nine on weeknights.
e.zh: 图书馆工作日晚上九点关门。

e.en: She always {closes} her laptop before leaving the desk.
e.zh: 她离开桌子前总会合上笔记本电脑。

e.en: Maya is my {closest} friend from college.
e.zh: 玛雅是我大学时最要好的朋友。

e.en: The {closest} gas station is ten miles away.
e.zh: 最近的加油站在十英里外。

closet.t:
n. 壁橱；储物间
adj. 隐秘的

e.en: Her {closet} is overflowing with vintage dresses.
e.zh: 她的衣柜里塞满了复古连衣裙。

e.en: He's a {closet} fan of cheesy pop music.
e.zh: 他偷偷迷恋那些俗气的流行歌曲。

e.en: He stayed {closeted} about his identity for years.
e.zh: 多年来他一直对自己的身份保持隐瞒。

e.en: The senator was {closeted} with advisors all afternoon.
e.zh: 那位参议员整个下午都和顾问们闭门商议。

e.en: The phone takes amazing {closeup} photos of flowers.
e.zh: 这款手机拍花朵特写效果惊艳。

e.en: Get a {closeup} of the bug on the leaf.
e.zh: 拍一张叶子上那只虫子的特写。

closing.t:
n. 闭幕；收盘
adj. 结束的

e.en: The {closing} ceremony will start at eight tonight.
e.zh: 闭幕式将于今晚八点开始。

e.en: We signed the papers at the {closing} yesterday.
e.zh: 我们昨天在过户手续上签了字。

e.en: The lab identified {clostridium} bacteria in the sample.
e.zh: 实验室在样本中检出了梭状芽孢杆菌。

e.en: Improperly canned food can harbor dangerous {clostridium}.
e.zh: 罐装不当的食品可能滋生危险的梭菌。

closure.t:
n. 关闭；了结
n. 闭包（编程）

e.en: The road {closure} caused major traffic delays.
e.zh: 道路封闭造成了严重的交通拥堵。

e.en: She needed {closure} after the difficult breakup.
e.zh: 那段艰难的分手后她需要一个了结。

e.en: Several {closures} are planned along the highway.
e.zh: 高速公路上计划进行多处封闭施工。

e.en: School {closures} were announced due to the snowstorm.
e.zh: 由于暴风雪,多所学校宣布停课。

clot.t:
n. 血块；凝块
v. 凝结

e.en: A blood {clot} in the leg can be dangerous.
e.zh: 腿部的血栓可能非常危险。

e.en: The cream began to {clot} after sitting out.
e.zh: 奶油放久后开始凝结。

e.en: Wipe the screen with a soft {cloth}.
e.zh: 用一块软布擦拭屏幕。

e.en: The dress is made from handwoven {cloth}.
e.zh: 这条裙子是用手织布做的。

e.en: The charity helps {clothe} children in need.
e.zh: 这家慈善机构帮助为贫困儿童提供衣物。

e.en: Parents struggle to feed and {clothe} large families.
e.zh: 父母要养活和供养一大家子并不容易。

clothed.t: adj. 穿着衣服的；被覆盖的

e.en: She was warmly {clothed} for the hike.
e.zh: 她穿得暖暖的去徒步。

e.en: The hills were {clothed} in autumn colors.
e.zh: 群山披上了秋天的色彩。

e.en: I need to wash these dirty {clothes}.
e.zh: 我得把这些脏衣服洗了。

e.en: He bought new {clothes} for the job interview.
e.zh: 他为面试买了新衣服。

clotheshorse.t:
n. 晾衣架
n. 爱打扮的人

e.en: My sister is a total {clotheshorse} who loves shopping.
e.zh: 我姐姐是个十足的衣服迷,超爱购物。

e.en: Hang the wet shirts on the {clotheshorse} to dry.
e.zh: 把湿衬衫挂在晾衣架上晾干。

e.en: Grandma still hangs sheets on the backyard {clothesline}.
e.zh: 奶奶仍把床单晾在后院的晾衣绳上。

e.en: The {clothesline} sagged under the heavy wet towels.
e.zh: 晾衣绳被湿毛巾压得弯了下去。

e.en: Use a {clothespin} to keep the chip bag sealed.
e.zh: 用一个衣夹把薯片袋夹紧。

e.en: She fastened the towel with a wooden {clothespin}.
e.zh: 她用一个木衣夹把毛巾夹住。

e.en: He visited his favorite {clothier} for a custom suit.
e.zh: 他去他最喜欢的服装商定做了一套西装。

e.en: The high-end {clothier} only sells handmade jackets.
e.zh: 那家高端服饰店只卖手工外套。

e.en: Pack warm {clothing} for the mountain trip.
e.zh: 去山里要带上保暖衣物。

e.en: The brand makes sustainable {clothing} from recycled materials.
e.zh: 该品牌用回收材料制作可持续服装。

clothings.t: n. 衣物（clothing 的少见复数）

e.en: Various traditional {clothings} were displayed at the museum.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了各式各样的传统服饰。

e.en: The shop imports {clothings} from several Asian countries.
e.zh: 这家店从几个亚洲国家进口服装。

e.en: Keep clean microfiber {cloths} for polishing the lenses.
e.zh: 准备一些干净的超细纤维布来擦镜片。

e.en: The kitchen drawer is full of dish {cloths}.
e.zh: 厨房抽屉里满是抹布。

e.en: Scones taste best with jam and {clotted} cream.
e.zh: 司康饼配果酱和凝脂奶油最美味。

e.en: The blood had {clotted} around the small wound.
e.zh: 血已在小伤口周围凝固了。

clotting.t:
n. 凝血；凝结
v. 凝结（clot 的现在分词）

e.en: Vitamin K is essential for blood {clotting}.
e.zh: 维生素K对血液凝固至关重要。

e.en: This medication prevents abnormal {clotting} in arteries.
e.zh: 这种药能预防动脉异常凝血。

cloture.t: n. (议会) 终止辩论程序

e.en: Senators voted for {cloture} to end the filibuster.
e.zh: 参议员投票通过结束辩论以终止冗长发言。

e.en: The motion for {cloture} narrowly passed the chamber.
e.zh: 终结辩论的动议在议会勉强通过。

cloud.t:
n. 云；云端（服务）
v. 使模糊

e.en: All my photos are backed up to the {cloud}.
e.zh: 我所有的照片都备份到了云端。

e.en: A dark {cloud} drifted across the afternoon sky.
e.zh: 一片乌云飘过午后的天空。

e.en: A sudden {cloudburst} flooded the streets in minutes.
e.zh: 一场突如其来的暴雨几分钟内就把街道淹没了。

e.en: We sheltered under a tree during the {cloudburst}.
e.zh: 暴雨倾盆时我们躲在一棵树下。

e.en: Anger {clouded} his judgment during the meeting.
e.zh: 愤怒让他在会议上判断失常。

e.en: The mirror {clouded} over with bathroom steam.
e.zh: 镜子被浴室的蒸汽蒙上了一层雾。

e.en: The forecast predicts increasing {cloudiness} tomorrow afternoon.
e.zh: 预报说明天下午云量将逐渐增多。

e.en: Slight {cloudiness} in the soup means it's spoiled.
e.zh: 汤变得略微浑浊就说明已经变质了。

clouding.t:
n. 变阴；模糊
v. 使阴沉

e.en: Stress is {clouding} my ability to think clearly.
e.zh: 压力正影响着我清晰思考的能力。

e.en: Steam from the kettle was {clouding} the window.
e.zh: 水壶的蒸汽让窗户蒙上了一层雾。

e.en: We hiked under a perfectly {cloudless} blue sky.
e.zh: 我们在万里无云的蓝天下徒步。

e.en: The {cloudless} night was perfect for stargazing.
e.zh: 那个晴朗无云的夜晚很适合观星。

e.en: The pillow has a soft, {cloudlike} feel.
e.zh: 这个枕头有种柔软如云的触感。

e.en: She wore a {cloudlike} layered tulle skirt.
e.zh: 她穿着一条云朵般层叠的薄纱裙。

e.en: Dark {clouds} are gathering over the mountains.
e.zh: 乌云正在山顶上聚集。

e.en: The plane climbed above the {clouds} smoothly.
e.zh: 飞机平稳地爬升到了云层之上。

e.en: It's {cloudy} today, so bring an umbrella.
e.zh: 今天阴天,带把伞吧。

e.en: The pond water looks {cloudy} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后池塘的水看起来很浑浊。

e.en: A small stream ran through the rocky {clough}.
e.zh: 一条小溪流过那条石质峡谷。

e.en: They hiked down into the wooded {clough}.
e.zh: 他们徒步走下树木茂密的山涧。

clout.t:
n. 影响力；权势
v. 猛击

e.en: The CEO has serious political {clout} in the city.
e.zh: 那位首席执行官在城里有相当大的政治影响力。

e.en: Influencers gain {clout} by going viral on TikTok.
e.zh: 网红通过在TikTok爆红来积累影响力。

clove.t:
n. 丁香（香料）
n. (蒜) 瓣

e.en: Add one {clove} of garlic to the sauce.
e.zh: 在酱汁里加一瓣大蒜。

e.en: The mulled wine smelled of cinnamon and {clove}.
e.zh: 热红酒散发着肉桂和丁香的香气。

e.en: Goats and deer have {cloven} hooves.
e.zh: 山羊和鹿都长着偶蹄。

e.en: The old oak was {cloven} by lightning.
e.zh: 那棵老橡树被闪电劈成了两半。

e.en: She found a four-leaf {clover} in the lawn.
e.zh: 她在草坪上找到了一棵四叶草。

e.en: Bees were buzzing around the wild {clover}.
e.zh: 蜜蜂在野生三叶草周围嗡嗡飞舞。

e.en: The highway exits via a large {cloverleaf} interchange.
e.zh: 高速公路通过一个大型苜蓿叶式立交出口。

e.en: She baked a beautiful {cloverleaf} dinner roll.
e.zh: 她烤了一个漂亮的三叶造型小餐包。

clovis.t: n. 克洛维斯 (地名/人名)

e.en: Archaeologists discovered a {clovis} spear point in the cave.
e.zh: 考古学家在洞穴中发现了一枚克洛维斯矛尖。

e.en: The {clovis} culture spread across ancient North America.
e.zh: 克洛维斯文化曾遍布古代北美洲。

clown.t:
n. 小丑
v. 扮小丑；胡闹

e.en: A {clown} made balloon animals at the kid's party.
e.zh: 一个小丑在儿童派对上做气球动物。

e.en: Stop trying to {clown} around during the lecture.
e.zh: 上课时别再嬉皮笑脸地胡闹了。

e.en: Stop {clowning} around and finish your homework now.
e.zh: 别再胡闹了，赶紧把作业做完。

e.en: The kids were {clowning} for the camera at the party.
e.zh: 孩子们在派对上对着镜头扮鬼脸。

e.en: His {clownish} antics made the whole office laugh.
e.zh: 他滑稽的举动逗得整个办公室哈哈大笑。

e.en: She wore a {clownish} outfit to the costume party.
e.zh: 她穿着一身小丑般的服装去化装舞会。

e.en: The circus {clowns} entertained children with funny tricks.
e.zh: 马戏团的小丑用滑稽把戏逗孩子们开心。

e.en: Some people are afraid of {clowns} since childhood.
e.zh: 有些人从小就害怕小丑。
