e.en: Fans flooded social media {congratulating} the team on their championship.
e.zh: 球迷们涌入社交媒体祝贺球队夺冠。

e.en: She spent the evening {congratulating} graduates and posing for photos.
e.zh: 她整晚都在祝贺毕业生并合影留念。

e.en: He gave her a hug as a {congratulation} for her success.
e.zh: 他拥抱她，以此祝贺她的成功。

e.en: A small bow served as his silent {congratulation}.
e.zh: 他微微鞠躬，无声地表示祝贺。

congratulations.t:
n. 恭喜，祝贺
int. 恭喜！

e.en: {Congratulations} on your new baby — she's adorable!
e.zh: 恭喜你喜得千金，她真可爱！

e.en: Send my {congratulations} to the bride and groom.
e.zh: 代我向新郎新娘致以祝贺。

e.en: She received a {congratulatory} message from the president himself.
e.zh: 她收到了总统本人发来的贺信。

e.en: He raised a {congratulatory} toast to the newlyweds.
e.zh: 他举杯向这对新人致以祝贺。

e.en: Each {congregant} lit a candle during the evening service.
e.zh: 晚间礼拜时，每位会众都点燃了一支蜡烛。

e.en: The pastor greeted every {congregant} at the door.
e.zh: 牧师在门口逐一问候每位前来礼拜的信众。

e.en: Students often {congregate} near the coffee shop after class.
e.zh: 下课后学生们常常聚集在咖啡店附近。

e.en: Pigeons {congregate} in the square waiting for crumbs.
e.zh: 鸽子聚集在广场上等着捡面包屑。

e.en: Hundreds of fans {congregated} outside the stadium before the concert.
e.zh: 演唱会前，数百名粉丝聚集在体育场外。

e.en: Reporters {congregated} around the courthouse waiting for the verdict.
e.zh: 记者们聚集在法院外等待判决结果。

congregates.t: v. 聚集（第三人称单数）

e.en: A noisy crowd {congregates} at this bar every Friday night.
e.zh: 每周五晚都有一群吵闹的人聚集在这家酒吧。

e.en: Wildlife often {congregates} near water during the dry season.
e.zh: 旱季时野生动物常常聚集在水源附近。

e.en: Teenagers were {congregating} outside the mall after school.
e.zh: 放学后青少年们在商场外聚集。

e.en: Whales are {congregating} in the bay to feed.
e.zh: 鲸鱼正聚集在海湾里觅食。

e.en: The {congregation} stood and sang the closing hymn together.
e.zh: 会众起立，一同唱起结束的赞美诗。

e.en: This church has a small but devoted {congregation}.
e.zh: 这座教堂的会众不多，但都很虔诚。

e.en: The service ended with a {congregational} prayer.
e.zh: 礼拜以会众共同祈祷作为结束。

e.en: She grew up attending a {congregational} church in Boston.
e.zh: 她从小在波士顿一所公理会教堂做礼拜。

e.en: Her grandfather was a devout {Congregationalist} minister.
e.zh: 她的外公是一位虔诚的公理会牧师。

e.en: The town's {Congregationalist} church dates back to 1820.
e.zh: 镇上的公理会教堂可以追溯到1820年。

e.en: Many rural {congregations} are shrinking as young people move away.
e.zh: 由于年轻人外迁，许多乡村教会的会众正在减少。

e.en: The bishop visits all the {congregations} in his diocese yearly.
e.zh: 主教每年都会走访其教区内所有的会众。

connected.t:
adj. 已连接的；相关的
v. connect 的过去式

e.en: My phone isn't {connected} to the office network yet.
e.zh: 我的手机还没有连接到公司网络。

e.en: She felt deeply {connected} to her grandmother's stories.
e.zh: 她对外婆讲的故事有很深的情感共鸣。

e.en: Social media gives us a feeling of constant {connectedness}.
e.zh: 社交媒体让我们感觉始终处于彼此连接之中。

e.en: Hiking alone, she missed a sense of {connectedness} with others.
e.zh: 独自徒步时,她渴望与他人之间的那种联系感。

e.en: My cousin moved to {Connecticut} for a tech job.
e.zh: 我表哥为了一份科技公司的工作搬到了康涅狄格州。

e.en: {Connecticut} is known for its colonial-era towns and coastline.
e.zh: 康涅狄格州以其殖民时期的小镇和海岸线闻名。

connecting.t:
v. 正在连接
adj. 连接的；中转的

e.en: We missed our {connecting} flight because of the delay.
e.zh: 由于航班延误,我们错过了转机航班。

e.en: A long bridge is {connecting} the two islands.
e.zh: 一座长桥把两座岛屿连接了起来。

connection.t:
n. 连接；网络连接
n. 关系；人脉

e.en: The Wi-Fi {connection} keeps dropping in this café.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆的 Wi-Fi 总是断线。

e.en: There's a clear {connection} between sleep and mood.
e.zh: 睡眠和情绪之间有明显的联系。

e.en: He landed the job through family {connections}.
e.zh: 他靠家里的人脉找到了那份工作。

e.en: The app shows train {connections} for your whole trip.
e.zh: 该应用会显示整段行程的列车换乘信息。

connective.t:
adj. 连接的
n. 连接词；结缔组织

e.en: Tendons are tough {connective} tissue that links muscle to bone.
e.zh: 肌腱是连接肌肉和骨骼的坚韧结缔组织。

e.en: Good writing relies on smooth {connective} phrases.
e.zh: 好的写作依赖于流畅的连接短语。

connectivity.t: n. 网络连接性；互联互通

e.en: Rural areas still struggle with poor internet {connectivity}.
e.zh: 农村地区仍然受困于网络连接不良的问题。

e.en: The new router boosts {connectivity} across the entire house.
e.zh: 新路由器提升了整间屋子的网络连接质量。

e.en: You'll need a USB-C {connector} for this monitor.
e.zh: 这台显示器需要用到 USB-C 接口。

e.en: She's a natural {connector} who introduces people to opportunities.
e.zh: 她天生擅长牵线搭桥,常为别人介绍机会。

connects.t: v. connect 的第三人称单数

e.en: This cable {connects} the camera directly to your laptop.
e.zh: 这根线把相机直接连到你的笔记本电脑上。

e.en: The new bridge {connects} downtown to the airport.
e.zh: 这座新桥把市中心和机场连接了起来。

conned.t: v. 欺骗（con 的过去式）

e.en: He {conned} his neighbor into investing in a fake startup.
e.zh: 他骗邻居投资了一家假初创公司。

e.en: Tourists are often {conned} by fake taxi drivers at the airport.
e.zh: 游客常常在机场被假出租车司机骗。

connemara.t: n. 康尼马拉（爱尔兰地区）

e.en: They drove through {Connemara} to see the wild Atlantic coast.
e.zh: 他们驱车穿过康尼马拉,去看狂野的大西洋海岸。

e.en: {Connemara} ponies are prized for their gentle temperament.
e.zh: 康尼马拉小马以温顺的性情而备受喜爱。

connexion.t: n. 连接（connection 的英式旧拼法）

e.en: The article uses the older spelling {connexion} throughout.
e.zh: 这篇文章通篇使用较老的拼写形式 connexion。

e.en: She felt a deep {connexion} to the village of her ancestors.
e.zh: 她对祖辈所在的那个村庄怀有深厚的情感。

e.en: His {connexions} in publishing helped launch her novel.
e.zh: 他在出版界的人脉帮她的小说顺利出版。

e.en: The diary mentions {connexions} between several London families.
e.zh: 日记中提到了伦敦几个家族之间的关系。

conning.t: v. 欺骗（con 的现在分词）

e.en: He's been {conning} elderly people out of their pensions.
e.zh: 他一直在骗取老年人的养老金。

e.en: The captain stood on the {conning} tower of the submarine.
e.zh: 舰长站在潜艇的指挥塔上。

conniption.t: n. 勃然大怒；歇斯底里

e.en: Mom had a {conniption} when she saw the broken vase.
e.zh: 妈妈看到那个摔碎的花瓶后大发雷霆。

e.en: Don't have a {conniption}—I'll fix the printer in a minute.
e.zh: 别急得跳脚,我马上就把打印机修好。

e.en: The fraud succeeded only with the {connivance} of senior managers.
e.zh: 这场骗局得手全靠高层管理者的纵容。

e.en: He claimed the leak happened without his {connivance}.
e.zh: 他声称泄密一事并没有他的暗中协助。

e.en: Officials should not {connive} with corrupt contractors.
e.zh: 官员不应与腐败的承包商串通一气。

e.en: They {connive} to push their rival out of the market.
e.zh: 他们密谋要把竞争对手挤出市场。

e.en: The film's villain is a {conniving} corporate lawyer.
e.zh: 电影中的反派是一个诡计多端的公司律师。

e.en: I don't trust her {conniving} smile one bit.
e.zh: 我一点也不相信她那阴险的笑容。

e.en: He's a true {connoisseur} of single-origin coffee.
e.zh: 他是一位真正懂行的单一产地咖啡爱好者。

e.en: You don't need to be a wine {connoisseur} to enjoy this bottle.
e.zh: 不必是品酒行家也能享受这瓶酒。

e.en: Cheese {connoisseurs} flock to the small shop in Lyon.
e.zh: 奶酪行家们纷纷光顾里昂那家小店。

e.en: The auction attracted art {connoisseurs} from around the world.
e.zh: 这场拍卖吸引了来自世界各地的艺术鉴赏家。

e.en: Wine {connoisseurship} takes years of patient tasting.
e.zh: 品酒鉴赏功夫需要多年耐心品尝才能练成。

e.en: Her {connoisseurship} of Japanese prints is widely respected.
e.zh: 她对日本浮世绘的鉴赏力广受推崇。

connotation.t: n. 言外之意；隐含意义

e.en: The word 'cheap' carries a negative {connotation} in English.
e.zh: cheap 这个词在英语里带有贬义。

e.en: 'Home' has a warmer {connotation} than 'house'.
e.zh: home 比 house 给人更温暖的感觉。

connotations.t: n. 内涵；弦外之音（复数）

e.en: 'Skinny' and 'slim' have very different {connotations}.
e.zh: skinny 和 slim 的情感色彩相差很大。

e.en: The brand name has unfortunate {connotations} in Spanish.
e.zh: 这个品牌名字在西班牙语里有不太好的联想含义。

connotative.t: adj. 含蓄的；有隐含意义的

e.en: Poets rely on the {connotative} power of everyday words.
e.zh: 诗人借助日常词汇的暗含意义来表达情感。

e.en: Translators must watch for the {connotative} meaning, not just the literal one.
e.zh: 译者必须关注词语的暗示义,而不只是字面义。

e.en: In English, 'home' can {connote} safety and belonging.
e.zh: 在英语里,home 一词常暗含安全感和归属感。

e.en: Bright colors often {connote} energy and optimism.
e.zh: 鲜艳的颜色常让人联想到活力与乐观。

e.en: For her, the word 'office' {connoted} stress and long hours.
e.zh: 对她而言,'办公室'一词意味着压力和漫长的加班。

e.en: In that era, white dresses {connoted} purity and tradition.
e.zh: 在那个年代,白色裙装象征着纯洁与传统。

connotes.t: v. connote 的第三人称单数

e.en: The word "home" {connotes} warmth and safety.
e.zh: "家"这个词隐含着温暖与安全的含义。

e.en: In tech, "agile" {connotes} flexibility and fast iteration.
e.zh: 在科技领域，"敏捷"暗示着灵活性和快速迭代。

e.en: She chose colors {connoting} calm and trust.
e.zh: 她选择了暗示平静与信任的颜色。

e.en: The brand uses imagery {connoting} luxury and exclusivity.
e.zh: 该品牌使用暗示奢华与专属感的图像。

e.en: They settled into quiet {connubial} bliss after the wedding.
e.zh: 婚礼后他们过上了宁静的夫妻生活。

e.en: The film explores {connubial} tensions in modern marriages.
e.zh: 这部电影探讨了现代婚姻中的夫妻矛盾。

conoco.t: n. 康菲石油（美国石油公司）

e.en: We stopped at a {Conoco} station to refuel.
e.zh: 我们在一家康菲加油站停车加油。

e.en: {Conoco} is a major American oil company.
e.zh: 康菲是美国一家大型石油公司。

e.en: She trained hard to {conquer} her fear of heights.
e.zh: 她刻苦训练以克服自己的恐高症。

e.en: The startup hopes to {conquer} the Asian market next year.
e.zh: 这家初创公司希望明年攻占亚洲市场。

conquered.t:
v. conquer 的过去式
adj. 被征服的

e.en: He finally {conquered} the marathon after years of training.
e.zh: 经过多年训练，他终于征服了马拉松。

e.en: Rome {conquered} much of Europe two thousand years ago.
e.zh: 罗马在两千年前征服了欧洲大部分地区。

conquering.t:
v. 正在征服
adj. 所向披靡的

e.en: She returned home like a {conquering} hero.
e.zh: 她像凯旋的英雄一样回到家中。

e.en: {Conquering} self-doubt is harder than any external challenge.
e.zh: 战胜自我怀疑比任何外部挑战都更难。

e.en: William the {Conqueror} invaded England in 1066.
e.zh: 征服者威廉于1066年入侵英格兰。

e.en: History rarely remembers the {conqueror} kindly.
e.zh: 历史很少会善待征服者。

conquers.t: v. conquer 的第三人称单数

e.en: Love {conquers} all, or so the song claims.
e.zh: 爱能战胜一切，至少歌里是这么唱的。

e.en: The team {conquers} every opponent with disciplined defense.
e.zh: 该队凭借严密防守战胜了每一个对手。

e.en: The Norman {conquest} reshaped English language and culture.
e.zh: 诺曼征服重塑了英语语言与文化。

e.en: Climbing Everest was her greatest personal {conquest}.
e.zh: 登顶珠峰是她最伟大的个人成就。

e.en: Alexander's {conquests} stretched from Greece to India.
e.zh: 亚历山大的征服疆域从希腊延伸到印度。

e.en: He boasts about his romantic {conquests} far too often.
e.zh: 他太爱炫耀自己情场上的战绩了。

conquistador.t: n. 征服者（尤指16世纪西班牙人）

e.en: The {conquistador} Cortés led the invasion of Mexico.
e.zh: 征服者科尔特斯率军入侵墨西哥。

e.en: Museums display armor worn by every Spanish {conquistador}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出着每位西班牙征服者所穿的盔甲。

e.en: {Congress} passed the new infrastructure bill last week.
e.zh: 国会上周通过了新的基础设施法案。

e.en: The medical {congress} attracted researchers from forty countries.
e.zh: 这次医学大会吸引了来自四十个国家的研究人员。

e.en: The bill faces tough {congressional} hearings next month.
e.zh: 该法案下个月将面临艰难的国会听证。

e.en: She works as a {congressional} aide in Washington.
e.zh: 她在华盛顿担任国会议员助理。

e.en: The {congressman} spoke passionately about climate policy.
e.zh: 这位国会议员就气候政策发表了热情洋溢的讲话。

e.en: Voters in the district reelected the same {congressman} for years.
e.zh: 该选区的选民连续多年都让同一位国会议员连任。

congressperson.t: n. 国会议员（中性称呼）

e.en: Each {congressperson} represents about 760,000 constituents.
e.zh: 每位国会议员代表约76万名选民。

e.en: Voters wrote to their {congressperson} demanding action on housing.
e.zh: 选民们给他们的国会议员写信，要求在住房问题上采取行动。

e.en: The {congresswoman} introduced a bill to expand childcare access.
e.zh: 这位女议员提出了一项扩大托儿服务的法案。

e.en: She became the first {congresswoman} elected from her state.
e.zh: 她成为该州首位当选的女性国会议员。

congruence.t:
n. 一致；吻合
n. (数学) 全等

e.en: There's a striking {congruence} between his words and his actions.
e.zh: 他言行之间高度一致，令人印象深刻。

e.en: The study found {congruence} between the two survey results.
e.zh: 研究发现这两份调查结果高度吻合。

congruent.t:
adj. 一致的；相符的
adj. (数学) 全等的

e.en: His values are perfectly {congruent} with the company's mission.
e.zh: 他的价值观与公司使命完全契合。

e.en: Two triangles are {congruent} if all sides match in length.
e.zh: 如果两个三角形所有边长都相等，它们就是全等的。

e.en: There's a pleasing {congruity} between the design and the brand.
e.zh: 设计与品牌之间存在着令人愉悦的一致性。

e.en: The report lacked {congruity} between its data and conclusions.
e.zh: 报告的数据与结论之间缺乏一致性。

e.en: Her calm reaction was {congruous} with her usual personality.
e.zh: 她冷静的反应与她一贯的性格相符。

e.en: The modern lobby felt {congruous} with the building's sleek exterior.
e.zh: 现代化的大堂与建筑流线型的外观十分协调。

conic.t: adj. 圆锥的；圆锥曲线的

e.en: Parabolas and ellipses are types of {conic} sections.
e.zh: 抛物线和椭圆都属于圆锥曲线。

e.en: The lamp has an elegant {conic} shade made of paper.
e.zh: 这盏灯有一个雅致的圆锥形纸灯罩。

e.en: Workers wore {conical} straw hats in the rice fields.
e.zh: 工人们戴着锥形草帽在稻田里劳作。

e.en: Volcanoes often have a classic {conical} shape.
e.zh: 火山通常呈典型的圆锥形。

conifer.t: n. 针叶树；松柏类植物

e.en: A tall {conifer} stood at the edge of the garden.
e.zh: 花园边缘矗立着一棵高大的针叶树。

e.en: Pine is the most common {conifer} in this region.
e.zh: 松树是这一地区最常见的针叶树。

e.en: Most of Canada is covered by vast {coniferous} forests.
e.zh: 加拿大大部分地区被广袤的针叶林覆盖。

e.en: {Coniferous} trees keep their needles throughout the winter.
e.zh: 针叶树整个冬天都不会落叶。

coniston.t: n. 科尼斯顿（英国地名）

e.en: We hiked around {Coniston} Water during our Lake District trip.
e.zh: 我们在湖区旅行时绕着科尼斯顿湖徒步。

e.en: {Coniston} is famous for its scenic mountain trails.
e.zh: 科尼斯顿以其风景如画的山间小径而闻名。

e.en: His theory remains largely {conjectural} without supporting evidence.
e.zh: 他的理论缺乏证据支持，基本上仍是推测性的。

e.en: The historian admitted some details were purely {conjectural}.
e.zh: 这位历史学家承认有些细节纯属推测。

conjecture.t:
n. 推测；猜想
v. 推测

e.en: Whether aliens exist is still pure {conjecture}.
e.zh: 外星人是否存在仍纯属猜测。

e.en: Analysts {conjecture} that interest rates will fall next quarter.
e.zh: 分析师推测下个季度利率将会下调。

conjectured.t: v. 推测（conjecture 的过去式）

e.en: Scientists {conjectured} that the comet would return in 200 years.
e.zh: 科学家推测这颗彗星将在两百年后回归。

e.en: She {conjectured} that he was hiding something from her.
e.zh: 她猜测他在向她隐瞒什么。

conjectures.t: n./v. 推测（conjecture 的复数/三单）

e.en: His book is full of bold {conjectures} about the universe.
e.zh: 他的书中充满了关于宇宙的大胆推测。

e.en: The detective {conjectures} that the suspect fled north.
e.zh: 侦探推测嫌疑人向北方逃跑了。

conjecturing.t: v. 推测（conjecture 的现在分词）

e.en: Reporters were {conjecturing} about the cause of the crash.
e.zh: 记者们正在猜测事故的起因。

e.en: Stop {conjecturing} and wait for the official results.
e.zh: 别再瞎猜了，等官方结果出来吧。

e.en: The two rivers {conjoin} just south of the city.
e.zh: 两条河流在城市南边交汇。

e.en: They tried to {conjoin} their efforts on the new project.
e.zh: 他们试图在新项目上联合努力。

conjoined.t:
adj. 连体的（如连体婴）
v. 结合

e.en: The {conjoined} twins underwent a successful separation surgery.
e.zh: 这对连体双胞胎成功接受了分离手术。

e.en: Their fates seemed {conjoined} from the very beginning.
e.zh: 他们的命运似乎从一开始就紧紧相连。

conjoining.t: v. 连接；结合（现在分词）

e.en: The bridge is {conjoining} the two halves of the city.
e.zh: 这座桥将城市的两半连接了起来。

e.en: She wrote about {conjoining} tradition with modern design.
e.zh: 她写了一篇关于将传统与现代设计相结合的文章。

e.en: The two universities run the program {conjointly}.
e.zh: 这两所大学共同运营该项目。

e.en: They own the cafe {conjointly} as business partners.
e.zh: 他们作为商业伙伴共同拥有这家咖啡馆。

e.en: The prison allows {conjugal} visits once a month.
e.zh: 这所监狱每月允许一次夫妻探视。

e.en: They celebrated fifty years of {conjugal} happiness.
e.zh: 他们庆祝了五十年的婚姻幸福。

conjugate.t:
v. (动词) 变位
adj. 共轭的

e.en: Students learn to {conjugate} French verbs in different tenses.
e.zh: 学生们学习如何变位法语动词的不同时态。

e.en: It's hard to {conjugate} irregular verbs from memory.
e.zh: 靠记忆变位不规则动词很困难。

e.en: In class we {conjugated} the verb 'to be' in every tense.
e.zh: 课上我们把动词 to be 的所有时态都变位了一遍。

e.en: The chemist used a {conjugated} polymer to build the solar cell.
e.zh: 化学家用一种共轭聚合物制造了太阳能电池。

conjugation.t:
n. 动词变位
n. (生物) 接合

e.en: Spanish verb {conjugation} takes a while to memorize.
e.zh: 西班牙语动词变位需要花些时间才能记住。

e.en: The app drills you on French {conjugation} every morning.
e.zh: 这款应用每天早上让你练习法语动词变位。

conjunction.t:
n. (语法) 连词
n. 结合；同时发生

e.en: 'And' is the most common {conjunction} in English.
e.zh: and 是英语中最常见的连词。

e.en: The festival runs in {conjunction} with the city's anniversary.
e.zh: 该节日与城市周年庆同时举办。

e.en: Coordinating {conjunctions} like 'but' and 'or' link equal clauses.
e.zh: 像 but 和 or 这样的并列连词用来连接同等分句。

e.en: Astronomers observed two rare planetary {conjunctions} this year.
e.zh: 天文学家今年观测到了两次罕见的行星合相。

e.en: The doctor examined the {conjunctiva} for signs of inflammation.
e.zh: 医生检查了结膜是否有发炎迹象。

e.en: Allergies often cause the {conjunctiva} to turn red and itchy.
e.zh: 过敏常常让结膜发红并发痒。

e.en: She was diagnosed with a mild {conjunctival} infection.
e.zh: 她被诊断出患有轻度结膜感染。

e.en: The drops are designed to relieve {conjunctival} irritation.
e.zh: 这种眼药水旨在缓解结膜刺激。

e.en: 'However' functions as a {conjunctive} adverb in that sentence.
e.zh: however 在那句话里充当连接副词。

e.en: Latin uses the {conjunctive} mood for hypothetical situations.
e.zh: 拉丁语用虚拟式表达假设情境。

e.en: The school sent him home with {conjunctivitis} again.
e.zh: 学校又因为他得了红眼病让他回家了。

e.en: Viral {conjunctivitis} spreads easily among young children.
e.zh: 病毒性结膜炎在小朋友之间很容易传染。

conjunctural.t: adj. 时势的；经济形势的

e.en: Analysts blamed the slowdown on {conjunctural} factors, not structural ones.
e.zh: 分析师将放缓归因于周期性因素,而非结构性问题。

e.en: The report focuses on {conjunctural} trends in the housing market.
e.zh: 该报告聚焦于房地产市场的短期周期趋势。

e.en: At this critical {conjuncture}, the company needs decisive leadership.
e.zh: 在这一关键时刻,公司需要果断的领导力。

e.en: The crisis arose from a rare {conjuncture} of events.
e.zh: 这场危机源于多个事件罕见地汇集在一起。

e.en: The novel opens with a midnight {conjuration} in the forest.
e.zh: 小说以森林中午夜的召唤仪式开场。

e.en: Her speech was a clever {conjuration} of childhood memories.
e.zh: 她的演讲巧妙地唤起了童年的回忆。

conjure.t:
v. 变魔术；召唤出
v. 使想起

e.en: The smell can {conjure} memories of my grandmother's kitchen.
e.zh: 那股气味能让我想起外婆厨房的味道。

e.en: Magicians {conjure} doves out of empty hats.
e.zh: 魔术师能从空帽子里变出鸽子。

e.en: The chef {conjured} a five-course meal from leftovers.
e.zh: 厨师用剩菜变出了一桌五道菜的大餐。

e.en: Her words {conjured} an image of summer by the sea.
e.zh: 她的话让我脑海中浮现出海边夏日的画面。

e.en: A street {conjurer} pulled a coin from behind my ear.
e.zh: 街头魔术师从我耳后变出了一枚硬币。

e.en: The children watched the {conjurer} in delighted silence.
e.zh: 孩子们出神地静静看着那位魔术师表演。

e.en: The word 'Paris' instantly {conjures} images of cafés and rain.
e.zh: '巴黎'这个词立刻让人想到咖啡馆和雨景。

e.en: She {conjures} elaborate desserts from the simplest ingredients.
e.zh: 她能用最简单的食材做出精致的甜点。

conjuring.t:
n. 魔术
v. 召唤；变出

e.en: He spent the afternoon {conjuring} excuses to skip the meeting.
e.zh: 他整个下午都在编借口想跷掉会议。

e.en: The magician's {conjuring} act left the audience astonished.
e.zh: 魔术师的变戏法表演让观众惊叹不已。

conjuror.t: n. 魔术师（conjurer 的异体）

e.en: A skilled {conjuror} kept the kids entertained at the party.
e.zh: 一位技艺高超的魔术师在派对上把孩子们逗得很开心。

e.en: The medieval {conjuror} was both feared and admired.
e.zh: 那位中世纪的术士既令人畏惧又令人敬佩。

conk.t:
v. 敲头
v. 抛锚（conk out）

e.en: My old laptop is about to {conk} out for good.
e.zh: 我那台旧笔记本快要彻底报废了。

e.en: Be careful not to {conk} your head on the low beam.
e.zh: 小心别让头撞到那根低横梁上。

conker.t: n. 七叶树果实（英式儿童游戏用）

e.en: He polished the {conker} until it gleamed like wood.
e.zh: 他把那颗七叶树果擦得像木头一样发亮。

e.en: British kids string a {conker} on a lace and battle friends.
e.zh: 英国小孩会把七叶树果穿上绳子和朋友斗果游戏。

e.en: The {conman} swindled retirees out of their savings.
e.zh: 那个骗子骗走了退休老人们的积蓄。

e.en: Police finally arrested the {conman} after a year-long chase.
e.zh: 警方追查一年后终于抓住了那个骗子。

conn.t:
v. (航海) 指挥操舵
n. 操舵指挥权

e.en: The captain ordered the lieutenant to take the {conn}.
e.zh: 舰长下令由中尉接管操舵指挥权。

e.en: She had the {conn} as the destroyer entered the harbor.
e.zh: 驱逐舰进港时由她负责操舵指挥。

connaught.t: n. 康诺特（爱尔兰地区名）

e.en: They booked a weekend at the famous {Connaught} hotel in Mayfair.
e.zh: 他们在梅菲尔著名的康诺特酒店订了一个周末。

e.en: {Connaught} is the westernmost province of Ireland.
e.zh: 康诺特是爱尔兰最西部的省份。

connect.t:
v. 连接；联系
v. 建立关系

e.en: You can {connect} the printer over Wi-Fi in seconds.
e.zh: 你可以在几秒内通过 Wi-Fi 连接打印机。

e.en: It's hard to {connect} with strangers at big parties.
e.zh: 在大型派对上很难和陌生人产生共鸣。

cons.t:
n. 缺点、不利因素（pros and cons）
v. 欺骗

e.en: List the pros and {cons} before making a decision.
e.zh: 在做决定前先列出利与弊。

e.en: He {cons} tourists out of money near the train station.
e.zh: 他在火车站附近骗游客的钱。

e.en: Marriage laws often forbid unions based on close {consanguinity}.
e.zh: 婚姻法通常禁止近亲血缘之间的结合。

e.en: The two families share a distant {consanguinity}.
e.zh: 这两个家族有着远亲血缘关系。

e.en: His {conscience} kept him awake all night.
e.zh: 良心让他整夜无法入睡。

e.en: She returned the wallet to clear her {conscience}.
e.zh: 她归还了钱包以求心安。

conscienceless.t: adj. 没良心的、泯灭良知的

e.en: The {conscienceless} scammer targeted elderly victims online.
e.zh: 那个毫无良心的骗子在网上专挑老年人下手。

e.en: Critics called the policy cruel and {conscienceless}.
e.zh: 批评者称这项政策残忍且毫无良知。

e.en: The verdict troubled the jurors' {consciences} for years.
e.zh: 这个判决多年来一直困扰着陪审员们的良心。

e.en: Honest leaders listen to their own {consciences}.
e.zh: 诚实的领导者会聆听自己的良心。

conscientious.t: adj. 认真尽责的、一丝不苟的

e.en: She is a {conscientious} student who never misses deadlines.
e.zh: 她是个尽责的学生，从不错过截止日期。

e.en: Our team needs more {conscientious} code reviewers.
e.zh: 我们团队需要更多认真负责的代码审查员。

conscientiously.t: adv. 认真尽责地、一丝不苟地

e.en: He {conscientiously} replied to every customer email.
e.zh: 他认真地回复了每一封客户邮件。

e.en: She {conscientiously} backs up her files each night.
e.zh: 她每晚都尽心地备份文件。

conscientiousness.t: n. 尽职尽责、严谨认真

e.en: Her {conscientiousness} made her the team's most trusted member.
e.zh: 她的认真负责让她成了团队最值得信赖的成员。

e.en: Psychologists rank {conscientiousness} as a key personality trait.
e.zh: 心理学家将尽责性列为关键的人格特质。

conscious.t:
adj. 有意识的、察觉到的
adj. 刻意的

e.en: She is very {conscious} of her tone in meetings.
e.zh: 她在开会时非常注意自己的语气。

e.en: The patient remained {conscious} throughout the surgery.
e.zh: 病人在整个手术过程中保持清醒。

e.en: He {consciously} avoids checking his phone during dinner.
e.zh: 他在吃饭时刻意不看手机。

e.en: She {consciously} chose a simpler lifestyle.
e.zh: 她有意识地选择了更简单的生活方式。

e.en: He lost {consciousness} after hitting his head.
e.zh: 他撞到头之后失去了知觉。

e.en: The book raises {consciousness} about climate change.
e.zh: 这本书提高了人们对气候变化的意识。

e.en: Some philosophers debate whether multiple {consciousnesses} can share one brain.
e.zh: 一些哲学家在讨论多个意识能否共存于一个大脑中。

e.en: The novel imagines two {consciousnesses} merging into one.
e.zh: 这部小说设想两种意识融合为一体。

conscript.t:
v. 征召入伍
n. 应征士兵

e.en: The army may {conscript} young men during wartime.
e.zh: 战时军队可能会征召年轻男子入伍。

e.en: Every {conscript} received six weeks of basic training.
e.zh: 每名应征士兵都接受了六周的基础训练。

conscripted.t: v. 征召入伍（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: He was {conscripted} into the army at eighteen.
e.zh: 他十八岁时被征召入伍。

e.en: Volunteers were {conscripted} to help after the flood.
e.zh: 洪水过后志愿者被征调前来帮忙。

e.en: The country abolished military {conscription} a decade ago.
e.zh: 该国十年前废除了义务兵役制。

e.en: Mass {conscription} reshaped society during World War One.
e.zh: 大规模征兵在一战期间重塑了社会。

consecrate.t: v. 使神圣化；献给（宗教）

e.en: The bishop will {consecrate} the new church on Sunday.
e.zh: 主教将于周日祝圣这座新教堂。

e.en: She vowed to {consecrate} her career to medical research.
e.zh: 她发誓将自己的事业奉献给医学研究。

e.en: The chapel was {consecrated} in a quiet ceremony.
e.zh: 这座小教堂在一场低调的仪式中被祝圣。

e.en: He {consecrated} years to caring for his ailing mother.
e.zh: 他把多年时光献给了照顾生病的母亲。

e.en: The {consecration} of the cathedral drew thousands of visitors.
e.zh: 大教堂的祝圣仪式吸引了数千名访客。

e.en: Her {consecration} to the cause inspired everyone.
e.zh: 她对这项事业的奉献激励了每一个人。

consecutive.t: adj. 连续的、接连不断的

e.en: The team won five {consecutive} games this month.
e.zh: 这支球队本月赢得了五场连胜。

e.en: She worked twelve {consecutive} hours without a break.
e.zh: 她连续工作了十二小时没有休息。

e.en: The pages are numbered {consecutively} from one to fifty.
e.zh: 这些页码从一到五十连续编号。

e.en: He won the championship three years {consecutively}.
e.zh: 他连续三年蝉联冠军。

consensual.t: adj. 经双方同意的、合意的

e.en: All adult relationships should be fully {consensual}.
e.zh: 所有成人之间的关系都应建立在双方自愿的基础上。

e.en: The decision was reached through {consensual} discussion.
e.zh: 这一决定是通过双方协商达成的。

e.en: Data should only be collected {consensually} from users.
e.zh: 数据只应在用户同意的情况下收集。

e.en: The board {consensually} approved the new strategy.
e.zh: 董事会一致同意通过了新战略。

e.en: The team reached a {consensus} after hours of debate.
e.zh: 经过数小时的辩论，团队达成了共识。

e.en: There is scientific {consensus} that the climate is warming.
e.zh: 科学界一致认为气候正在变暖。

e.en: Different fields form their own expert {consensuses}.
e.zh: 不同领域会形成各自的专家共识。

e.en: Political {consensuses} rarely survive a change of government.
e.zh: 政治共识很少能在政府更迭后延续。

consent.t:
n. 同意、许可
v. 同意、答应

e.en: Doctors must obtain {consent} before any procedure.
e.zh: 医生在任何手术前必须取得同意。

e.en: Her parents would never {consent} to the marriage.
e.zh: 她的父母绝不会同意这桩婚事。

e.en: She {consented} to share her data with researchers.
e.zh: 她同意与研究人员分享自己的数据。

e.en: He {consented} to the meeting only after much persuasion.
e.zh: 经过反复劝说，他才同意参加会议。

consenting.t:
adj. 自愿同意的
v. 同意（现在分词）

e.en: The law applies only to {consenting} adults.
e.zh: 该法律只适用于自愿的成年人。

e.en: She nodded, {consenting} to the new terms.
e.zh: 她点头表示同意新的条款。

consents.t: n./v. 同意（consent 的第三人称/复数）

e.en: The app stores user {consents} for data processing.
e.zh: 该应用会保存用户的数据处理同意书。

e.en: She rarely {consents} to give media interviews.
e.zh: 她很少同意接受媒体采访。

e.en: Every action has a {consequence}, however small.
e.zh: 每个行为都会有后果，无论多小。

e.en: Skipping breakfast had no real {consequence} for her workday.
e.zh: 不吃早餐对她的工作日没什么实际影响。

e.en: He didn't fully understand the {consequences} of his decision.
e.zh: 他没有完全意识到自己决定的后果。

e.en: Climate change will bring serious long-term {consequences}.
e.zh: 气候变化将带来严重的长期后果。

consequent.t: adj. 随之而来的、作为结果的

e.en: Heavy rain and the {consequent} flooding closed the highway.
e.zh: 暴雨以及随之而来的洪水使高速公路关闭。

e.en: The merger and its {consequent} layoffs shocked employees.
e.zh: 合并以及随之而来的裁员震惊了员工。

consequential.t: adj. 重大的、有深远影响的

e.en: This was the most {consequential} election in decades.
e.zh: 这是几十年来最具影响力的一次选举。

e.en: Her early career choices proved deeply {consequential}.
e.zh: 她早期的职业选择被证明影响深远。

e.en: The road was icy; {consequently}, the bus was delayed.
e.zh: 路面结冰，因此公交车晚点了。

e.en: He skipped practice and {consequently} lost his starting spot.
e.zh: 他翘掉了训练，结果失去了首发位置。

conservancy.t: n. 自然保护组织；保育

e.en: The Nature {Conservancy} protects millions of acres worldwide.
e.zh: 大自然保护协会在全球保护着数百万英亩土地。

e.en: A local {conservancy} runs the wildlife reserve.
e.zh: 一家当地保护机构管理着这个野生动物保护区。

conservation.t: n. 环境保护；（能量）守恒

e.en: Wildlife {conservation} requires both funding and political will.
e.zh: 野生动物保护需要资金和政治意愿并重。

e.en: Energy {conservation} starts with simple daily habits.
e.zh: 节约能源要从日常的小习惯做起。

e.en: The {conservationist} spent decades protecting endangered tigers.
e.zh: 这位环保人士花了数十年保护濒危的老虎。

e.en: She became a passionate {conservationist} after visiting Borneo.
e.zh: 游览婆罗洲后她成为了一名热情的环保主义者。

e.en: Different regions follow distinct wildlife {conservations} strategies.
e.zh: 不同地区采取各自不同的野生动物保护策略。

e.en: Marine and forest {conservations} require very different approaches.
e.zh: 海洋保护与森林保护需要截然不同的方法。

conservatism.t: n. 保守主义、守旧思想

e.en: Fiscal {conservatism} dominated the party's economic policy.
e.zh: 财政保守主义主导了该党的经济政策。

e.en: Her cautious {conservatism} kept the company stable through downturns.
e.zh: 她审慎的保守作风让公司在低谷中保持稳定。

conservative.t:
adj. 保守的、传统的
n. 保守派人士

e.en: He takes a {conservative} approach to investing his savings.
e.zh: 他在投资储蓄方面采取保守的策略。

e.en: The {conservative} estimate puts the cost at two million.
e.zh: 保守估计这笔费用约为两百万。

e.en: She dresses {conservatively} for client meetings downtown.
e.zh: 她在与客户开会时穿着保守。

e.en: The team {conservatively} predicts ten percent growth next year.
e.zh: 团队保守预计明年增长百分之十。

e.en: Many {conservatives} oppose the proposed tax reform bill.
e.zh: 许多保守派反对这项税改提案。

e.en: Social {conservatives} gathered at the convention this weekend.
e.zh: 社会保守派本周末齐聚大会现场。

e.en: His political {conservativism} shaped decades of party policy.
e.zh: 他的政治保守主义影响了该党几十年的政策。

e.en: Fiscal {conservativism} dominated the budget debate this year.
e.zh: 财政保守主义主导了今年的预算辩论。

conservatoire.t: n. 音乐学院、艺术学院

e.en: She studied violin at the Paris {conservatoire} for six years.
e.zh: 她在巴黎音乐学院学了六年小提琴。

e.en: The {conservatoire} accepts only the most talented young musicians.
e.zh: 这所音乐学院只录取最有天赋的年轻乐手。

conservator.t: n. 文物修复师；管理员

e.en: The museum {conservator} carefully restored the damaged painting.
e.zh: 博物馆的修复师小心地修复了那幅受损画作。

e.en: A court-appointed {conservator} now manages her finances.
e.zh: 现在由法院指定的监管人打理她的财务。

conservatories.t: n. 温室；音乐学院（复数）

e.en: Several music {conservatories} offer scholarships to international students.
e.zh: 几所音乐学院为国际学生提供奖学金。

e.en: Victorian-era {conservatories} once housed exotic plants from abroad.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代的温室曾种植来自海外的奇异植物。

conservatory.t:
n. 玻璃温室、阳光房
n. 音乐学院

e.en: She practices piano daily at the {conservatory} downtown.
e.zh: 她每天在市中心的音乐学院练钢琴。

e.en: We had tea in the sunny glass {conservatory}.
e.zh: 我们在阳光明媚的玻璃花房里喝茶。

e.en: Please {conserve} water during the summer drought.
e.zh: 夏季干旱期间请节约用水。

e.en: Athletes {conserve} energy in the early laps of the race.
e.zh: 运动员在比赛前几圈会保存体力。

conserved.t: v. 节约、保护（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: The old library has been carefully {conserved} for future generations.
e.zh: 那座古老的图书馆为后代被精心保存了下来。

e.en: She {conserved} her phone battery during the long flight.
e.zh: 她在长途航班上节省着手机电量。

e.en: He's known as a careful {conserver} of household resources.
e.zh: 他以精打细算节约家庭资源著称。

e.en: The {conserver} of the estate protected its historic gardens.
e.zh: 庄园的守护者保护了那些历史悠久的花园。

e.en: This building design {conserves} energy through smart insulation.
e.zh: 这种建筑设计通过智能保温节约能源。

e.en: Grandma makes homemade strawberry {conserves} every summer.
e.zh: 奶奶每年夏天都会自制草莓果酱。

conserving.t: v. 保护；节约（现在分词）

e.en: The app helps users in {conserving} their mobile data.
e.zh: 这款应用帮助用户节省移动流量。

e.en: {Conserving} forests is critical for fighting climate change.
e.zh: 保护森林对应对气候变化至关重要。

e.en: He grew up in {Consett}, a small town in northern England.
e.zh: 他在英格兰北部的小镇康塞特长大。

e.en: The old steelworks at {Consett} closed decades ago.
e.zh: 康塞特的老钢铁厂几十年前就关闭了。

e.en: Please {consider} all the options before making a decision.
e.zh: 请在做决定前考虑所有选项。

e.en: Many {consider} her the best player on the team.
e.zh: 许多人认为她是队里最出色的球员。

considerable.t: adj. 相当大的；值得考虑的

e.en: The project required a {considerable} amount of time and money.
e.zh: 这个项目需要投入相当多的时间和金钱。

e.en: She has {considerable} experience in software engineering.
e.zh: 她在软件工程方面有丰富的经验。

e.en: Prices have risen {considerably} over the past year.
e.zh: 过去一年物价上涨了不少。

e.en: The new model is {considerably} faster than the previous one.
e.zh: 新款的速度比上一代快得多。

considerate.t: adj. 体贴的；为他人着想的

e.en: It was very {considerate} of you to bring an umbrella.
e.zh: 你能带把伞来真是太贴心了。

e.en: She's a {considerate} roommate who always cleans up.
e.zh: 她是个体贴的室友,总会主动打扫。

e.en: He spoke {considerately} to the upset customer on the phone.
e.zh: 他在电话里体贴地安抚了那位不满的顾客。

e.en: She {considerately} lowered her voice in the quiet library.
e.zh: 她在安静的图书馆里体贴地压低了声音。

e.en: After careful {consideration}, she accepted the job offer.
e.zh: 经过慎重考虑,她接受了这份工作。

e.en: Please show some {consideration} for your neighbors at night.
e.zh: 夜里请多体谅一下邻居。

e.en: Several {considerations} influenced our final design choice.
e.zh: 有几个因素影响了我们最终的设计选择。

e.en: Safety {considerations} must come before cost savings.
e.zh: 安全方面的考量必须优先于节省成本。

considered.t:
adj. 经过深思熟虑的
v. 考虑（过去式）

e.en: She {considered} moving abroad after graduation.
e.zh: 毕业后她考虑过出国发展。

e.en: His response was thoughtful and well {considered}.
e.zh: 他的回答经过深思熟虑,很周到。

considering.t:
prep. 考虑到
v. 考虑（现在分词）

e.en: I'm {considering} buying a new laptop next month.
e.zh: 我正在考虑下个月买台新笔记本电脑。

e.en: {Considering} the bad weather, the turnout was impressive.
e.zh: 考虑到天气恶劣,出席人数已经很可观了。

considers.t: v. 认为；考虑（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {considers} every angle before making big decisions.
e.zh: 她在做重大决定前会权衡方方面面。

e.en: The committee {considers} new applications every Monday.
e.zh: 委员会每周一审议新的申请。

e.en: The boss never made a move without his trusted {consigliere}.
e.zh: 老大没有他的心腹顾问从不轻举妄动。

e.en: In the film, the {consigliere} advises the family on legal matters.
e.zh: 电影中,这位军师为家族出谋划策处理法律事务。

e.en: She decided to {consign} her old furniture to the secondhand shop.
e.zh: 她决定把旧家具寄售到二手店。

e.en: Critics {consign} the album to the bargain bin of pop music.
e.zh: 评论家把这张专辑打入了流行音乐的廉价货堆。

e.en: The package was {consigned} to an overnight courier service.
e.zh: 包裹已交由隔夜快递公司寄送。

e.en: His early novels were {consigned} to obscurity for decades.
e.zh: 他的早期小说被遗忘了几十年。

e.en: The {consignee} must sign for the package upon delivery.
e.zh: 收货人必须在送达时签收包裹。

e.en: Customs delays affected the {consignee} waiting at the port.
e.zh: 海关延误影响了在港口等候的收货方。

consigning.t: v. 托运；委托（现在分词）

e.en: She's {consigning} her designer bags to an online resale site.
e.zh: 她正把名牌包寄卖到一个在线转售网站。

e.en: The verdict is {consigning} him to years behind bars.
e.zh: 这一判决将让他在牢里度过多年。

e.en: A large {consignment} of medical supplies arrived this morning.
e.zh: 今早抵达了一大批医疗物资。

e.en: She sells vintage clothes on {consignment} at a local shop.
e.zh: 她在当地一家小店里寄售复古服装。

e.en: The warehouse received three {consignments} of imported wine today.
e.zh: 仓库今天收到了三批进口葡萄酒。

e.en: Smaller {consignments} are easier to inspect at customs.
e.zh: 小批量货物在海关更容易查验。

e.en: The {consignor} ships the goods directly to our warehouse.
e.zh: 发货方将货物直接发送至我们的仓库。

e.en: Each {consignor} receives sixty percent of the final sale price.
e.zh: 每位寄售人可获得最终售价的百分之六十。

consigns.t: v. 托运（第三人称单数）

e.en: She regularly {consigns} unworn clothes to a thrift store.
e.zh: 她经常把没穿过的衣服寄卖到二手店。

e.en: History {consigns} forgotten leaders to a single footnote.
e.zh: 历史把被遗忘的领导人压缩成一条脚注。

e.en: The team will {consist} of five engineers and a designer.
e.zh: 团队将由五名工程师和一名设计师组成。

e.en: Healthy meals usually {consist} of vegetables, protein, and grains.
e.zh: 健康饮食通常由蔬菜、蛋白质和谷物组成。

e.en: Breakfast {consisted} of toast, eggs, and fresh coffee.
e.zh: 早餐有吐司、鸡蛋和新鲜咖啡。

e.en: The audience {consisted} mostly of college students.
e.zh: 观众大多是大学生。

e.en: The recipe calls for two different {consistencies} of cream.
e.zh: 这份食谱需要用到两种稠度不同的奶油。

e.en: Testing revealed minor {consistencies} between the two reports.
e.zh: 测试发现两份报告之间存在少量一致之处。

e.en: The batter should have the {consistency} of thick cream.
e.zh: 面糊的稠度应该像浓奶油一样。

e.en: {Consistency} in training is more important than intensity.
e.zh: 训练的持续性比强度更重要。

consistent.t: adj. 一致的；始终如一的

e.en: His performance has been {consistent} throughout the season.
e.zh: 他整个赛季的表现都很稳定。

e.en: The results are {consistent} with our earlier hypothesis.
e.zh: 结果与我们先前的假设相符。

consistently.t: adv. 一贯地；始终如一地

e.en: She {consistently} delivers her projects ahead of schedule.
e.zh: 她总是提前完成自己的项目。

e.en: The app {consistently} ranks among the top free downloads.
e.zh: 这款应用一直稳居免费下载榜前列。

e.en: We ordered a platter {consisting} of cheese, fruit, and bread.
e.zh: 我们点了一份由奶酪、水果和面包组成的拼盘。

e.en: A panel {consisting} of three judges reviewed each submission.
e.zh: 由三位评委组成的小组审阅了每份投稿。

consists.t: v. 由…组成（第三人称单数）

e.en: The course {consists} of ten online lessons and a final project.
e.zh: 该课程包含十节网课和一个期末项目。

e.en: Her diet mainly {consists} of vegetables and lean protein.
e.zh: 她的饮食主要由蔬菜和瘦肉蛋白组成。

e.en: Belgium uses a {consociational} system to balance ethnic communities.
e.zh: 比利时采用协合制来平衡各族裔群体。

e.en: Scholars debate whether {consociational} democracy works in deeply divided societies.
e.zh: 学者们就协合民主在严重分裂社会中是否奏效争论不休。

e.en: His grandfather invested heavily in British government {consol} bonds.
e.zh: 他祖父曾大量投资英国政府的统一公债。

e.en: The {consol} paid a fixed annual interest with no maturity date.
e.zh: 这种统一公债按年支付固定利息,没有到期日。

e.en: Her kind words brought him much-needed {consolation} after the loss.
e.zh: 她的暖心话语在他失去亲人后给了他莫大的安慰。

e.en: Losing the final was tough, but reaching it was some {consolation}.
e.zh: 输掉决赛很难受,但能闯进决赛多少是种慰藉。

e.en: Small {consolations} like coffee and music got her through the week.
e.zh: 咖啡和音乐这些小慰藉帮她熬过了这一周。

e.en: Friends offered warm {consolations} after the unexpected news.
e.zh: 朋友们在听到意外消息后给予了温暖的安慰。

console.t:
n. 控制台；游戏主机
v. 安慰

e.en: She tried to {console} her friend after the bad news.
e.zh: 听到坏消息后,她努力安慰朋友。

e.en: He plays games on his new gaming {console} every weekend.
e.zh: 他每个周末都用新游戏机打游戏。

e.en: The coach {consoled} the team after their narrow defeat.
e.zh: 教练在球队惜败后安慰了队员们。

e.en: She {consoled} herself with a warm cup of cocoa.
e.zh: 她用一杯暖暖的可可来安慰自己。

e.en: He became the family {consoler} during their darkest days.
e.zh: 在最艰难的日子里,他成了家中的精神支柱。

e.en: Music has always been her quiet {consoler} after long shifts.
e.zh: 长班结束后,音乐一直是她默默的慰藉者。

consoles.t:
n. 控制台（复数）
v. 安慰

e.en: The latest gaming {consoles} feature stunning 4K graphics.
e.zh: 最新款游戏机支持惊艳的 4K 画质。

e.en: She always {consoles} her younger brother when he cries.
e.zh: 弟弟哭的时候,她总会安慰他。

e.en: We need to {consolidate} our debts into one monthly payment.
e.zh: 我们需要把各项债务合并成每月一次还款。

e.en: The company plans to {consolidate} its three offices into one.
e.zh: 公司计划把三个办事处合并成一个。

e.en: The startup {consolidated} three offices into one headquarters.
e.zh: 这家初创公司将三个办公室合并为一个总部。

e.en: She read the {consolidated} report before the board meeting.
e.zh: 她在董事会会议前阅读了合并报告。

consolidates.t: v. 巩固；合并（第三人称单数）

e.en: This app {consolidates} all your bills into one screen.
e.zh: 这个应用把你所有的账单整合到一个界面。

e.en: The new policy {consolidates} power in the central office.
e.zh: 新政策将权力集中到了总部。

consolidating.t: v. 巩固；合并（现在分词）

e.en: The bank is {consolidating} its branches across the region.
e.zh: 该银行正在整合其在该地区的分行。

e.en: She is {consolidating} her notes before the final exam.
e.zh: 她正在期末考试前整理她的笔记。

e.en: The industry has seen massive {consolidation} over the past decade.
e.zh: 过去十年里,该行业经历了大规模的整合。

e.en: Memory {consolidation} during sleep helps you retain new information.
e.zh: 睡眠期间的记忆巩固有助于你保留新信息。

e.en: He works as a freight {consolidator} at the shipping port.
e.zh: 他在港口担任货运整合员。

e.en: The startup became a major {consolidator} in the cloud market.
e.zh: 这家初创公司成为云市场的主要整合者。

consoling.t:
adj. 安慰的
v. 安慰（现在分词）

e.en: She spent the evening {consoling} her heartbroken friend.
e.zh: 她整晚都在安慰她伤心的朋友。

e.en: His {consoling} words helped me get through the loss.
e.zh: 他安慰的话语帮我度过了那段失去亲人的时光。

e.en: She patted his shoulder {consolingly} after the bad news.
e.zh: 听到坏消息后,她安慰地拍了拍他的肩膀。

e.en: The teacher smiled {consolingly} at the disappointed student.
e.zh: 老师对失望的学生安慰地笑了笑。

e.en: The chef served a clear beef {consomme} as the first course.
e.zh: 主厨上了一道清炖牛肉清汤作为第一道菜。

e.en: A good {consomme} should be perfectly transparent and richly flavored.
e.zh: 一份好的清炖肉汤应当完全清澈且味道浓郁。

consonance.t: n. 协调；和谐；辅音押韵

e.en: His actions are in {consonance} with the company's values.
e.zh: 他的行为与公司的价值观一致。

e.en: The poem uses {consonance} to create a musical effect.
e.zh: 这首诗运用辅音押韵营造出音乐般的效果。

consonant.t:
n. 辅音
adj. 一致的

e.en: The letter B is a {consonant} in English.
e.zh: 字母B在英语中是一个辅音字母。

e.en: Her decision is {consonant} with our team's principles.
e.zh: 她的决定与我们团队的原则相符。

e.en: English has 21 {consonants} and 5 vowels.
e.zh: 英语有21个辅音字母和5个元音字母。

e.en: Toddlers often struggle to pronounce certain {consonants} clearly.
e.zh: 幼儿常常难以清晰地发出某些辅音。

constricted.t:
adj. 收缩的；狭窄的
v. 收紧（constrict 过去式）

e.en: Her throat felt {constricted} during the panic attack.
e.zh: 恐慌发作时她感觉喉咙发紧。

e.en: The narrow valley {constricted} the river's flow.
e.zh: 狭窄的山谷束缚了河水的流动。

constricting.t:
adj. 令人拘束的
v. 使收缩（现在分词）

e.en: He loosened the {constricting} tie around his neck.
e.zh: 他松开了脖子上勒得紧紧的领带。

e.en: She found the small town's expectations {constricting}.
e.zh: 她觉得这个小镇的期待让人感到压抑。

e.en: The doctor noticed a {constriction} in the patient's airway.
e.zh: 医生发现病人的气道有一处狭窄。

e.en: Budget {constriction} forced the team to cut features.
e.zh: 预算紧缩迫使团队删减了功能。

e.en: Avoid {constrictive} clothing during long flights.
e.zh: 长途飞行时避免穿过紧的衣物。

e.en: The new policies feel {constrictive} to many employees.
e.zh: 许多员工觉得新政策束缚感很强。

e.en: A boa {constrictor} can grow up to four meters long.
e.zh: 一条蟒蛇最长可以长到四米。

e.en: The snake is a powerful {constrictor} that crushes its prey.
e.zh: 这种蛇是会勒紧并压碎猎物的强力绞杀者。

e.en: Cold air can {constringe} the small blood vessels in the skin.
e.zh: 冷空气会使皮肤里的小血管收缩。

e.en: Astringent lotions {constringe} the pores after cleansing.
e.zh: 收敛性化妆水会在洁面后收紧毛孔。

construct.t:
v. 建造；构建
n. 概念；构造

e.en: Engineers will {construct} a new bridge across the river.
e.zh: 工程师们将在河上建造一座新桥。

e.en: Race is largely a social {construct}, not a biological fact.
e.zh: 种族在很大程度上是社会建构,而非生物学事实。

constructed.t:
adj. 建成的
v. 建造（过去式）

e.en: The company {constructed} its headquarters in just two years.
e.zh: 这家公司仅用两年就建成了总部大楼。

e.en: She carefully {constructed} an argument backed by data.
e.zh: 她精心构建了一个有数据支撑的论点。

constructing.t: v. 建造；构建（现在分词）

e.en: Workers are {constructing} a new subway line downtown.
e.zh: 工人们正在市中心修建一条新地铁线。

e.en: The author spent months {constructing} the novel's plot.
e.zh: 作者花了数月时间构思小说的情节。

e.en: The {construction} of the stadium will finish next spring.
e.zh: 体育场的建设将于明年春天完工。

e.en: Sentence {construction} matters a lot in formal writing.
e.zh: 句子结构在正式写作中非常重要。

e.en: The bridge failed due to {constructional} defects.
e.zh: 这座桥因施工缺陷而坍塌。

e.en: Linguists study {constructional} patterns across languages.
e.zh: 语言学家研究不同语言中的构式模式。

constructionist.t: n. 建构主义者；严格解释者

e.en: The judge takes a strict {constructionist} view of the law.
e.zh: 这位法官对法律持严格的字面解释立场。

e.en: A {constructionist} approach treats meaning as socially built.
e.zh: 建构主义方法把意义视为由社会塑造而成。

e.en: Ancient stone {constructions} still stand in the desert.
e.zh: 古老的石砌建筑至今仍矗立在沙漠中。

e.en: English uses several passive {constructions} in formal writing.
e.zh: 英语在正式写作中会使用多种被动结构。

e.en: She gave me {constructive} feedback on my draft.
e.zh: 她对我的草稿提出了建设性的反馈。

e.en: Let's keep the discussion {constructive} and respectful.
e.zh: 我们让讨论保持建设性和尊重。

e.en: Try to criticize his work {constructively} rather than harshly.
e.zh: 试着以建设性的方式而不是苛刻地批评他的作品。

e.en: The team handled the conflict {constructively} and moved on.
e.zh: 团队以建设性的方式处理了冲突,然后继续前进。

constructivism.t: n. 建构主义（艺术、哲学流派）

e.en: {Constructivism} argues that learners build their own understanding.
e.zh: 建构主义认为学习者会自己建构理解。

e.en: Russian {constructivism} influenced modern graphic design.
e.zh: 俄罗斯构成主义对现代平面设计产生了影响。

constructivist.t:
n. 建构主义者
adj. 建构主义的

e.en: Her teaching follows a {constructivist} approach to learning.
e.zh: 她的教学采用建构主义的学习方式。

e.en: The museum displayed {constructivist} paintings from the 1920s.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了二十年代的构成主义画作。

constructs.t:
n. 构念（复数）
v. 建造（三单）

e.en: Psychologists test theoretical {constructs} like motivation and trust.
e.zh: 心理学家会检验动机、信任等理论建构。

e.en: The team {constructs} prototypes within a single weekend.
e.zh: 该团队会在一个周末内搭建出原型。

e.en: Don't {construe} my silence as agreement with the plan.
e.zh: 不要把我的沉默理解为同意这个计划。

e.en: Courts must {construe} the statute according to its plain meaning.
e.zh: 法院必须按照法规的字面含义来解释它。

consubstantial.t: adj. 同质的；同体的（神学）

e.en: Christian doctrine teaches that the Son is {consubstantial} with the Father.
e.zh: 基督教教义认为圣子与圣父同质同体。

e.en: The two ideas are so close they feel almost {consubstantial}.
e.zh: 这两种观念如此接近,几乎可以说是同体的。

e.en: The Italian {consul} attended the trade fair in Shanghai.
e.zh: 意大利领事出席了在上海举行的贸易展。

e.en: Roman senators elected a new {consul} every year.
e.zh: 罗马元老院每年选出一位新的执政官。

e.en: Apply for a visa at the nearest {consular} office.
e.zh: 请到最近的领事办公室申请签证。

e.en: The embassy provides {consular} services to citizens abroad.
e.zh: 大使馆为海外公民提供领事服务。

e.en: I picked up my new passport at the Chinese {consulate}.
e.zh: 我在中国领事馆领取了新护照。

e.en: Protesters gathered outside the {consulate} all afternoon.
e.zh: 抗议者整个下午都聚集在领事馆外。

e.en: Please {consult} a doctor before changing your medication.
e.zh: 更改药物前请先咨询医生。

e.en: You can {consult} the user manual for setup instructions.
e.zh: 你可以查阅用户手册了解安装说明。

e.en: Big tech {consultancies} hire thousands of graduates each year.
e.zh: 大型科技咨询公司每年都会招聘成千上万的毕业生。

e.en: Boutique {consultancies} often specialize in one industry.
e.zh: 小型精品咨询公司通常只专注于某个行业。

consultancy.t: n. 咨询公司；咨询业务

e.en: She left her job to start a design {consultancy}.
e.zh: 她辞职创办了一家设计咨询公司。

e.en: The firm offers {consultancy} services to fintech startups.
e.zh: 该公司为金融科技初创企业提供咨询服务。

e.en: They hired a {consultant} to fix their messy supply chain.
e.zh: 他们聘请了一位顾问来整顿混乱的供应链。

e.en: As a freelance {consultant}, she sets her own hours.
e.zh: 作为独立顾问,她可以自己安排工作时间。

e.en: External {consultants} reviewed the company's security practices.
e.zh: 外部顾问审查了公司的安全实践。

e.en: Management {consultants} often travel four days a week.
e.zh: 管理顾问通常每周出差四天。

e.en: Book a free {consultation} with our financial advisor online.
e.zh: 在线预约一次与我们财务顾问的免费咨询。

e.en: The decision was made after {consultation} with the staff.
e.zh: 该决定是在与员工协商后做出的。

e.en: The clinic offers free 15-minute {consultations} on weekdays.
e.zh: 诊所工作日提供 15 分钟的免费咨询。

e.en: Public {consultations} on the new law begin next month.
e.zh: 关于新法律的公众咨询将于下个月开始。

e.en: The CEO prefers a {consultative} style of leadership.
e.zh: 这位 CEO 偏好协商式的领导风格。

e.en: The committee plays a {consultative} role, not a decisive one.
e.zh: 该委员会扮演的是咨询角色,而非决策角色。

e.en: She {consulted} a lawyer before signing the contract.
e.zh: 她在签合同前咨询了一位律师。

e.en: I {consulted} the docs and found the answer quickly.
e.zh: 我查阅了文档,很快就找到了答案。

consulting.t:
adj. 咨询的
n. 咨询业务

e.en: After college, he joined a {consulting} firm in New York.
e.zh: 大学毕业后,他加入了纽约的一家咨询公司。

e.en: She makes decisions without {consulting} her team first.
e.zh: 她做决定时从不先征求团队的意见。

e.en: He {consults} the dictionary whenever he meets a new word.
e.zh: 他每遇到生词都会查字典。

e.en: Our doctor {consults} at three different hospitals each week.
e.zh: 我们的医生每周在三家不同的医院出诊。

consumable.t:
adj. 可消费的
n. 消耗品

e.en: Printer ink is a {consumable} that needs frequent replacement.
e.zh: 打印机墨水是一种需要经常更换的耗材。

e.en: The blog turns research into easily {consumable} content.
e.zh: 这个博客把研究内容变成容易消化的形式。

e.en: Teenagers {consume} hours of short videos every day.
e.zh: 青少年每天会消耗大量时间看短视频。

e.en: Electric cars {consume} far less energy than gas cars.
e.zh: 电动车的能耗远低于燃油车。

e.en: She was {consumed} by anxiety before the big presentation.
e.zh: 重要演讲前她被焦虑吞没。

e.en: The fire {consumed} the entire warehouse within minutes.
e.zh: 大火在几分钟内吞噬了整个仓库。

e.en: The {consumer} confidence index dropped sharply last month.
e.zh: 消费者信心指数上个月大幅下滑。

e.en: This phone is aimed at the budget {consumer} market.
e.zh: 这款手机面向的是预算型消费市场。

e.en: Black Friday is often criticized as peak {consumerism}.
e.zh: 黑色星期五常被批评为消费主义的巅峰。

e.en: Some millennials are pushing back against rampant {consumerism}.
e.zh: 一些千禧一代正在抵制泛滥的消费主义。

consumerist.t:
adj. 消费主义的
n. 消费主义者

e.en: Modern cities reflect a deeply {consumerist} culture.
e.zh: 现代城市反映出一种根深蒂固的消费主义文化。

e.en: The film satirizes the {consumerist} lifestyle of suburbia.
e.zh: 这部电影讽刺了郊区那种消费至上的生活方式。

e.en: {Consumers} now expect free shipping on most online orders.
e.zh: 消费者现在期望大多数网购订单都能免运费。

e.en: Younger {consumers} care more about brand values than price.
e.zh: 年轻消费者更看重品牌价值而非价格。

e.en: The data center {consumes} as much power as a small city.
e.zh: 这座数据中心的耗电量相当于一座小城市。

e.en: Social media {consumes} too much of my evening.
e.zh: 社交媒体占用了我太多晚上的时间。

consuming.t:
adj. 强烈的；耗费的
v. 消耗（现在分词）

e.en: Editing the video was incredibly time-{consuming}.
e.zh: 剪辑这段视频极其耗时。

e.en: He spent the weekend {consuming} an entire TV series.
e.zh: 他整个周末都在追完一整部电视剧。

consummate.t:
adj. 完美的；技艺高超的
v. 完成；圆满达成

e.en: She is a {consummate} professional who never misses a deadline.
e.zh: 她是个完美的职业人士，从不错过截止日期。

e.en: The chef displayed {consummate} skill while preparing the meal.
e.zh: 那位厨师在准备餐点时展现了精湛的技艺。

e.en: The lawyer argued the case {consummately} before the jury.
e.zh: 那位律师在陪审团面前完美地陈述了案件。

e.en: She handled the difficult client {consummately} and calmly.
e.zh: 她极其娴熟而冷静地应对了那位棘手的客户。

e.en: The signed treaty marked the {consummation} of years of talks.
e.zh: 签署的条约标志着多年谈判的圆满完成。

e.en: Winning the award felt like the {consummation} of his career.
e.zh: 获奖让他感觉像是事业的巅峰成就。

e.en: The kiss was the {consummatory} act of their long courtship.
e.zh: 那个吻是他们漫长追求的完成性举动。

e.en: Eating is a {consummatory} behavior that follows the search for food.
e.zh: 进食是一种紧随觅食之后的完成性行为。

e.en: Coffee {consumption} has risen sharply among young workers.
e.zh: 年轻上班族的咖啡消费量大幅上升。

e.en: The app tracks your daily water {consumption} automatically.
e.zh: 这款应用会自动追踪你每天的饮水量。

e.en: The report compares energy {consumptions} across several countries.
e.zh: 这份报告比较了几个国家的能源消耗量。

e.en: Household water {consumptions} vary widely by region.
e.zh: 家庭用水量因地区不同差异很大。

e.en: Modern smartphones are highly {consumptive} of battery power.
e.zh: 现代智能手机非常耗电。

e.en: The novel features a {consumptive} poet dying of tuberculosis.
e.zh: 小说塑造了一位身患肺痨即将离世的诗人。

consort.t:
n. 配偶（尤指君主的）
v. 结交

e.en: The queen and her {consort} attended the state dinner.
e.zh: 女王和她的配偶出席了国宴。

e.en: He refuses to {consort} with people he doesn't trust.
e.zh: 他拒绝与不信任的人来往。

consortia.t: n. 联盟、财团（consortium 的复数）

e.en: Several research {consortia} are funding the climate project.
e.zh: 多个研究联盟正在为这个气候项目提供资金。

e.en: International {consortia} often share data across universities.
e.zh: 国际联盟通常在各大学之间共享数据。

e.en: A {consortium} of banks financed the massive infrastructure project.
e.zh: 由多家银行组成的财团为这项大型基础设施项目提供了资金。

e.en: The tech {consortium} agreed on a new industry standard.
e.zh: 该科技联盟就一项新的行业标准达成了一致。

conspecific.t:
adj. 同物种的
n. 同种生物

e.en: Wolves often cooperate when hunting with {conspecific} pack members.
e.zh: 狼在与同种群成员一起捕猎时常常会合作。

e.en: Birds use songs to communicate with {conspecific} individuals.
e.zh: 鸟类用鸣叫与同种个体进行交流。

e.en: The book offers a useful {conspectus} of modern philosophy.
e.zh: 这本书提供了一份有用的现代哲学概览。

e.en: Her thesis began with a {conspectus} of recent research.
e.zh: 她的论文以一份近期研究综述开篇。

conspicuous.t: adj. 显眼的、引人注目的

e.en: Her bright red coat made her {conspicuous} in the crowd.
e.zh: 她那件鲜红的外套让她在人群中格外显眼。

e.en: The CEO's absence at the meeting was {conspicuous}.
e.zh: 首席执行官缺席会议这件事十分显眼。

conspicuously.t: adv. 显眼地、惹人注目地

e.en: His name was {conspicuously} missing from the guest list.
e.zh: 他的名字在嘉宾名单上明显地缺席了。

e.en: She dressed {conspicuously} to attract attention at the party.
e.zh: 她在派对上穿着显眼以吸引注意。

e.en: Online {conspiracies} spread quickly across social media platforms.
e.zh: 网络阴谋论在各大社交媒体平台上迅速传播。

e.en: Historians uncovered several political {conspiracies} from the 1800s.
e.zh: 历史学家揭露了19世纪的几起政治阴谋。

e.en: The {conspiracy} to defraud investors lasted for several years.
e.zh: 这场欺骗投资者的阴谋持续了好几年。

e.en: He believes in a {conspiracy} theory about the moon landing.
e.zh: 他相信一个关于登月的阴谋论。

e.en: The lead {conspirator} was sentenced to fifteen years in prison.
e.zh: 主谋被判处十五年监禁。

e.en: Investigators identified a third {conspirator} in the bank robbery.
e.zh: 调查人员确定了银行抢劫案中的第三名同谋。

e.en: She gave him a {conspiratorial} wink across the dinner table.
e.zh: 她隔着餐桌向他使了个心照不宣的眼色。

e.en: The forum is full of {conspiratorial} posts about the election.
e.zh: 这个论坛上充斥着关于选举的阴谋论帖子。

conspiratorially.t: adv. 诡秘地、鬼鬼祟祟地

e.en: He whispered {conspiratorially} about the surprise birthday party.
e.zh: 他鬼鬼祟祟地小声谈论着那个惊喜生日派对。

e.en: The two friends grinned {conspiratorially} at each other.
e.zh: 两个朋友相视一笑,像是有什么秘密。

e.en: Several executives {conspire} to manipulate the stock price.
e.zh: 几名高管密谋操纵股票价格。

e.en: Bad weather and traffic seemed to {conspire} against my trip.
e.zh: 恶劣天气和交通状况似乎都在跟我的行程作对。

e.en: The village {constable} arrived to investigate the break-in.
e.zh: 村里的警员赶来调查这起入室盗窃案。

e.en: She was promoted from {constable} to detective last year.
e.zh: 她去年从警员晋升为侦探。

constabulary.t:
n. 警察部队
adj. 警察的

e.en: The local {constabulary} responded quickly to the emergency call.
e.zh: 当地警察部队迅速回应了紧急呼叫。

e.en: He served in the rural {constabulary} for thirty years.
e.zh: 他在乡村警队服役了三十年。

e.en: His {constancy} as a friend means everything to her.
e.zh: 他作为朋友的忠贞不渝对她意义重大。

e.en: The {constancy} of the temperature surprised the researchers.
e.zh: 温度的恒定令研究人员感到惊讶。

constant.t:
adj. 不断的、恒定的
n. 常数

e.en: My phone receives {constant} notifications throughout the day.
e.zh: 我的手机一整天都在不停地收到通知。

e.en: The speed of light is a physical {constant}.
e.zh: 光速是一个物理常数。

constantinople.t: n. 君士坦丁堡（今伊斯坦布尔）

e.en: {Constantinople} was the capital of the Byzantine Empire for centuries.
e.zh: 君士坦丁堡曾是拜占庭帝国数个世纪的首都。

e.en: The fall of {Constantinople} in 1453 changed European history.
e.zh: 1453年君士坦丁堡的陷落改变了欧洲的历史。

e.en: My little brother {constantly} interrupts me while I'm studying.
e.zh: 我学习的时候,我弟弟总是不停地打扰我。

e.en: Technology is {constantly} evolving in the smartphone industry.
e.zh: 智能手机行业的技术在不断发展。

constellation.t:
n. 星座
n. 一组、一系列

e.en: Orion is the easiest {constellation} to spot in winter.
e.zh: 猎户座是冬季最容易辨认的星座。

e.en: The app offers a {constellation} of features for content creators.
e.zh: 这款应用为内容创作者提供了一系列功能。

e.en: The sudden price hike caused {consternation} among loyal customers.
e.zh: 突然涨价让忠实顾客感到惊愕。

e.en: She stared at the broken vase in {consternation}.
e.zh: 她惊愕地盯着那只摔碎的花瓶。

e.en: The report listed the public's various {consternations} about the policy.
e.zh: 该报告列出了公众对这项政策的种种忧虑。

e.en: Daily {consternations} at work began to wear her down.
e.zh: 工作中每天的种种烦扰开始消磨她的精力。

e.en: Eating too much cheese can {constipate} young children.
e.zh: 吃太多奶酪会让小孩便秘。

e.en: Certain medications {constipate} patients as a side effect.
e.zh: 某些药物的副作用是让患者便秘。

e.en: Drinking more water helps if you feel {constipated}.
e.zh: 如果你感觉便秘,多喝水会有帮助。

e.en: The toddler was {constipated} after switching to solid foods.
e.zh: 幼儿在改吃固体食物后出现了便秘。

e.en: A high-fiber diet can help relieve chronic {constipation}.
e.zh: 高纤维饮食有助于缓解慢性便秘。

e.en: The doctor prescribed medication for her persistent {constipation}.
e.zh: 医生为她持续的便秘开了药。

constituencies.t: n. 选区、支持者群体（复数）

e.en: Politicians must balance the needs of different {constituencies}.
e.zh: 政客必须平衡不同选区的需求。

e.en: The brand appeals to several distinct customer {constituencies}.
e.zh: 该品牌吸引了几个不同的客户群体。

constituency.t:
n. 选区
n. 支持者群体

e.en: She represents a rural {constituency} in northern England.
e.zh: 她代表英格兰北部的一个农村选区。

e.en: The product has built a loyal {constituency} of young users.
e.zh: 该产品建立起了一批忠实的年轻用户群体。

constituent.t:
n. 组成部分、选民
adj. 构成的

e.en: Each {constituent} of the recipe matters to the final taste.
e.zh: 配方中的每一种成分都关系到最终的味道。

e.en: A {constituent} called the senator about the new bill.
e.zh: 一位选民就这项新法案打电话给参议员。

e.en: Women {constitute} nearly half of the company's workforce.
e.zh: 女性占公司员工总数的近一半。

e.en: These actions {constitute} a serious breach of contract.
e.zh: 这些行为构成了严重的违约。

e.en: The committee was {constituted} to review the new proposal.
e.zh: 委员会的成立是为了审查这项新提案。

e.en: His comments {constituted} a clear violation of company policy.
e.zh: 他的言论明显违反了公司的政策。

constitutes.t: v. 构成（constitute 第三人称单数）

e.en: Reading every day {constitutes} an important part of her routine.
e.zh: 每天阅读是她日常生活中重要的一部分。

e.en: What exactly {constitutes} cheating in this online game?
e.zh: 在这款网络游戏中,究竟什么算作作弊?

constituting.t: v. 构成（constitute 现在分词）

e.en: The students {constituting} the debate team trained every weekend.
e.zh: 组成辩论队的学生们每个周末都进行训练。

e.en: Plastic waste {constituting} the bulk of ocean pollution alarms scientists.
e.zh: 塑料垃圾占据海洋污染的大部分,这令科学家们感到震惊。

constitution.t:
n. 宪法
n. 体质、构成

e.en: The country's {constitution} guarantees freedom of speech to all citizens.
e.zh: 该国宪法保障所有公民的言论自由。

e.en: She has a strong {constitution} and rarely gets sick.
e.zh: 她体质很好,很少生病。

e.en: The Supreme Court ruled the new law was {constitutional}.
e.zh: 最高法院裁定这项新法律符合宪法。

e.en: Grandpa takes a {constitutional} walk every morning after breakfast.
e.zh: 爷爷每天早餐后都会出去散步锻炼身体。

e.en: American {constitutionalism} relies on a balance of three branches.
e.zh: 美国宪政依赖于三权分立的平衡。

e.en: The professor specializes in comparative {constitutionalism} across democracies.
e.zh: 这位教授专攻各民主国家的比较宪政研究。

e.en: The judge is known as a strict {constitutionalist} on legal matters.
e.zh: 这位法官以在法律问题上严格遵循宪法而闻名。

e.en: As a {constitutionalist}, she opposes any expansion of executive power.
e.zh: 作为一名宪政主义者,她反对任何行政权力的扩张。

e.en: The court will decide the {constitutionality} of the new immigration law.
e.zh: 法院将就这项新移民法是否合宪作出裁决。

e.en: Critics questioned the {constitutionality} of the president's executive order.
e.zh: 批评人士质疑总统行政命令的合宪性。

e.en: Citizens are {constitutionally} entitled to a fair trial.
e.zh: 公民享有宪法赋予的公正审判权。

e.en: He is {constitutionally} unable to sit still for long.
e.zh: 他天生就坐不住,无法长时间安静下来。

e.en: Many countries have rewritten their {constitutions} since the war.
e.zh: 自战争以来,许多国家已重写了他们的宪法。

e.en: Athletes with strong {constitutions} recover faster from intense training.
e.zh: 体质强健的运动员能更快地从高强度训练中恢复。

e.en: Trust is a {constitutive} element of any healthy relationship.
e.zh: 信任是任何健康关系的基本要素。

e.en: The court reviewed the {constitutive} rules of the organization.
e.zh: 法院审查了该组织的构成性规则。

e.en: Tight budgets {constrain} what the team can build this quarter.
e.zh: 紧张的预算限制了团队本季度能开发的内容。

e.en: Don't let fear {constrain} your career choices.
e.zh: 别让恐惧束缚你的职业选择。

e.en: Designers feel {constrained} by the strict brand guidelines.
e.zh: 设计师们觉得被严格的品牌规范所束缚。

e.en: The startup operated under {constrained} resources for years.
e.zh: 这家初创公司多年来在资源紧张下运营。

constraining.t:
v. 限制（constrain 现在分词）
adj. 约束性的

e.en: Legacy code can be surprisingly {constraining} for new features.
e.zh: 遗留代码对新功能的限制可能出乎意料地大。

e.en: She found the dress code overly {constraining} at work.
e.zh: 她觉得工作时的着装规定过于拘束。

e.en: Time is the biggest {constraint} on this project.
e.zh: 时间是这个项目最大的限制因素。

e.en: Add a unique {constraint} to prevent duplicate emails.
e.zh: 添加唯一性约束以防止邮箱重复。

constraints.t: n. 约束、限制条件（复数）

e.en: The engineers worked within tight memory {constraints}.
e.zh: 工程师们在严格的内存限制下工作。

e.en: Family {constraints} kept her from traveling abroad.
e.zh: 家庭的牵绊让她无法出国旅行。

e.en: Tight collars can {constrict} blood flow to the head.
e.zh: 过紧的衣领会阻碍血液流向头部。

e.en: New regulations may {constrict} small business growth.
e.zh: 新法规可能会抑制小企业的发展。

e.en: The baby slept {contentedly} in her mother's arms.
e.zh: 宝宝在妈妈怀里安然地睡着了。

e.en: He sipped his coffee {contentedly} on the balcony.
e.zh: 他在阳台上惬意地啜着咖啡。

e.en: Her main {contention} is that remote work boosts productivity.
e.zh: 她的主要观点是远程办公能提升效率。

e.en: Pay raises remain a source of {contention} between staff and management.
e.zh: 加薪仍是员工与管理层之间的争议焦点。

e.en: The lawyer dismissed the witness's {contentions} as baseless.
e.zh: 律师驳斥证人的说法毫无根据。

e.en: His {contentions} about climate policy sparked heated debate.
e.zh: 他对气候政策的论点引发了激烈讨论。

contentious.t: adj. 有争议的；好争论的

e.en: Immigration remains a {contentious} issue in many countries.
e.zh: 移民在许多国家仍是一个有争议的议题。

e.en: The meeting turned {contentious} when budgets came up.
e.zh: 讨论到预算时,会议变得火药味十足。

e.en: The {contentiousness} of the debate surprised the moderator.
e.zh: 辩论的激烈程度让主持人都感到意外。

e.en: His {contentiousness} made teamwork nearly impossible.
e.zh: 他的好斗让团队合作几乎无法进行。

e.en: The politician's speech was polished but largely {contentless}.
e.zh: 那位政客的演讲很漂亮,却基本没有实质内容。

e.en: Avoid posting {contentless} updates just to fill the feed.
e.zh: 不要为了刷屏而发空洞无物的动态。

e.en: Gardening brings her a deep sense of {contentment}.
e.zh: 园艺给她带来一种深深的满足感。

e.en: He sighed with {contentment} after the home-cooked meal.
e.zh: 吃完家常饭,他满足地叹了口气。

e.en: Please check the {contents} of the package upon delivery.
e.zh: 请在收货时核对包裹里的物品。

e.en: The table of {contents} lists every chapter clearly.
e.zh: 目录清楚地列出了每一章。

e.en: The park is {conterminous} with the national forest to the north.
e.zh: 该公园与北面的国家森林边界相接。

e.en: The map covers the {conterminous} United States only.
e.zh: 这张地图只涵盖美国本土相邻的各州。

e.en: The Italian {contessa} hosted a glamorous dinner at her villa.
e.zh: 那位意大利伯爵夫人在别墅里举办了豪华晚宴。

e.en: She played a mysterious {contessa} in the period drama.
e.zh: 她在那部年代剧里饰演一位神秘的伯爵夫人。

contest.t:
n. 比赛
v. 争夺；质疑

e.en: She won first prize in the photography {contest}.
e.zh: 她在摄影比赛中获得了一等奖。

e.en: The lawyers plan to {contest} the verdict in court.
e.zh: 律师们打算在法庭上对判决提出异议。

contestable.t: adj. 可争议的；可竞争的

e.en: The election results are {contestable} under current law.
e.zh: 根据现行法律,选举结果可以被提出异议。

e.en: His claim to ownership is highly {contestable}.
e.zh: 他的所有权主张大有争议余地。

e.en: Each {contestant} had ninety seconds to answer the question.
e.zh: 每位参赛者有九十秒时间回答问题。

e.en: The youngest {contestant} surprised everyone by winning.
e.zh: 最年轻的参赛者夺冠,让大家都惊讶。

e.en: The new border has been a site of constant {contestation}.
e.zh: 这条新边界一直是争议不断的地方。

e.en: His ideas about justice invite serious {contestation}.
e.zh: 他关于正义的看法引发了激烈的争论。

contested.t:
adj. 有争议的
v. 争夺（过去式）

e.en: The election was {contested} in three swing states.
e.zh: 选举在三个摇摆州遭到了挑战。

e.en: This is a hotly {contested} seat in parliament.
e.zh: 这是议会中一个竞争激烈的席位。

e.en: She is {contesting} the fine she received last week.
e.zh: 她正在对上周收到的罚单提出申诉。

e.en: Two siblings are {contesting} the will in court.
e.zh: 两兄妹正在法庭上争夺遗嘱继承权。

contests.t:
n. 比赛（复数）
v. 争夺

e.en: The website hosts weekly coding {contests} for students.
e.zh: 该网站每周为学生举办编程比赛。

e.en: He {contests} every parking ticket he gets.
e.zh: 他每张违停罚单都要去申诉。

e.en: The quote makes more sense when read in {context}.
e.zh: 结合上下文来看,这句话就好理解多了。

e.en: You need to understand the historical {context} of the war.
e.zh: 你需要了解这场战争的历史背景。

e.en: The same word can mean different things in different {contexts}.
e.zh: 同一个词在不同语境里意思可能不同。

e.en: The model performs poorly in low-resource {contexts}.
e.zh: 该模型在资源匮乏的场景下表现欠佳。

contextual.t: adj. 上下文的；与语境相关的

e.en: The app provides {contextual} hints based on what you're typing.
e.zh: 这个应用会根据你输入的内容给出情境化提示。

e.en: Translation requires {contextual} understanding, not just vocabulary.
e.zh: 翻译需要语境理解,不只是词汇。

contextualise.t: v. 将…置于语境中（英式拼写）

e.en: The teacher tried to {contextualise} the formula with real examples.
e.zh: 老师试图用实际例子来给这个公式建立语境。

e.en: We need to {contextualise} these results within the broader study.
e.zh: 我们需要把这些结果放在更大的研究背景下来看。

contextualization.t: n. 语境化；结合上下文

e.en: Proper {contextualization} helps readers grasp the article's purpose.
e.zh: 恰当的背景说明能帮助读者把握文章主旨。

e.en: The exhibit lacks {contextualization} of the artifacts' origins.
e.zh: 展览缺乏对文物来源的背景介绍。

e.en: Good journalists {contextualize} statistics so readers understand them.
e.zh: 优秀的记者会为数据提供背景,让读者看得懂。

e.en: Let me {contextualize} this decision with some company history.
e.zh: 让我结合公司一些历史来说明这个决定。

contextualized.t:
adj. 结合语境的
v. 语境化（过去式）

e.en: The professor {contextualized} the poem within Victorian society.
e.zh: 教授把这首诗放在维多利亚时代的社会背景中讲解。

e.en: Modern AI uses {contextualized} word embeddings for better accuracy.
e.zh: 现代人工智能使用上下文相关的词向量以提升准确率。

e.en: The chatbot responds {contextually} based on previous messages.
e.zh: 这个聊天机器人会根据上文做出符合语境的回复。

e.en: That joke only works {contextually} among close friends.
e.zh: 那个笑话只有在熟朋友之间才听得懂。

contig.t: n. 重叠群（基因组测序片段）

e.en: Each {contig} represents a continuous stretch of assembled DNA.
e.zh: 每个重叠群代表一段拼接好的连续 DNA 序列。

e.en: The genome assembler merged thousands of short reads into one {contig}.
e.zh: 基因组拼接程序把数千条短读段合并成一个重叠群。

e.en: The {contiguity} of the two parks makes hiking easy.
e.zh: 两个公园相邻,徒步起来很方便。

e.en: Memory {contiguity} can significantly improve cache performance.
e.zh: 内存连续性可以显著提升缓存性能。

e.en: The states are {contiguous}, sharing a long river border.
e.zh: 这两个州相邻,隔着一条长长的河。

e.en: Allocate a {contiguous} block of memory for the array.
e.zh: 为这个数组分配一块连续的内存。

e.en: The exercises help patients regain bladder {continence} after surgery.
e.zh: 这些练习帮助患者在术后恢复对膀胱的控制力。

e.en: The monks practiced {continence} as part of their vows.
e.zh: 僧侣们将节制作为戒律的一部分来修行。

e.en: Africa is the second-largest {continent} on Earth.
e.zh: 非洲是地球上第二大洲。

e.en: She backpacked across the {continent} for six months.
e.zh: 她背包穿越整个大陆走了六个月。

continental.t: adj. 大陆的；欧洲大陆的

e.en: We had a light {continental} breakfast at the hotel.
e.zh: 我们在酒店吃了一份简单的欧陆式早餐。

e.en: The storm swept across the entire {continental} United States.
e.zh: 风暴横扫了整个美国本土。

e.en: She has now traveled to all seven {continents}.
e.zh: 她现在已经走遍七大洲了。

e.en: Tectonic plates slowly push the {continents} apart over time.
e.zh: 地壳板块随着时间慢慢把各大洲推开。

contingency.t: n. 意外情况；应急事件

e.en: Every good project plan includes a {contingency} for delays.
e.zh: 好的项目计划都会为延误留一手应急方案。

e.en: We set aside funds as a {contingency} for emergencies.
e.zh: 我们留出一笔钱作为应急储备金。

contingent.t:
adj. 视情况而定的
n. 分遣队

e.en: The bonus is {contingent} on hitting our quarterly targets.
e.zh: 奖金的发放取决于能否完成季度目标。

e.en: A small {contingent} of fans waited outside the stadium.
e.zh: 一小批粉丝在体育场外等候。

e.en: The contract is {contingently} valid until both parties sign.
e.zh: 合同在双方签字前只是有条件地生效。

e.en: Funds are released {contingently}, based on milestone reviews.
e.zh: 资金会在里程碑审核通过后有条件地拨付。

continua.t: n. 连续体（continuum 的复数）

e.en: Researchers describe several {continua} of human behavior, not strict categories.
e.zh: 研究者用若干连续谱来描述人类行为,而非严格分类。

e.en: Color and pitch both lie on perceptual {continua}.
e.zh: 颜色和音高都属于感知上的连续体。

e.en: His {continual} interruptions made the meeting drag on.
e.zh: 他不停地打断让会议拖得很长。

e.en: The software receives {continual} updates from the developers.
e.zh: 这款软件会从开发者那里持续收到更新。

e.en: She's {continually} checking her phone for new messages.
e.zh: 她不停地刷手机看有没有新消息。

e.en: The team {continually} improves the product based on feedback.
e.zh: 团队根据反馈不断改进产品。

e.en: The judge granted a {continuance} until next month.
e.zh: 法官批准把案件延期到下个月审理。

e.en: The {continuance} of this program depends on funding.
e.zh: 这个项目能否继续要看资金情况。

e.en: The film is a direct {continuation} of the previous story.
e.zh: 这部电影是前作故事的直接延续。

e.en: We hope for the {continuation} of peace talks next week.
e.zh: 我们希望下周和谈能够继续进行。

e.en: Press any key to {continue} installing the application.
e.zh: 按任意键继续安装该应用程序。

e.en: Doctors advised her to {continue} the treatment for another month.
e.zh: 医生建议她再继续治疗一个月。

continued.t:
adj. 持续的
v. 继续（过去式）

e.en: Heavy rain {continued} throughout the weekend without a break.
e.zh: 整个周末大雨一直下个不停。

e.en: Thank you for your {continued} support of our channel.
e.zh: 感谢你一直以来对我们频道的支持。

continues.t: v. 继续（第三人称单数）

e.en: The series {continues} next Tuesday at eight.
e.zh: 这部剧将在下周二晚八点继续播出。

e.en: Demand for electric cars {continues} to grow rapidly.
e.zh: 电动汽车的需求仍在快速增长。

e.en: She is {continuing} her studies at a graduate school abroad.
e.zh: 她正在国外的研究生院继续学业。

e.en: Despite the rain, the team kept {continuing} the match.
e.zh: 尽管下雨,球队仍坚持继续比赛。

e.en: The film has several {continuities} between scenes that fans noticed.
e.zh: 影迷们注意到电影场景之间有几处连贯性细节。

e.en: Historians study the {continuities} linking ancient and modern cultures.
e.zh: 历史学家研究连接古今文化的种种延续性。

e.en: The new manager ensures {continuity} during the company restructuring.
e.zh: 新经理确保公司重组期间业务的连续性。

e.en: There's a {continuity} error where the actor's cup disappears.
e.zh: 有个穿帮镜头,演员手里的杯子突然不见了。

e.en: The harpsichord plays the {continuo} part throughout the baroque concerto.
e.zh: 羽管键琴在整首巴洛克协奏曲中担任通奏低音。

e.en: A skilled {continuo} player improvises chords from a bass line.
e.zh: 熟练的通奏低音演奏者会根据低音线即兴配和弦。

e.en: The app provides {continuous} updates on your delivery status.
e.zh: 这款应用持续更新你的配送状态。

e.en: She suffered {continuous} headaches for nearly two weeks.
e.zh: 她连续头痛了将近两周。

e.en: The server has been running {continuously} for over a year.
e.zh: 这台服务器已经不间断运行了一年多。

e.en: He talked {continuously} during the entire flight to Tokyo.
e.zh: 飞往东京的整个航程他一直说个不停。

e.en: Gender exists on a {continuum} rather than as fixed categories.
e.zh: 性别是一个连续谱,而非固定的类别。

e.en: Space and time form a single {continuum} in physics.
e.zh: 在物理学中,空间和时间构成一个统一的连续体。

e.en: Pain made her face {contort} into a grimace.
e.zh: 疼痛让她的脸扭曲成痛苦的表情。

e.en: Yoga teachers can {contort} their bodies into amazing shapes.
e.zh: 瑜伽老师能把身体扭成各种惊人的姿势。

e.en: His face {contorted} in agony as the medic arrived.
e.zh: 医护人员到达时,他的脸因剧痛而扭曲。

e.en: The crash left the metal frame badly {contorted}.
e.zh: 撞击让金属车架严重变形。

e.en: The dancer's final {contortion} drew gasps from the audience.
e.zh: 舞者最后一个扭体动作引得观众惊叹。

e.en: His logical {contortion} failed to convince anyone in the room.
e.zh: 他那番牵强的逻辑没能说服在场任何人。

e.en: The circus {contortionist} folded herself into a tiny glass box.
e.zh: 马戏团的柔术演员把自己折叠进一个小玻璃箱里。

e.en: You'd need to be a {contortionist} to fit in this seat.
e.zh: 想坐进这个座位你得是柔术演员才行。

contour.t:
n. 轮廓；外形
v. 勾勒轮廓

e.en: The map shows every {contour} of the mountain range.
e.zh: 这张地图显示了山脉的每一条等高线。

e.en: She traced the {contour} of his jaw with her finger.
e.zh: 她用手指描摹着他下颌的轮廓。

contoured.t: adj. 有轮廓的；贴合形状的

e.en: The chair has a {contoured} back for lumbar support.
e.zh: 这把椅子的椅背做了贴合腰部的曲线设计。

e.en: She {contoured} her cheeks with bronzer before the photo shoot.
e.zh: 拍照前她用古铜粉在脸颊上修了容。

e.en: The lawyer presented arguments both pro and {contra} the proposal.
e.zh: 律师提出了支持和反对该提案的双方论点。

e.en: His latest paper runs {contra} to mainstream economic theory.
e.zh: 他最近的论文与主流经济学理论相悖。

e.en: Customs officers seized the {contraband} cigarettes at the border.
e.zh: 海关人员在边境扣押了走私香烟。

e.en: Smartphones are considered {contraband} in most maximum-security prisons.
e.zh: 在大多数高度戒备监狱里,智能手机属于违禁品。

e.en: The clinic offers free {contraception} to all university students.
e.zh: 该诊所为所有大学生免费提供避孕用品。

e.en: Modern {contraception} has transformed women's reproductive choices worldwide.
e.zh: 现代避孕方法改变了全球女性的生育选择。

contraceptive.t:
n. 避孕药具
adj. 避孕的

e.en: She switched to a different {contraceptive} pill last month.
e.zh: 她上个月换了另一种避孕药。

e.en: Doctors recommend using {contraceptive} methods to prevent unwanted pregnancies.
e.zh: 医生建议使用避孕方法以防意外怀孕。

contract.t:
n. 合同；契约
v. 签合同；收缩

e.en: Please read the {contract} carefully before signing anything.
e.zh: 签字之前请仔细阅读合同。

e.en: Metals {contract} when temperatures drop below freezing.
e.zh: 温度降至冰点以下时金属会收缩。

e.en: She {contracted} a freelancer to redesign the company website.
e.zh: 她聘请了一位自由职业者重新设计公司网站。

e.en: He {contracted} a rare virus while traveling through the rainforest.
e.zh: 他在穿越雨林时感染了一种罕见病毒。

e.en: Heart muscle has unique {contractile} properties that pump blood continuously.
e.zh: 心肌具有独特的收缩特性,能持续泵送血液。

e.en: The amoeba has a {contractile} vacuole that expels excess water.
e.zh: 变形虫有一个伸缩泡用来排出多余水分。

e.en: Caffeine can increase the {contractility} of cardiac muscle fibers.
e.zh: 咖啡因可以增强心肌纤维的收缩力。

e.en: Doctors measured the {contractility} of his heart after surgery.
e.zh: 医生在术后测量了他的心脏收缩能力。

contracting.t: v. 签约；收缩（现在分词）

e.en: The pupils are {contracting} in response to the bright light.
e.zh: 瞳孔正在因强光而收缩。

e.en: The startup is {contracting} with several major retailers this quarter.
e.zh: 这家初创公司本季度正在与几家大型零售商签约合作。

e.en: "Don't" is a {contraction} of "do not" in English.
e.zh: 英语里 don't 是 do not 的缩写形式。

e.en: Each {contraction} brought her closer to giving birth.
e.zh: 每一次宫缩都让她更接近分娩。

e.en: The central bank adopted {contractionary} policy to fight rising inflation.
e.zh: 央行采取紧缩性政策以对抗不断上升的通胀。

e.en: Higher interest rates have a {contractionary} effect on the economy.
e.zh: 较高的利率对经济有紧缩作用。

e.en: We hired a {contractor} to remodel the kitchen this spring.
e.zh: 我们今年春天请了一位承包商来翻修厨房。

e.en: She works as an independent {contractor} for several tech companies.
e.zh: 她以独立承包商的身份为几家科技公司工作。

e.en: Three {contractors} submitted bids for the school renovation project.
e.zh: 三家承包商对学校翻新项目提交了投标。

e.en: Many software companies rely on overseas {contractors} for development work.
e.zh: 许多软件公司依靠海外承包商完成开发工作。

contracts.t:
n. 合同（复数）
v. 签约；收缩

e.en: The legal team reviews all {contracts} before the CEO signs them.
e.zh: 法务团队在CEO签字前会审阅所有合同。

e.en: Wood naturally {contracts} and expands with seasonal humidity changes.
e.zh: 木材会随季节湿度变化自然地收缩和膨胀。

e.en: He has a {contractual} obligation to finish the project by June.
e.zh: 他有合同义务在六月前完成项目。

e.en: Breaking a {contractual} agreement can result in heavy financial penalties.
e.zh: 违反合同协议可能导致严厉的经济处罚。

contractually.t: adv. 按合同地；契约上地

e.en: The actor is {contractually} bound to promote the film internationally.
e.zh: 该演员根据合同有义务为这部电影做国际宣传。

e.en: Employees are {contractually} required to give two weeks' notice.
e.zh: 员工按合同规定需提前两周告知离职。

e.en: After the burn healed, she developed a {contracture} in her wrist.
e.zh: 烧伤痊愈后,她的手腕出现了挛缩。

e.en: Physical therapy can prevent {contracture} in immobilized joints.
e.zh: 物理治疗可以防止固定关节出现挛缩。

e.en: The witness's statement seems to {contradict} the official police report.
e.zh: 证人的陈述似乎与警方的正式报告相矛盾。

e.en: Don't {contradict} your manager publicly during team meetings.
e.zh: 不要在团队会议上公开反驳你的经理。

e.en: The new evidence {contradicted} everything the prosecution had argued.
e.zh: 新证据推翻了控方此前的所有主张。

e.en: She {contradicted} her own claim within minutes of making it.
e.zh: 她说完那番话没几分钟就自相矛盾了。

contradicting.t: v. 反驳；相矛盾（现在分词）

e.en: He kept {contradicting} himself throughout the entire job interview.
e.zh: 他在整场面试中不断自相矛盾。

e.en: The two reports are clearly {contradicting} each other on key facts.
e.zh: 两份报告在关键事实上明显相互矛盾。

e.en: There's a clear {contradiction} between his words and his actions.
e.zh: 他的言行之间存在明显的矛盾。

e.en: Saying you're vegan while eating cheese is a {contradiction}.
e.zh: 自称纯素食者却吃奶酪本身就是矛盾。

e.en: The investigators found numerous {contradictions} in his alibi.
e.zh: 调查人员在他的不在场证明中发现了大量矛盾之处。

e.en: Life is full of small {contradictions} we learn to accept.
e.zh: 生活充满了我们渐渐学会接受的小矛盾。

e.en: The two studies produced {contradictory} results about coffee's health effects.
e.zh: 两项研究关于咖啡健康影响的结果相互矛盾。

e.en: She received {contradictory} advice from her doctor and her trainer.
e.zh: 她从医生和教练那里得到了相互矛盾的建议。

e.en: This data {contradicts} the company's claim of record profits.
e.zh: 这些数据与公司声称创纪录利润的说法相矛盾。

e.en: Her latest tweet {contradicts} what she said on the podcast.
e.zh: 她最新的推文与她在播客里说的话自相矛盾。

e.en: In {contradistinction} to her sister, Maya prefers quiet evenings at home.
e.zh: 与她姐姐截然不同,玛雅喜欢在家中度过安静的夜晚。

e.en: The author defines art in {contradistinction} to mere craft.
e.zh: 作者将艺术与单纯的工艺进行对比来下定义。

contraflow.t: n. 逆向车道；对向通行

e.en: Drivers faced a long {contraflow} system due to bridge repairs.
e.zh: 由于桥梁维修,司机们遇到了一段很长的对向通行路段。

e.en: The motorway introduced a {contraflow} lane during the morning rush.
e.zh: 高速公路在早高峰时段启用了反向车道。

e.en: A long white {contrail} stretched across the clear blue sky.
e.zh: 一道长长的白色尾迹划过晴朗的蓝天。

e.en: The jet's {contrail} slowly faded into wispy clouds above us.
e.zh: 喷气机的航迹云在我们头顶慢慢散成稀薄的云絮。

e.en: Pregnancy may {contraindicate} the use of this particular medication.
e.zh: 怀孕可能是使用这种特定药物的禁忌。

e.en: Doctors {contraindicate} aspirin for children under twelve years old.
e.zh: 医生不建议十二岁以下儿童服用阿司匹林。

e.en: Liver disease is a {contraindication} for taking this antibiotic.
e.zh: 肝病是服用这种抗生素的禁忌症。

e.en: Always check the label for any {contraindication} before taking medicine.
e.zh: 服药前请务必查看标签上的禁忌信息。

e.en: A stroke often affects the {contralateral} side of the body.
e.zh: 中风通常会影响身体的对侧。

e.en: Surgeons sometimes graft skin from the {contralateral} limb.
e.zh: 外科医生有时会从对侧肢体取皮移植。

e.en: Her rich {contralto} voice filled the entire concert hall.
e.zh: 她浑厚的女低音回荡在整个音乐厅。

e.en: The choir desperately needed another {contralto} for the upcoming performance.
e.zh: 合唱团为即将到来的演出急需再招一位女低音。

contraption.t: n. 奇怪的装置；玩意儿

e.en: He built a strange {contraption} that brews coffee using bicycle pedals.
e.zh: 他造了一个奇怪的装置,用自行车踏板来煮咖啡。

e.en: What is that bizarre {contraption} sitting on your desk?
e.zh: 你桌上那个奇怪的玩意儿是什么?

e.en: The inventor's garage was filled with bizarre wooden {contraptions}.
e.zh: 发明家的车库里堆满了各种古怪的木制装置。

e.en: Kids love building Rube Goldberg {contraptions} from household objects.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢用家里的物品搭建鲁布·戈德堡式的连锁装置。

e.en: Bach's fugues are famous for their complex {contrapuntal} structure.
e.zh: 巴赫的赋格曲以其复杂的对位结构而闻名。

e.en: The composer wove a {contrapuntal} melody through the string quartet.
e.zh: 作曲家在弦乐四重奏中编织了一段对位旋律。

contrarian.t: n. 逆向投资者；唱反调的人

e.en: He's a {contrarian} investor who buys when everyone else sells.
e.zh: 他是个逆向投资者,别人都抛售时他反而买入。

e.en: Her {contrarian} views often spark heated debates on social media.
e.zh: 她唱反调的观点经常在社交媒体上引发激烈辩论。

e.en: Hot and cold are {contraries} that cannot exist in the same place.
e.zh: 冷与热是相反的两极,无法同时存在于同一处。

e.en: The philosopher explored how {contraries} actually depend on each other.
e.zh: 那位哲学家探讨了对立面其实如何相互依存。

e.en: He always behaves {contrarily} just to annoy his older brother.
e.zh: 他总爱故意唱反调,就为了气他哥哥。

e.en: {Contrarily} to expectations, the small startup outperformed every competitor.
e.zh: 出乎意料的是,这家小初创公司超越了所有竞争对手。

e.en: His {contrariness} in meetings frustrates the whole team.
e.zh: 他在会议上的执拗让整个团队都很无奈。

e.en: The toddler's sudden {contrariness} surprised her parents.
e.zh: 这孩子突然的执拗让父母吃了一惊。

e.en: He loves crowds; {contrariwise}, his sister prefers solitude.
e.zh: 他喜欢热闹;反过来,他妹妹更喜欢独处。

e.en: Sales rose in Asia; {contrariwise}, they fell in Europe.
e.zh: 亚洲销售增长;相反,欧洲却下滑了。

contrary.t:
adj. 相反的
n. 相反的事物

e.en: {Contrary} to popular belief, sugar doesn't cause hyperactivity.
e.zh: 与大众认知相反,糖并不会让人变得多动。

e.en: His opinion was {contrary} to everyone else's.
e.zh: 他的意见与其他所有人都相反。

contrast.t:
n. 对比；反差
v. 形成对比

e.en: There's a sharp {contrast} between the two designs.
e.zh: 这两种设计之间有鲜明的对比。

e.en: You can {contrast} the colors in the photo editor.
e.zh: 你可以在图片编辑器里调整对比度。

e.en: The teacher {contrasted} the two novels in class.
e.zh: 老师在课堂上对比了这两部小说。

e.en: Her calm voice {contrasted} sharply with the chaos outside.
e.zh: 她平静的嗓音与外面的混乱形成了鲜明对比。

contrasting.t: adj. 形成对比的；差异明显的

e.en: The room features two {contrasting} shades of blue.
e.zh: 房间里有两种形成对比的蓝色调。

e.en: They have {contrasting} views on remote work.
e.zh: 他们对远程办公持有截然不同的观点。

contact.t:
v. 联系
n. 联系人；接触

e.en: Please {contact} customer support if your order is delayed.
e.zh: 如果订单延误，请联系客服。

e.en: She lost {contact} with her old roommate after graduation.
e.zh: 毕业后她与老室友失去了联系。

e.en: I {contacted} the landlord about the broken heater yesterday.
e.zh: 我昨天联系了房东，告知暖气坏了。

e.en: Several recruiters {contacted} her after she updated her profile.
e.zh: 她更新简介后，好几位招聘者主动联系了她。

contacting.t: v. 联系（contact 现在分词）

e.en: Thank you for {contacting} us about the billing issue.
e.zh: 感谢您就账单问题与我们联系。

e.en: She is {contacting} clients to confirm next week's meetings.
e.zh: 她正在联系客户确认下周的会议。

contacts.t:
n. 联系人；隐形眼镜
v. 联系

e.en: He synced his {contacts} from his phone to the laptop.
e.zh: 他把手机上的联系人同步到了笔记本电脑。

e.en: She wears daily disposable {contacts} instead of glasses.
e.zh: 她戴日抛隐形眼镜代替框架眼镜。

contagion.t: n. 传染；（情绪、风险）蔓延

e.en: Strict hygiene rules help prevent {contagion} in hospitals.
e.zh: 严格的卫生规定有助于防止医院内的传染。

e.en: Fear spread through the market like financial {contagion}.
e.zh: 恐慌像金融传染般在市场中蔓延。

e.en: Public health officials track new {contagions} around the world.
e.zh: 公共卫生官员追踪世界各地出现的新传染病。

e.en: History records many devastating {contagions} before modern medicine.
e.zh: 在现代医学出现前，史上记录了许多毁灭性的传染病。

contagious.t: adj. 有传染性的；易扩散的

e.en: Measles is extremely {contagious} among unvaccinated children.
e.zh: 麻疹在未接种疫苗的儿童中极易传染。

e.en: Her laughter was so {contagious} that everyone joined in.
e.zh: 她的笑声极具感染力，每个人都跟着笑了起来。

e.en: This snack bar does not {contain} any nuts or dairy.
e.zh: 这款零食棒不含任何坚果或乳制品。

e.en: Firefighters worked overnight to {contain} the spreading wildfire.
e.zh: 消防员通宵奋战，控制蔓延的野火。

containable.t: adj. 可遏制的；可控制的

e.en: The outbreak is {containable} if reported early enough.
e.zh: 如果及早上报，这次疫情是可以控制的。

e.en: Engineers said the leak was small and easily {containable}.
e.zh: 工程师表示泄漏量很小，很容易控制住。

contained.t:
v. 包含（过去式）
adj. 克制的

e.en: The package {contained} a handwritten note and a small gift.
e.zh: 包裹里装着一张手写便条和一份小礼物。

e.en: Authorities have {contained} the chemical spill near the river.
e.zh: 当局已控制住了河边的化学品泄漏。

e.en: Store the leftover soup in an airtight {container} overnight.
e.zh: 把剩下的汤放进密封容器里过夜。

e.en: The shipping {container} held thousands of imported electronics.
e.zh: 那个集装箱里装着数千件进口电子产品。

e.en: Most modern apps are {containerized} using Docker for easy deployment.
e.zh: 大多数现代应用使用 Docker 容器化以便于部署。

e.en: The port handles thousands of {containerized} shipments every day.
e.zh: 该港口每天处理数千个集装箱货运。

e.en: Wash the plastic {containers} before reusing them for leftovers.
e.zh: 在用塑料容器装剩菜前要先洗干净。

e.en: Kubernetes manages {containers} across hundreds of cloud servers.
e.zh: Kubernetes 在数百台云服务器上管理容器。

e.en: Avoid foods {containing} too much added sugar or salt.
e.zh: 避免食用含有过多添加糖或盐的食物。

e.en: She found a box {containing} her grandmother's old letters.
e.zh: 她发现了一个装着祖母旧信件的盒子。

e.en: Quick {containment} of the leak prevented serious environmental damage.
e.zh: 对泄漏的迅速控制避免了严重的环境破坏。

e.en: The hospital set up a {containment} zone for infected patients.
e.zh: 医院为感染患者设立了隔离区。

e.en: This drink {contains} caffeine and is not for children.
e.zh: 这款饮料含有咖啡因，不适合儿童饮用。

e.en: The folder {contains} all documents related to the project.
e.zh: 该文件夹包含与项目相关的所有文档。

e.en: Lead is a dangerous {contaminant} sometimes found in old pipes.
e.zh: 铅是一种危险的污染物，有时存在于老旧水管中。
