e.zh: 我们把每个角落都翻遍了找那枚丢失的戒指。

e.en: Spiders had built webs in every {cranny} of the shed.
e.zh: 蜘蛛在棚屋的每一道缝隙里都结了网。

e.en: Bryan {Cranston} won an Emmy for Breaking Bad.
e.zh: 布莱恩·克兰斯顿凭《绝命毒师》获得了艾美奖。

e.en: {Cranston} is a city just south of Providence, Rhode Island.
e.zh: 克兰斯顿是罗德岛州普罗维登斯南边的一座城市。

crap.t:
n. 废话；垃圾（粗俗）
adj. 糟糕的

e.en: Most of the comments online are absolute {crap}.
e.zh: 网上大多数评论都是一堆废话。

e.en: Don't believe the {crap} that influencer posts.
e.zh: 别相信那个网红发的那些胡说八道。

creaking.t:
n. 吱吱嘎嘎的声音
v. 发出吱嘎声

e.en: The {creaking} floorboards woke me up in the middle of the night.
e.zh: 嘎吱作响的地板让我半夜被惊醒。

e.en: My knees are {creaking} after that long hike yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天长途徒步后我的膝盖嘎吱作响。

creaky.t: adj. 嘎吱作响的；老旧的

e.en: The old hotel had {creaky} floors and dim lighting.
e.zh: 那家老旧酒店地板嘎吱作响,灯光昏暗。

e.en: My grandfather walks with {creaky} knees these days.
e.zh: 我爷爷如今走起路来膝盖嘎吱作响。

cream.t:
n. 奶油；乳霜
adj. 奶油色的

e.en: I always add a splash of {cream} to my morning coffee.
e.zh: 我总是会在早晨的咖啡里加一点奶油。

e.en: She rubbed sunscreen {cream} on her arms before the beach.
e.zh: 去海滩前她在手臂上涂了防晒霜。

creamed.t:
adj. 加了奶油的
v. 搅成糊状

e.en: My grandmother served {creamed} corn at every Thanksgiving dinner.
e.zh: 我奶奶每年感恩节晚餐都会做奶油玉米。

e.en: Our team got {creamed} in the championship game last weekend.
e.zh: 我们队在上周末的冠军赛中惨败。

e.en: I prefer vanilla {creamer} in my coffee instead of milk.
e.zh: 我喝咖啡时更喜欢加香草奶精而不是牛奶。

e.en: She poured oat {creamer} into her latte at the cafe.
e.zh: 她在咖啡馆里往拿铁里倒了燕麦奶精。

creamery.t: n. 乳制品加工厂；奶品店

e.en: The local {creamery} sells fresh ice cream every Saturday.
e.zh: 当地的奶制品店每周六都出售新鲜冰淇淋。

e.en: We toured a small {creamery} that makes artisan cheese.
e.zh: 我们参观了一家制作手工奶酪的小型奶制品厂。

e.en: The avocado adds a wonderful {creaminess} to the smoothie.
e.zh: 牛油果给奶昔增添了一种美妙的奶油质感。

e.en: I love the rich {creaminess} of homemade mashed potatoes.
e.zh: 我喜欢自制土豆泥那种浓郁的奶油口感。

e.en: She tried several anti-aging {creams} before finding one she liked.
e.zh: 她试用了好几种抗衰老面霜才找到一款喜欢的。

e.en: The bakery sells pastries filled with sweet {creams}.
e.zh: 那家烘焙店出售各种夹心奶油糕点。

e.en: Her grandmother collected vintage {creamware} from English potteries.
e.zh: 她外婆收藏了来自英国陶瓷厂的复古奶油色瓷器。

e.en: The museum displayed eighteenth-century {creamware} dinner plates.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了十八世纪的奶油色陶瓷餐盘。

e.en: This pasta sauce has a rich, {creamy} texture I love.
e.zh: 这款意面酱浓郁顺滑,口感非常好。

e.en: She painted the walls a warm {creamy} white color.
e.zh: 她把墙壁刷成了温暖的奶白色。

crease.t:
n. 折痕；皱褶
v. 弄皱

e.en: There's a sharp {crease} down the front of his trousers.
e.zh: 他裤子前面有一道笔直的折痕。

e.en: Try not to {crease} the photo when you put it away.
e.zh: 收起照片时尽量别把它弄出折痕。

e.en: My shirt got badly {creased} inside the suitcase.
e.zh: 我的衬衫在行李箱里被压得满是褶皱。

e.en: Her forehead {creased} with worry as she read the letter.
e.zh: 她读信时眉头因担忧而紧皱起来。

creases.t:
n. 折痕（复数）
v. 弄出褶皱

e.en: Steam easily removes {creases} from cotton shirts.
e.zh: 蒸汽可以轻松去除棉衬衫上的褶皱。

e.en: Tiny {creases} appeared at the corners of her eyes when she smiled.
e.zh: 她一笑,眼角就出现了细小的纹路。

e.en: You can {create} a free account in under a minute.
e.zh: 你可以在一分钟内创建一个免费账户。

e.en: The new policy could {create} more problems than it solves.
e.zh: 这项新政策可能制造的麻烦比解决的还多。

created.t: v. 创建了；创造了（过去式）

e.en: She {created} a Notion page to track all her tasks.
e.zh: 她建了一个 Notion 页面来跟踪所有任务。

e.en: The film {created} a huge buzz on social media.
e.zh: 这部电影在社交媒体上引发了巨大的讨论。

creates.t: v. 创建；创造（第三人称单数）

e.en: This app {creates} a backup of your photos every night.
e.zh: 这个应用每晚都会自动备份你的照片。

e.en: Working from home {creates} a better balance for many people.
e.zh: 在家办公为许多人带来了更好的平衡。

creating.t: v. 正在创建；正在创造

e.en: She's {creating} short videos for her cooking channel.
e.zh: 她正在为自己的美食频道制作短视频。

e.en: The construction noise is {creating} problems for nearby residents.
e.zh: 施工噪音正给附近居民带来困扰。

e.en: The doctor checked his {creatinine} levels to assess kidney function.
e.zh: 医生检查了他的肌酐水平以评估肾功能。

e.en: High {creatinine} in the blood may indicate kidney problems.
e.zh: 血液中肌酐偏高可能提示肾脏有问题。

e.en: The {creation} of the new app took almost two years.
e.zh: 这款新应用的开发花了将近两年时间。

e.en: This dessert is the chef's latest {creation}.
e.zh: 这道甜点是主厨最新的作品。

e.en: Some schools still teach {creationism} alongside evolution.
e.zh: 有些学校仍把神创论和进化论一起教授。

e.en: He wrote a book criticizing {creationism} from a scientific perspective.
e.zh: 他写了一本书从科学角度批判神创论。

creations.t: n. 创作品；发明物（复数）

e.en: Her latest {creations} are on display at the local gallery.
e.zh: 她最新的作品正在本地画廊展出。

e.en: The pastry chef's {creations} look almost too pretty to eat.
e.zh: 那位糕点师的作品漂亮得让人不忍下口。

creative.t: adj. 有创意的；创造性的

e.en: We need a more {creative} approach to this marketing problem.
e.zh: 我们需要用更有创意的方法来解决这个营销问题。

e.en: She works as a {creative} director at an ad agency.
e.zh: 她在一家广告公司担任创意总监。

e.en: The team responded {creatively} to the budget cuts.
e.zh: 团队对预算削减做出了富有创意的应对。

e.en: He uses social media {creatively} to grow his small business.
e.zh: 他创造性地利用社交媒体发展自己的小生意。

e.en: The judges praised the {creativeness} of her science project.
e.zh: 评委们称赞了她科学作品的创造性。

e.en: His {creativeness} shows in every detail of the design.
e.zh: 设计的每个细节都体现出他的创造力。

e.en: Different {creativities} emerge when teams come from varied backgrounds.
e.zh: 团队成员背景各异时,会涌现出不同形式的创造力。

e.en: The workshop celebrates the {creativities} of children worldwide.
e.zh: 该工作坊展示并庆祝世界各地儿童的多元创造力。

e.en: Sleep plays a key role in boosting {creativity}.
e.zh: 充足的睡眠对提升创造力起着关键作用。

e.en: This job demands a lot of {creativity} and patience.
e.zh: 这份工作需要大量的创造力和耐心。

e.en: She's a popular {creator} on TikTok with millions of followers.
e.zh: 她是 TikTok 上的人气创作者,拥有数百万粉丝。

e.en: The {creator} of the series gave a talk at the festival.
e.zh: 该剧的创作者在电影节上做了一场演讲。

e.en: YouTube pays {creators} based on ad revenue and views.
e.zh: YouTube 根据广告收入和观看量向创作者付费。

e.en: The platform offers tools to help small {creators} grow.
e.zh: 该平台提供工具帮助小型创作者成长。

e.en: A strange {creature} was spotted in the forest last night.
e.zh: 昨晚有人在森林里看到一只奇怪的生物。

e.en: My cat is such a lazy {creature} in the afternoon.
e.zh: 我家的猫下午总是一副懒洋洋的样子。

e.en: The poem reflects on our shared {creaturely} weaknesses.
e.zh: 这首诗反思了我们作为生灵共有的脆弱。

e.en: He writes about food with an honest, {creaturely} pleasure.
e.zh: 他笔下的食物流露出一种坦率而本能的愉悦。

e.en: Deep-sea {creatures} have adapted to extreme darkness.
e.zh: 深海生物已经适应了极端的黑暗环境。

e.en: Humans are social {creatures} who need connection.
e.zh: 人类是需要彼此连接的社会性生物。

creb.t: n. CREB 蛋白（与记忆相关的转录因子）

e.en: Researchers found that {CREB} plays a key role in long-term memory.
e.zh: 研究人员发现 CREB 蛋白在长期记忆中起关键作用。

e.en: The drug appears to activate the {CREB} signaling pathway.
e.zh: 该药物似乎能激活 CREB 信号通路。

creche.t: n. 托儿所；耶稣诞生像

e.en: She drops her son off at the {creche} before work.
e.zh: 她上班前会把儿子送到托儿所。

e.en: The hotel offers a {creche} so parents can enjoy dinner.
e.zh: 这家酒店提供托儿服务,方便家长安心用餐。

cred.t: n. 可信度；声望（credibility 缩写）

e.en: Wearing vintage sneakers gives him serious street {cred}.
e.zh: 穿复古球鞋让他在街头很有面子。

e.en: Her years at NASA gave her real scientific {cred}.
e.zh: 她在美国航空航天局的多年经历让她在学界真正受认可。

e.en: The new evidence lends {credence} to her theory.
e.zh: 新的证据为她的理论增添了可信度。

e.en: I don't give much {credence} to anonymous online reviews.
e.zh: 我不太相信匿名的网络评论。

e.en: You'll need a teaching {credential} to apply for this job.
e.zh: 申请这份工作需要教师资格证书。

e.en: Never share your login {credential} with anyone.
e.zh: 千万不要把你的登录凭证告诉任何人。

credentialed.t: adj. 持有证书的；有资格的

e.en: Only fully {credentialed} nurses can administer this medication.
e.zh: 只有持证的注册护士才能给药这种药物。

e.en: The conference is open to {credentialed} journalists.
e.zh: 该会议仅向持有记者证的媒体人士开放。

credentialing.t:
n. 资格认证
v. 颁发资质

e.en: The hospital's {credentialing} process can take several weeks.
e.zh: 医院的资质审核流程可能需要几周时间。

e.en: New {credentialing} rules will affect part-time instructors.
e.zh: 新的资格认证规定将影响兼职讲师。

credentials.t: n. 凭据（账号密码）；资质证明

e.en: Please don't email your login {credentials} to anyone.
e.zh: 请不要把你的登录账号密码通过邮件发给任何人。

e.en: Her {credentials} as a researcher are impressive.
e.zh: 她作为研究员的资历令人印象深刻。

e.en: A sleek walnut {credenza} sat against the office wall.
e.zh: 办公室靠墙摆着一个简约的胡桃木矮柜。

e.en: She stores extra dishes inside the dining-room {credenza}.
e.zh: 她把多余的餐具收在餐厅的矮边柜里。

e.en: The scandal damaged the {credibilities} of several major networks.
e.zh: 这起丑闻损害了几家大型电视网的公信力。

e.en: Different sources have different {credibilities} on this topic.
e.zh: 在这个话题上,不同来源的可信度各不相同。

e.en: Lying once can destroy a journalist's {credibility} forever.
e.zh: 撒一次谎就可能彻底毁掉一名记者的公信力。

e.en: The study lacks {credibility} because the sample was too small.
e.zh: 由于样本太小,这项研究缺乏可信度。

e.en: We need a {credible} witness to back up the story.
e.zh: 我们需要一位可信的证人来佐证这件事。

e.en: There's no {credible} evidence that the rumor is true.
e.zh: 没有可信的证据表明这则传闻属实。

e.en: He {credibly} denied any involvement in the leak.
e.zh: 他以令人信服的方式否认与此次泄密有关。

e.en: The startup can now {credibly} compete with industry giants.
e.zh: 这家初创公司现在已能与行业巨头一较高下。

credit.t:
n. 信用；额度；功劳
v. 归功于

e.en: You'll get full {credit} for your work on this project.
e.zh: 你在这个项目上的工作会得到充分的认可。

e.en: I paid for the flight with my {credit} card.
e.zh: 我用信用卡支付了机票费用。

e.en: The report's {creditability} suffered after key facts were disputed.
e.zh: 在关键事实遭到质疑后,这份报告的可信性受到了影响。

e.en: Years of accurate forecasts built up the team's {creditability}.
e.zh: 多年准确的预测为这个团队建立了可信度。

creditable.t: adj. 值得称赞的；可信的

e.en: She gave a {creditable} performance in her first interview.
e.zh: 她在第一次面试中表现得相当不错。

e.en: The team made a {creditable} effort despite the loss.
e.zh: 尽管输了比赛,这支队伍仍打出了值得称道的表现。

e.en: The young pianist performed quite {creditably} at the recital.
e.zh: 那位年轻钢琴家在独奏会上表现相当出色。

e.en: The rookie handled the pressure {creditably} in his debut game.
e.zh: 这位新秀在首场比赛中应对压力的表现可圈可点。

credited.t: v. 记入（账户）；归功于（过去式）

e.en: She is {credited} with inventing the first practical electric car.
e.zh: 她被认为是第一辆实用电动汽车的发明者。

e.en: The refund was {credited} to my account this morning.
e.zh: 退款今早已经入账到我的账户。

crediting.t: v. 正在记入；正在归功

e.en: Always remember to share artwork while {crediting} the original artist.
e.zh: 分享插画时一定要记得标注原作者。

e.en: The bank is {crediting} interest to savings accounts tomorrow.
e.zh: 银行将于明天将利息入账到储蓄账户。

e.en: The company must repay its largest {creditor} within thirty days.
e.zh: 公司必须在三十天内偿还其最大债权人的款项。

e.en: After bankruptcy, every {creditor} got only a small fraction back.
e.zh: 破产后,每位债权人只能拿回很小一部分钱。

credits.t:
n. 片尾/片头字幕名单
n. 学分；信用额

e.en: Don't leave the theater before the closing {credits} finish.
e.zh: 片尾字幕放完之前别离开影院。

e.en: He earned enough {credits} to graduate a semester early.
e.zh: 他修够了学分,可以提前一个学期毕业。

e.en: The bank assesses your {creditworthiness} before approving any loan.
e.zh: 银行在批准贷款前会评估你的信用状况。

e.en: Paying bills on time gradually improves your {creditworthiness}.
e.zh: 按时支付账单可以逐步提升你的信用度。

creditworthy.t: adj. 有良好信用的；可放贷的

e.en: Only {creditworthy} customers qualify for the lowest interest rate.
e.zh: 只有信用良好的客户才能享受最低利率。

e.en: A steady job makes you look more {creditworthy} to lenders.
e.zh: 稳定的工作会让贷款机构觉得你更值得信任。

e.en: "Move fast and learn faster" is the startup's {credo}.
e.zh: “快速行动,更快学习”是这家初创公司的信条。

e.en: Honesty above all has always been her personal {credo}.
e.zh: 诚信至上一直是她的人生信条。

e.en: The plot twist really stretched the audience's {credulity}.
e.zh: 剧情的反转实在让观众难以相信。

e.en: Online scammers often exploit the {credulity} of elderly users.
e.zh: 网络骗子常常利用老年用户的轻信下手。

e.en: Don't be so {credulous}—not everything online is true.
e.zh: 别这么轻信,网上的东西不都是真的。

e.en: The scam targeted {credulous} investors hoping for quick profits.
e.zh: 这场骗局专门针对希望快速赚钱的轻信投资者。

cree.t: n. 克里人（北美原住民）；其语言

e.en: Many {Cree} communities are working to revive their language.
e.zh: 许多克里族社区正致力于复兴他们的语言。

e.en: She grew up speaking {Cree} on the reserve in Manitoba.
e.zh: 她在马尼托巴省的保留地长大,从小说克里语。

e.en: Everyone is welcome here, regardless of race or {creed}.
e.zh: 无论种族或信仰,这里都欢迎所有人。

e.en: Kindness to strangers is part of his personal {creed}.
e.zh: 善待陌生人是他个人信条的一部分。

e.en: The church holds firmly to its traditional {creedal} statements.
e.zh: 这间教会坚定地坚守其传统的信条声明。

e.en: Their disagreement was more {creedal} than personal.
e.zh: 他们的分歧更多是信仰层面的,而非个人恩怨。

e.en: We waded across the shallow {creek} to reach the trail.
e.zh: 我们涉过浅浅的小溪走到步道上。

e.en: A small {creek} runs behind our backyard all year.
e.zh: 一条小溪常年从我们后院流过。

e.en: Several {creeks} feed into this river during spring.
e.zh: 春天有几条小溪汇入这条河。

e.en: The hikers crossed three {creeks} before lunch.
e.zh: 徒步者在午餐前涉过了三条小溪。

e.en: He carried his catch home in a wicker {creel}.
e.zh: 他用柳条鱼篓把渔获带回了家。

e.en: The fisherman strapped a leather {creel} over his shoulder.
e.zh: 那位渔夫把皮革鱼篓挎在肩上。

creep.t:
v. 悄悄移动；蔓延
n. 讨厌鬼

e.en: Don't {creep} up behind me like that again.
e.zh: 别再那样从我背后偷偷靠近。

e.en: That guy at the bar is a total {creep}.
e.zh: 酒吧里那家伙真是个让人发毛的怪人。

e.en: A flowering {creeper} covered the entire garden wall.
e.zh: 一株开花的藤蔓爬满了整面花园墙。

e.en: Players fear the green {creeper} mob in Minecraft.
e.zh: 玩家都害怕《我的世界》里那只绿色苦力怕。

creepiest.t: adj. 最毛骨悚然的（creepy 最高级）

e.en: That was the {creepiest} horror movie I've ever watched.
e.zh: 那是我看过最毛骨悚然的恐怖片。

e.en: He told us the {creepiest} story around the campfire.
e.zh: 他在篝火旁讲了最让人发毛的故事。

creepiness.t: n. 令人毛骨悚然；瘆人

e.en: The doll's smile added an extra layer of {creepiness}.
e.zh: 那娃娃的笑容又增添了一层诡异感。

e.en: There's a certain {creepiness} to abandoned hospitals.
e.zh: 废弃医院总带着一种让人发毛的气息。

creeping.t:
adj. 缓慢渐进的
v. 爬行（creep 的现在分词）

e.en: A vine was slowly {creeping} up the brick wall.
e.zh: 一株藤蔓正缓缓爬上砖墙。

e.en: Doubt kept {creeping} into her mind before the exam.
e.zh: 考试前怀疑不断涌入她的脑海。

creeps.t:
n. 毛骨悚然的感觉
v. 悄悄爬行

e.en: That haunted house really gives me the {creeps}.
e.zh: 那栋鬼屋真让我浑身起鸡皮疙瘩。

e.en: Inflation slowly {creeps} into everyday grocery prices.
e.zh: 通胀正悄悄渗入日常的食品价格中。

creepy.t: adj. 令人毛骨悚然的；诡异的

e.en: The abandoned mall felt really {creepy} at night.
e.zh: 那座废弃商场夜里感觉真让人发毛。

e.en: It's {creepy} how the algorithm knows what I want.
e.zh: 算法知道我想要什么,这种感觉真诡异。

e.en: The family chose to {cremate} their grandfather instead of burying him.
e.zh: 家人选择火化祖父,而不是土葬。

e.en: Many cultures {cremate} the deceased as part of tradition.
e.zh: 许多文化按传统将逝者火化。

cremated.t: v. 已火化（cremate 的过去式）

e.en: She wanted to be {cremated} and scattered at sea.
e.zh: 她希望被火化后骨灰撒入大海。

e.en: His remains were {cremated} in a private ceremony.
e.zh: 他的遗体在一场私人仪式上被火化。

e.en: They held a small ceremony before the {cremation}.
e.zh: 他们在火化前举行了一场小型仪式。

e.en: {Cremation} has become more common than burial in cities.
e.zh: 在城市里,火葬已比土葬更为常见。

e.en: The funeral procession drove slowly toward the {crematorium}.
e.zh: 送葬车队缓缓驶向火葬场。

e.en: A new {crematorium} was built on the city outskirts.
e.zh: 城郊新建了一座火葬场。

crematory.t:
n. 火葬场
adj. 火葬的

e.en: The {crematory} operates seven days a week.
e.zh: 这家火葬场每周七天都营业。

e.en: Workers at the {crematory} handled each urn with care.
e.zh: 火葬场的工作人员小心地处理每一个骨灰罐。

e.en: She ordered a {creme} brulee for dessert.
e.zh: 她点了一份焦糖布丁作为甜点。

e.en: The cake was filled with vanilla {creme}.
e.zh: 蛋糕里夹着香草奶油馅。

cremona.t: n. 克雷莫纳（意大利城市，以制琴闻名）

e.en: The violin was crafted in {Cremona}, Italy.
e.zh: 这把小提琴是在意大利克雷莫纳制作的。

e.en: {Cremona} is famous for its centuries-old violin makers.
e.zh: 克雷莫纳以其数百年历史的制琴师闻名。

crenellate.t: v. 在城墙上筑雉堞（锯齿形垛口）

e.en: Medieval masons would {crenellate} castle walls for defense.
e.zh: 中世纪石匠会在城堡墙上修筑垛口以利防御。

e.en: Architects sometimes {crenellate} rooflines to mimic old fortresses.
e.zh: 建筑师有时会在屋顶做出垛口以模仿古老堡垒。

crenellated.t: adj. 有雉堞的；城垛状的

e.en: The castle had a tall, {crenellated} stone tower.
e.zh: 城堡有一座高高的、带垛口的石塔。

e.en: A {crenellated} wall surrounded the medieval town.
e.zh: 一道带垛口的城墙环绕着这座中世纪小镇。

crenellation.t: n. 雉堞；城墙上的垛口

e.en: Each {crenellation} on the wall sheltered a single archer.
e.zh: 城墙上的每个垛口都可掩护一名弓箭手。

e.en: The fortress's {crenellation} survived eight hundred years intact.
e.zh: 这座要塞的垛墙完整保存了八百年。

creole.t:
n. 克里奥尔人/语
adj. 克里奥尔的

e.en: Haitian {Creole} is spoken by millions in the Caribbean.
e.zh: 加勒比地区有数百万人讲海地克里奥尔语。

e.en: We had spicy {Creole} shrimp for dinner in New Orleans.
e.zh: 我们在新奥尔良晚餐吃了辣味克里奥尔虾。

creolization.t: n. 语言/文化的克里奥尔化

e.en: The {creolization} of cuisines reshaped Caribbean cooking forever.
e.zh: 菜系的克里奥尔化彻底重塑了加勒比饮食。

e.en: Linguists study {creolization} to understand how new languages emerge.
e.zh: 语言学家研究克里奥尔化以理解新语言如何形成。

creosote.t: n. 杂酚油（防腐木材用）

e.en: The old fence posts were soaked in {creosote}.
e.zh: 那些旧栅栏柱浸过杂酚油防腐。

e.en: {Creosote} buildup in the chimney can cause house fires.
e.zh: 烟囱里积聚的木焦油可能引发火灾。

e.en: She ordered a Nutella {crepe} from the street vendor.
e.zh: 她向街边小贩点了一份能多益可丽饼。

e.en: He wore a black {crepe} dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了一条黑色绉绸礼服去参加晚宴。

crept.t: v. 悄悄爬行（creep 的过去式）

e.en: She {crept} downstairs so she wouldn't wake anyone.
e.zh: 她蹑手蹑脚下楼,以免吵醒别人。

e.en: A small smile {crept} across his face.
e.zh: 一丝微笑悄悄爬上了他的脸。

crepuscular.t: adj. 黄昏的；晨昏活动的（动物）

e.en: Deer are {crepuscular} animals, most active at dawn and dusk.
e.zh: 鹿是晨昏性动物,在拂晓和黄昏最为活跃。

e.en: The forest had a soft, {crepuscular} glow at sunset.
e.zh: 日落时分,森林笼罩在柔和的暮光中。

crescendo.t:
n. 渐强；高潮
v. 逐渐增强

e.en: The music rose to a thrilling {crescendo} at the finale.
e.zh: 音乐在终曲处推向一个激动人心的高潮。

e.en: Public anger reached a {crescendo} after the announcement.
e.zh: 公告发布后,公众的愤怒达到了顶点。

crescent.t:
n. 新月；月牙形物
adj. 新月形的

e.en: A thin {crescent} moon hung above the rooftops.
e.zh: 一弯新月悬在屋顶之上。

e.en: She bit into a buttery {crescent} roll for breakfast.
e.zh: 她早餐咬了一口黄油牛角面包。

e.en: He sprinkled fresh {cress} on top of the soup.
e.zh: 他在汤上撒了些新鲜水芹。

e.en: The sandwich came with egg and {cress} filling.
e.zh: 那份三明治夹着鸡蛋和水芹。

cressida.t: n. 克蕾西达（人名；天王星卫星）

e.en: Shakespeare's {Cressida} is a complex tragic heroine.
e.zh: 莎士比亚笔下的克瑞西达是个复杂的悲剧女主角。

e.en: She named her daughter {Cressida} after the play.
e.zh: 她以那部戏剧为女儿取名克瑞西达。

cresson.t: n. 克雷松（法语：水芹；地名/人名）

e.en: The salad featured peppery {cresson} and goat cheese.
e.zh: 那道沙拉用了辛香的法式水芹和山羊奶酪。

e.en: French chefs often garnish soup with {cresson}.
e.zh: 法国厨师常用水芹来点缀汤品。

crest.t:
n. 顶峰；浪尖；纹章
v. 达到顶点

e.en: We finally reached the {crest} of the hill at sunset.
e.zh: 我们终于在日落时登上山顶。

e.en: The school {crest} was embroidered on every blazer.
e.zh: 校徽绣在每一件西装外套上。

crested.t: adj. 有冠毛的；带纹章的

e.en: A {crested} bird landed on the feeder this morning.
e.zh: 今早一只有冠的鸟落在了喂食器上。

e.en: She {crested} the ridge and saw the valley below.
e.zh: 她登上山脊,看见下方的山谷。

crestfallen.t: adj. 垂头丧气的；沮丧的

e.en: He looked {crestfallen} after losing the final match.
e.zh: 输掉决赛后他显得十分沮丧。

e.en: The {crestfallen} child stared at her broken toy.
e.zh: 那个垂头丧气的孩子盯着她坏掉的玩具。

cresting.t:
v. 达到顶峰
n. 屋顶装饰带

e.en: The river is {cresting} earlier than forecasters predicted.
e.zh: 河水比预报员预测的更早达到峰值。

e.en: Surfers waited for the wave {cresting} near the reef.
e.zh: 冲浪者等候着在礁石附近浪头翻涌的浪花。

cretaceous.t:
adj. 白垩纪的
n. 白垩纪

e.en: Tyrannosaurus rex roamed the earth during the {Cretaceous} period.
e.zh: 霸王龙在白垩纪时期漫步地球。

e.en: Scientists found {Cretaceous} fossils embedded in the cliff.
e.zh: 科学家在悬崖中发现了白垩纪的化石。

cretan.t:
adj. 克里特岛的
n. 克里特人

e.en: We tasted authentic {Cretan} olive oil at the market.
e.zh: 我们在集市上品尝了正宗的克里特橄榄油。

e.en: The {Cretan} coastline is famous for its hidden coves.
e.zh: 克里特海岸线以隐秘的小海湾闻名。

e.en: We spent two weeks vacationing in {Crete} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们在克里特岛度了两周假。

e.en: {Crete} is the largest island in Greece.
e.zh: 克里特岛是希腊最大的岛屿。

e.en: Don't act like a {cretin} during the interview.
e.zh: 面试时别表现得像个白痴。

e.en: He called the driver a {cretin} for running the light.
e.zh: 他骂那个闯红灯的司机是个蠢货。

e.en: Iodine deficiency can cause {cretinism} in newborns.
e.zh: 碘缺乏会导致新生儿发生克汀病。

e.en: Salt iodization programs nearly eliminated {cretinism} worldwide.
e.zh: 食盐加碘计划几乎在全球消除了克汀病。

e.en: His {cretinous} remarks ruined the entire dinner conversation.
e.zh: 他那些蠢话毁了整顿晚饭的谈话。

e.en: Critics called the policy a {cretinous} waste of money.
e.zh: 批评者称该政策是愚蠢的浪费金钱。

e.en: The climber nearly fell into a deep glacial {crevasse}.
e.zh: 那位登山者差点掉进一条深深的冰川裂缝。

e.en: Rescue teams searched the {crevasse} for missing skiers.
e.zh: 救援队在冰川裂缝中搜寻失踪的滑雪者。

e.en: A small lizard darted into a {crevice} in the rock.
e.zh: 一只小蜥蜴窜进了岩石的缝隙里。

e.en: Coins had fallen into every {crevice} of the sofa.
e.zh: 硬币掉进了沙发的每一条缝里。

crew.t:
n. 全体船员、机组人员
n. 团队；一伙人

e.en: The film {crew} worked late into the night.
e.zh: 摄制组工作到深夜。

e.en: The flight {crew} welcomed passengers as they boarded.
e.zh: 机组人员在乘客登机时致以欢迎。

e.en: We changed trains at {Crewe} on our way north.
e.zh: 我们北上途中在克鲁站换乘列车。

e.en: {Crewe} has long been a major British railway junction.
e.zh: 克鲁长期以来是英国重要的铁路枢纽。

crewed.t:
adj. 载人的
v. 当船员 (过去式)

e.en: NASA plans a {crewed} mission to Mars next decade.
e.zh: NASA计划下个十年执行一次载人火星任务。

e.en: The yacht is {crewed} by a team of five sailors.
e.zh: 这艘游艇由五名船员驾驶。

e.en: One {crewman} stayed behind to repair the radio.
e.zh: 一名船员留下来修理无线电。

e.en: Each {crewman} received a medal for the rescue.
e.zh: 每位船员都因这次救援获得了一枚奖章。

e.en: My {crewmate} got voted out in the first round.
e.zh: 我的队友在第一轮就被投票淘汰了。

e.en: She trusted her {crewmate} to finish the repairs.
e.zh: 她信任队友把维修工作做完。

e.en: Every {crewmember} must complete safety training annually.
e.zh: 每位机组成员每年都必须完成安全培训。

e.en: A {crewmember} helped the elderly passenger find her seat.
e.zh: 一位机组成员帮那位老年乘客找到了座位。

crews.t: n. 船员们；团队 (crew 复数)

e.en: Cleanup {crews} worked through the night after the storm.
e.zh: 风暴过后,清理队伍通宵工作。

e.en: Two camera {crews} covered the political rally.
e.zh: 两组摄影团队报道了这场政治集会。

crib.t:
n. 婴儿床
v. 抄袭；作弊

e.en: The baby fell asleep peacefully in the wooden {crib}.
e.zh: 宝宝在木制婴儿床里安然入睡。

e.en: He tried to {crib} answers from his classmate during the test.
e.zh: 他考试时试图抄同学的答案。

cribbage.t: n. 克里比奇纸牌游戏

e.en: My grandfather taught me how to play {cribbage} as a child.
e.zh: 我小时候爷爷教我玩克里比奇牌。

e.en: They spent the rainy afternoon at a {cribbage} board.
e.zh: 他们在克里比奇牌桌前度过了那个雨天的下午。

e.en: The {cribriform} plate separates the nasal cavity from the brain.
e.zh: 筛板将鼻腔与大脑分隔开。

e.en: Doctors examined damage to the {cribriform} bone after the injury.
e.zh: 医生检查了受伤后筛骨的损伤情况。

e.en: I woke up with a painful {crick} in my neck.
e.zh: 我醒来时脖子落枕了,很疼。

e.en: Sleeping on the plane gave him a bad {crick}.
e.zh: 在飞机上睡觉让他落枕了。

cricket.t:
n. 板球运动
n. 蟋蟀

e.en: He plays {cricket} every Saturday with his local club.
e.zh: 他每周六都和本地俱乐部一起打板球。

e.en: A {cricket} chirped loudly outside the bedroom window.
e.zh: 一只蟋蟀在卧室窗外大声鸣叫。

e.en: She became the youngest {cricketer} to score a century.
e.zh: 她成为最年轻的击出百分的板球运动员。

e.en: The retired {cricketer} now coaches schoolchildren on weekends.
e.zh: 这位退役板球运动员现在周末教孩子们打球。

e.en: India has a long and proud {cricketing} tradition.
e.zh: 印度有着悠久而自豪的板球传统。

e.en: His {cricketing} career ended after a serious knee injury.
e.zh: 他的板球生涯因严重的膝伤而结束。

crickets.t: n. 蟋蟀 (复数)；鸦雀无声 (网络用语)

e.en: I told a joke and got nothing but {crickets}.
e.zh: 我讲了个笑话,结果全场鸦雀无声。

e.en: The {crickets} sang all night long in the meadow.
e.zh: 草地上的蟋蟀整晚都在鸣叫。

e.en: The doctor pressed gently on the {cricoid} cartilage during intubation.
e.zh: 医生在插管时轻按环状软骨。

e.en: The {cricoid} ring sits just below the thyroid cartilage.
e.zh: 环状软骨位于甲状软骨的正下方。

cried.t: v. 哭泣；喊叫 (cry 过去式)

e.en: She {cried} for hours after hearing the sad news.
e.zh: 听到这个噩耗后她哭了好几个小时。

e.en: "Watch out!" he {cried} as the car swerved.
e.zh: 汽车急转时他大喊:“小心!”

e.en: The town {crier} announced the news in the village square.
e.zh: 镇上的传报员在村广场上宣布消息。

e.en: My little sister is a real {crier} during sad movies.
e.zh: 我妹妹看伤感电影时特别爱哭。

cries.t:
v. 哭；叫喊 (cry 第三人称)
n. 喊叫声

e.en: The baby's {cries} woke everyone up at midnight.
e.zh: 婴儿的哭声半夜把大家都吵醒了。

e.en: She {cries} every time she watches that movie.
e.zh: 每次看那部电影她都会哭。

e.en: "{Crikey}, that snake is huge!" he exclaimed loudly.
e.zh: “天哪,那条蛇好大!”他大声惊呼。

e.en: {Crikey}, I didn't expect the bill to be so high.
e.zh: 哎呀,我没想到账单这么高。

e.en: The cop chased the {crim} down a narrow alley.
e.zh: 警察沿着一条狭窄的小巷追赶那个罪犯。

e.en: He's been a small-time {crim} since his teens.
e.zh: 他从十几岁起就是个小混混。

e.en: The detective solved the {crime} within a single week.
e.zh: 侦探在一周之内就破了这起案件。

e.en: It's a {crime} to waste such delicious food.
e.zh: 浪费这么好吃的食物简直是罪过。

e.en: The {Crimea} peninsula has a long and turbulent history.
e.zh: 克里米亚半岛有着悠久而动荡的历史。

e.en: Tourists once flocked to the beaches of {Crimea}.
e.zh: 游客曾蜂拥前往克里米亚的海滩。

e.en: The {Crimean} War shaped modern military medicine significantly.
e.zh: 克里米亚战争对现代军事医学产生了深远影响。

e.en: She studied {Crimean} architecture during her semester abroad.
e.zh: 她在国外交换学习期间研究了克里米亚建筑。

crimes.t: n. 罪行；犯罪 (crime 复数)

e.en: He was charged with multiple {crimes} after the investigation.
e.zh: 调查结束后他被指控犯有多项罪行。

e.en: War {crimes} must be prosecuted no matter how long ago.
e.zh: 无论过去多久,战争罪都必须受到追究。

criminal.t:
n. 罪犯
adj. 犯罪的；刑事的

e.en: The {criminal} was finally caught after years on the run.
e.zh: 那名罪犯潜逃多年后终于被抓获。

e.en: It's {criminal} how much they charge for coffee here.
e.zh: 这里咖啡卖这么贵,简直离谱。

criminalise.t: v. 将…定为犯罪 (英式拼写)

e.en: Many countries now {criminalise} the possession of certain drugs.
e.zh: 许多国家现在将持有某些毒品定为犯罪。

e.en: Activists argue we should not {criminalise} homelessness.
e.zh: 活动人士认为不应将无家可归视为犯罪。

e.en: The {criminalist} carefully analyzed fibers found at the scene.
e.zh: 刑侦专家仔细分析了在现场发现的纤维。

e.en: She trained as a {criminalist} specializing in DNA evidence.
e.zh: 她接受培训成为一名专攻DNA证据的刑侦专家。

e.en: Poverty is often linked to higher rates of {criminality}.
e.zh: 贫困往往与较高的犯罪率相关。

e.en: The judge questioned the {criminality} of the defendant's actions.
e.zh: 法官质疑被告行为的犯罪性质。

e.en: The {criminalization} of marijuana has been widely debated lately.
e.zh: 将大麻定罪的做法近来引发广泛争论。

e.en: Critics oppose the {criminalization} of peaceful protest.
e.zh: 批评人士反对将和平抗议定为犯罪。

e.en: Lawmakers voted to {criminalize} the sharing of deepfake images.
e.zh: 立法者投票将传播深度伪造图像定为犯罪。

e.en: The new bill would {criminalize} aggressive door-to-door sales.
e.zh: 这项新法案将把强势的上门推销定为违法行为。

e.en: The restaurant's pasta is {criminally} underrated by local critics.
e.zh: 这家餐厅的意面被本地评论家严重低估了。

e.en: He was found {criminally} liable for the accident.
e.zh: 他被判对这起事故负有刑事责任。

e.en: The police arrested three {criminals} after the bank robbery.
e.zh: 银行抢劫案后警方逮捕了三名罪犯。

e.en: Cybersecurity experts help track {criminals} operating online.
e.zh: 网络安全专家帮助追踪在网上活动的罪犯。

e.en: The professor presented her latest {criminological} research at the conference.
e.zh: 教授在会议上展示了她最新的犯罪学研究。

e.en: {Criminological} studies often examine the root causes of violence.
e.zh: 犯罪学研究常常探讨暴力的根本原因。

e.en: The {criminologist} interviewed inmates to understand patterns of reoffending.
e.zh: 这位犯罪学家采访囚犯以了解再犯的规律。

e.en: A leading {criminologist} testified at the high-profile trial.
e.zh: 一位知名犯罪学家在这场备受关注的审判中作证。

e.en: She majored in {criminology} and now works for the FBI.
e.zh: 她主修犯罪学,现在在联邦调查局工作。

e.en: Modern {criminology} draws on psychology, sociology, and data science.
e.zh: 现代犯罪学借鉴了心理学、社会学和数据科学。

crimp.t:
v. 压褶；卷曲
n. 褶皱

e.en: Use pliers to {crimp} the metal connector onto the wire.
e.zh: 用钳子将金属接头压接到电线上。

e.en: The rain put a {crimp} in our weekend plans.
e.zh: 这场雨打乱了我们周末的计划。

e.en: She wore her hair {crimped} for the eighties-themed party.
e.zh: 她为八十年代主题派对烫了波浪卷发。

e.en: Supply shortages {crimped} the company's growth last quarter.
e.zh: 供应短缺抑制了公司上季度的增长。

crimplene.t: n. 克林普纶 (一种合成纤维)

e.en: My grandmother still wears her old {crimplene} dresses proudly.
e.zh: 奶奶仍自豪地穿着她那些旧的涤纶皱布连衣裙。

e.en: The seventies were full of brightly colored {crimplene} suits.
e.zh: 七十年代到处是色彩鲜艳的涤纶皱布套装。

crimson.t:
n. 深红色；绯红
adj. 深红色的

e.en: Her cheeks turned {crimson} when he complimented her dress.
e.zh: 他夸她裙子好看时,她脸涨得通红。

e.en: The autumn leaves blazed {crimson} against the gray sky.
e.zh: 秋叶在灰色天空映衬下泛着深红色。

cringe.t:
v. 感到尴尬；畏缩
n. 尴尬

e.en: I {cringe} every time I see my old social media posts.
e.zh: 每次看到自己以前发的帖子我都感到尴尬。

e.en: His pickup line made everyone at the table {cringe}.
e.zh: 他的搭讪台词让饭桌上的每个人都尴尬不已。

e.en: She watched the awkward speech, {cringing} the entire time.
e.zh: 她看着那场尴尬的演讲,全程都在脚趾抠地。

e.en: The dog kept {cringing} away from the loud thunderstorm.
e.zh: 那只狗一直畏缩着躲避响亮的雷暴。

e.en: A small furry {critter} dashed across the trail.
e.zh: 一只毛茸茸的小动物窜过了小路。

e.en: What kind of {critter} keeps eating my tomato plants?
e.zh: 是什么小东西一直在啃我的番茄苗？

croak.t:
v. (青蛙) 呱呱叫
v. 嘶哑地说

e.en: The frogs {croak} loudly after every summer rain.
e.zh: 每场夏雨过后青蛙都会大声地叫。

e.en: His voice came out as a hoarse {croak} this morning.
e.zh: 他今早的声音听起来像沙哑的蛙鸣。

croaker.t:
n. 爱抱怨的人
n. 石首鱼

e.en: We caught a small {croaker} off the fishing pier.
e.zh: 我们在渔人码头钓到了一条小石首鱼。

e.en: The {croaker} is a popular catch along the Atlantic coast.
e.zh: 石首鱼是大西洋沿岸常见的渔获。

croaking.t:
n. 呱呱叫声
adj. 嘶哑的

e.en: Frogs were {croaking} all night beside the pond.
e.zh: 青蛙在池塘边整夜地叫个不停。

e.en: His {croaking} voice gave away that he had a cold.
e.zh: 他沙哑的嗓音暴露了他正在感冒。

e.en: My voice gets {croaky} after talking for hours straight.
e.zh: 我连续说几个小时话后嗓子会变得沙哑。

e.en: She sounded {croaky} on the phone because of allergies.
e.zh: 她因为过敏，电话里的声音听起来沙哑哑的。

e.en: My new neighbor is a friendly {Croat} from Split.
e.zh: 我的新邻居是来自斯普利特的一位友善的克罗地亚人。

e.en: The team's star striker is a {Croat} who plays in Italy.
e.zh: 球队的明星前锋是一名在意大利效力的克罗地亚人。

e.en: We spent two weeks sailing along the coast of {Croatia}.
e.zh: 我们花了两周时间沿着克罗地亚海岸航行。

e.en: {Croatia} joined the European Union back in 2013.
e.zh: 克罗地亚早在 2013 年就加入了欧盟。

croatian.t:
adj. 克罗地亚的
n. 克罗地亚语

e.en: She's learning {Croatian} before moving to Zagreb.
e.zh: 她在搬到萨格勒布之前正在学习克罗地亚语。

e.en: The restaurant serves authentic {Croatian} seafood dishes.
e.zh: 这家餐厅供应正宗的克罗地亚海鲜菜肴。

e.en: A massive {croc} sunbathed on the riverbank.
e.zh: 一条巨大的鳄鱼在河岸上晒太阳。

e.en: He bought bright pink {Crocs} for the summer.
e.zh: 他买了一双亮粉色的洞洞鞋过夏天。

crochet.t:
v. 用钩针编织
n. 钩针织物

e.en: My grandma taught me how to {crochet} a simple scarf.
e.zh: 奶奶教我用钩针钩了一条简单的围巾。

e.en: She sells handmade {crochet} bags on Etsy.
e.zh: 她在 Etsy 上出售手工钩针包。

crocheted.t:
adj. 钩针编织的
v. 钩织（过去式）

e.en: She {crocheted} a tiny hat for the newborn baby.
e.zh: 她为新生儿钩了一顶小小的帽子。

e.en: The {crocheted} blanket kept us warm during the storm.
e.zh: 那条钩针毯子在暴风雨中让我们暖暖的。

e.en: She enjoys {crocheting} while watching her favorite shows.
e.zh: 她喜欢一边追剧一边钩毛线。

e.en: {Crocheting} has become a popular hobby on TikTok.
e.zh: 钩针编织在 TikTok 上成了热门爱好。

crock.t:
n. 陶罐
n. 胡说（俚语）

e.en: That excuse is a complete {crock} and you know it.
e.zh: 那个借口完全是胡扯，你心里清楚。

e.en: She stored the soup in a heavy clay {crock}.
e.zh: 她把汤盛在一个厚重的陶罐里。

e.en: Please load the dirty {crockery} into the dishwasher.
e.zh: 请把脏的碗碟放进洗碗机里。

e.en: The hotel uses elegant white {crockery} for breakfast.
e.zh: 酒店早餐用的是雅致的白色餐具。

e.en: I tossed everything into the {crockpot} before work.
e.zh: 我上班前把所有食材都丢进了慢炖锅。

e.en: This {crockpot} chili tastes even better the next day.
e.zh: 这道慢炖锅辣肉酱第二天吃更入味。

e.en: A huge {crocodile} slid silently into the murky river.
e.zh: 一条巨大的鳄鱼悄无声息地滑进浑浊的河里。

e.en: Don't trust her {crocodile} tears for one second.
e.zh: 她那些猫哭老鼠的眼泪一秒都不能信。

e.en: Saltwater {crocodiles} can grow over six meters long.
e.zh: 咸水鳄能长到六米以上。

e.en: Tourists watched the {crocodiles} basking on the riverbank.
e.zh: 游客们看着鳄鱼在河岸上晒太阳。

crocodilian.t:
adj. 鳄鱼的
n. 鳄目动物

e.en: Alligators and caimans are both {crocodilian} reptiles.
e.zh: 短吻鳄和凯门鳄都属于鳄目爬行动物。

e.en: The fossil belonged to an extinct {crocodilian} species.
e.zh: 这块化石属于一种已灭绝的鳄类物种。

e.en: A purple {crocus} pushed through the late winter snow.
e.zh: 一朵紫色的番红花从残雪中钻了出来。

e.en: Saffron is harvested from a special kind of {crocus}.
e.zh: 藏红花是从一种特殊的番红花上采集而来的。

e.en: Her family runs a small {croft} in the Scottish highlands.
e.zh: 她家在苏格兰高地经营着一处小农庄。

e.en: The old {croft} has stood on this hillside for centuries.
e.zh: 这座古老的小农舍在这山坡上已矗立了数百年。

e.en: The {crofter} sold fresh wool at the village market.
e.zh: 那位佃农在村市上出售新鲜的羊毛。

e.en: Each {crofter} tends a few sheep and a small garden.
e.zh: 每位小农都养几只羊，还打理一小块菜园。

e.en: The {crofters} raised sheep on the rocky highland soil.
e.zh: 那些小农户在多石的高地上养羊。

e.en: Scottish {crofters} fought for land rights in the 1880s.
e.zh: 苏格兰小农在1880年代为土地权而抗争。

crofting.t: n. (苏格兰) 小农耕作制

e.en: {Crofting} remains a way of life in the Hebrides.
e.zh: 小农耕作在赫布里底群岛仍是一种生活方式。

e.en: She inherited a small {crofting} plot from her grandfather.
e.zh: 她从祖父那里继承了一小块小农耕地。

crohn.t: n. 克罗恩（病名，如克罗恩病）

e.en: He was diagnosed with {Crohn}'s disease last year.
e.zh: 他去年被诊断出患有克罗恩病。

e.en: {Crohn}'s disease causes chronic inflammation in the gut.
e.zh: 克罗恩病会引起肠道慢性炎症。

e.en: I had a buttery {croissant} with my morning coffee.
e.zh: 我早上配着咖啡吃了一个香酥的可颂。

e.en: The bakery's almond {croissant} sells out by ten.
e.zh: 那家面包店的杏仁可颂十点前就卖光了。

e.en: We took the train to {Cromer} for the weekend.
e.zh: 我们坐火车去克罗默度周末。

e.en: {Cromer} is famous for its sweet brown crabs.
e.zh: 克罗默以其鲜美的褐蟹而闻名。

e.en: Oliver {Cromwell} ruled England as Lord Protector.
e.zh: 奥利弗·克伦威尔以护国公身份统治英格兰。

e.en: Thomas {Cromwell} served as chief minister to Henry VIII.
e.zh: 托马斯·克伦威尔曾任亨利八世的首席大臣。

cromwellian.t: adj. 克伦威尔（时代/风格）的

e.en: The {Cromwellian} army crushed the royalist forces.
e.zh: 克伦威尔的军队击溃了保王党势力。

e.en: Ireland still remembers the harsh {Cromwellian} conquest.
e.zh: 爱尔兰至今仍铭记克伦威尔时期的残酷征服。

e.en: In the fairy tale, an old {crone} offered her an apple.
e.zh: 童话里,一个老巫婆递给她一个苹果。

e.en: The villagers feared the {crone} who lived in the woods.
e.zh: 村民们害怕那个住在林中的老妪。

cronies.t: n. 密友；死党（常含贬义）

e.en: The mayor handed contracts to his political {cronies}.
e.zh: 市长把合同发给了自己的政治死党。

e.en: He spent the evening drinking with his old {cronies}.
e.zh: 他和老哥们儿喝了一晚上酒。

e.en: That executive is just a {crony} of the chairman.
e.zh: 那位高管不过是董事长的亲信而已。

e.en: He hired an old {crony} to run the department.
e.zh: 他雇了一位老朋友来管理这个部门。

cronyism.t: n. 任人唯亲；裙带关系

e.en: The administration was accused of blatant {cronyism}.
e.zh: 该政府被指责公然任人唯亲。

e.en: Voters are tired of the {cronyism} in city hall.
e.zh: 选民们厌倦了市政厅里的裙带关系。

crook.t:
n. 骗子；罪犯
n. 弯钩

e.en: That landlord is a complete {crook}.
e.zh: 那个房东就是个彻头彻尾的骗子。

e.en: She carried the puppy in the {crook} of her arm.
e.zh: 她把小狗抱在臂弯里。

crooked.t:
adj. 弯曲的；歪的
adj. 不诚实的

e.en: The painting on the wall is slightly {crooked}.
e.zh: 墙上那幅画有点歪。

e.en: A {crooked} cop was finally arrested for taking bribes.
e.zh: 一名贪污的警察终于因受贿被捕。

e.en: The sign hung {crookedly} above the shop door.
e.zh: 招牌歪歪斜斜地挂在店门上方。

e.en: He smiled {crookedly} when he heard the news.
e.zh: 他听到消息时嘴角斜斜地扬起一抹笑。

e.en: The {crookedness} of the old fence made it charming.
e.zh: 那道旧栅栏歪歪扭扭的样子反而显得别致。

e.en: Investigators uncovered the {crookedness} of the deal.
e.zh: 调查人员揭露了这笔交易的不正当之处。

croon.t: v. 低声吟唱；柔声歌唱

e.en: She would {croon} softly to the baby at night.
e.zh: 她晚上会轻声哼唱哄宝宝入睡。

e.en: Old singers still {croon} love songs at the lounge.
e.zh: 老歌手们仍在酒廊里低吟着情歌。

e.en: Frank Sinatra was the most famous {crooner} of his era.
e.zh: 弗兰克·辛纳屈是他那个时代最著名的低音歌手。

e.en: The lounge {crooner} held the audience spellbound.
e.zh: 酒廊里的低吟歌手让听众如痴如醉。

crooning.t:
n. 低声吟唱
adj. 低吟的

e.en: He kept {crooning} the same old jazz standard.
e.zh: 他不停地低声哼唱着那首老爵士经典。

e.en: Her {crooning} voice filled the smoky bar.
e.zh: 她低吟的嗓音弥漫在烟雾缭绕的酒吧里。

crop.t:
n. 农作物；收成
v. 裁剪（图片）

e.en: This year's wheat {crop} was the best in a decade.
e.zh: 今年的小麦收成是十年来最好的。

e.en: You can {crop} the photo to focus on her face.
e.zh: 你可以裁剪一下照片,把焦点放在她的脸上。

e.en: Floods destroyed thousands of acres of {cropland}.
e.zh: 洪水毁掉了数千英亩的农田。

e.en: Developers want to convert {cropland} into housing.
e.zh: 开发商想把农田改建成住宅。

crinkle.t:
v. 起皱
n. 褶皱

e.en: His eyes {crinkle} at the corners when he smiles.
e.zh: 他笑起来眼角会皱起细纹。

e.en: Don't {crinkle} the wrapping paper before the party starts.
e.zh: 派对开始前别把包装纸弄皱。

e.en: She smoothed the {crinkled} map across the kitchen table.
e.zh: 她把皱巴巴的地图在餐桌上铺平。

e.en: His face {crinkled} into a warm, familiar smile.
e.zh: 他脸上皱起一抹温暖而熟悉的笑容。

e.en: The baby loves toys with {crinkly} fabric inside them.
e.zh: 宝宝喜欢里面有沙沙作响布料的玩具。

e.en: Grandma's hands felt warm and {crinkly} like old paper.
e.zh: 奶奶的手温暖而满是皱纹,像旧纸一样。

e.en: The bride's gown was supported by a stiff {crinoline} underneath.
e.zh: 新娘礼服下面用硬挺的衬裙撑起。

e.en: Victorian women wore {crinoline} skirts that filled entire doorways.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代女性的衬裙宽得能塞满整个门口。

criollo.t: n. 克里奥罗（人/可可品种）

e.en: This chocolate is made from rare {criollo} cacao beans.
e.zh: 这款巧克力是用稀有的克里奥罗可可豆制成的。

e.en: The {criollo} horse is prized for its endurance and toughness.
e.zh: 克里奥罗马因其耐力和坚韧而备受推崇。

e.en: "{Cripes}, I forgot my wallet at home again!" he muttered.
e.zh: “天哪,我又把钱包忘在家里了!”他嘟囔道。

e.en: {Cripes}, that movie was way scarier than I expected.
e.zh: 我的天,那部电影比我预想的吓人多了。

cripple.t:
v. 使残疾、严重损害
n. 跛子（冒犯用法）

e.en: The cyberattack could {cripple} the entire banking system overnight.
e.zh: 这次网络攻击可能一夜之间瘫痪整个银行系统。

e.en: Heavy sanctions {cripple} the country's already fragile economy.
e.zh: 严厉的制裁使该国本已脆弱的经济陷入瘫痪。

e.en: The hurricane {crippled} the island's power grid for weeks.
e.zh: 飓风使该岛的电网瘫痪了数周。

e.en: Software bugs {crippled} the launch of the new app.
e.zh: 软件漏洞使新应用的发布陷入瘫痪。

cripples.t: v. 使残疾（cripple 的三单）

e.en: Inflation {cripples} families trying to afford basic groceries.
e.zh: 通胀让那些勉强买得起日用品的家庭不堪重负。

e.en: A single bug sometimes {cripples} an entire production server.
e.zh: 一个小漏洞有时就能让整个生产服务器瘫痪。

crippling.t:
adj. 造成严重损害的
v. 使残疾（进行式）

e.en: Many graduates struggle with {crippling} student loan debt.
e.zh: 许多毕业生背负着压得喘不过气的学生贷款。

e.en: She suffers from {crippling} anxiety before every public talk.
e.zh: 每次公开演讲前她都被严重焦虑困扰。

e.en: The government has handled three major {crises} this year.
e.zh: 政府今年已经应对了三次重大危机。

e.en: Climate {crises} are now a regular feature of global news.
e.zh: 气候危机如今已是全球新闻的常态话题。

e.en: The company is facing a serious financial {crisis} this quarter.
e.zh: 公司本季度正面临严重的财务危机。

e.en: She had a midlife {crisis} and bought a motorcycle.
e.zh: 她中年危机发作,买了一辆摩托车。

crisp.t:
adj. 酥脆的、清爽的
n. 薯片（英式）

e.en: The morning air felt {crisp} and clean after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后清晨的空气清新而凉爽。

e.en: She bit into the {crisp}, juicy apple with delight.
e.zh: 她兴致勃勃地咬了一口又脆又多汁的苹果。

e.en: I had {crispbread} with cheese and tomato for breakfast.
e.zh: 我早餐吃了脆面包配奶酪和番茄。

e.en: Swedish {crispbread} stays fresh for months in a sealed tin.
e.zh: 瑞典脆面包在密封铁罐里能保鲜数月。

crisped.t:
adj. 烤脆的
v. 使变脆（过去式）

e.en: The bacon {crisped} nicely in the hot cast-iron pan.
e.zh: 培根在烧热的铸铁锅里煎得焦脆。

e.en: Autumn leaves {crisped} underfoot as we walked through the park.
e.zh: 我们走过公园时,秋叶在脚下嘎吱作响。

e.en: These fries taste much {crispier} than yesterday's batch.
e.zh: 这些薯条比昨天那批要脆得多。

e.en: Air frying makes the chicken skin {crispier} without extra oil.
e.zh: 用空气炸锅能让鸡皮更脆，还不用加油。

e.en: The manager spoke {crisply} and ended the meeting early.
e.zh: 经理说话干脆利落，会议提前结束了。

e.en: Her white shirt was ironed {crisply} for the interview.
e.zh: 她的白衬衫为面试熨得笔挺。

e.en: I love the {crispness} of fresh apples in autumn.
e.zh: 我喜欢秋天新鲜苹果的爽脆口感。

e.en: The photo's {crispness} really shows off the new camera.
e.zh: 这张照片的清晰度充分展现了新相机的实力。

e.en: He grabbed a bag of cheese {crisps} from the shelf.
e.zh: 他从货架上抓了一包奶酪味薯片。

e.en: British {crisps} come in some very unusual flavors.
e.zh: 英国的薯片有许多非常奇特的口味。

e.en: This pizza crust is perfectly {crispy} on the bottom.
e.zh: 这块披萨的底部酥脆得恰到好处。

e.en: I prefer my bacon really {crispy} in the morning.
e.zh: 我早上喜欢吃特别脆的培根。

crisscross.t:
v. 纵横交错
adj. 十字形的

e.en: Hiking trails {crisscross} the entire national park.
e.zh: 徒步小道纵横交错地遍布整个国家公园。

e.en: She drew a {crisscross} pattern on top of the pie.
e.zh: 她在派的顶部划出了交叉的花纹。

e.en: Power lines {crisscrossed} the sky above the old town.
e.zh: 电线在老城区上空纵横交错。

e.en: He has {crisscrossed} the country promoting his book.
e.zh: 他为推广新书已经走遍了全国各地。

e.en: The {Cristo} statue towers over Rio de Janeiro.
e.zh: 基督像高耸地俯瞰着里约热内卢。

e.en: Tourists climb the hill to photograph the famous {Cristo}.
e.zh: 游客们爬上山去拍那座著名的基督像。

crit.t:
n. 暴击（游戏）
n. 评论（critique 缩写）

e.en: My character landed a {crit} and finished the boss off.
e.zh: 我的角色打出了暴击，把 BOSS 解决了。

e.en: The team had a quick design {crit} after lunch.
e.zh: 午饭后团队进行了一次简短的设计评审。

criteria.t: n. 标准、准则（criterion 的复数）

e.en: Applicants must meet all the {criteria} listed online.
e.zh: 申请人必须满足网上列出的所有条件。

e.en: What {criteria} did you use to pick the winner?
e.zh: 你是按照什么标准挑出获胜者的？

e.en: Speed is a {criterial} feature when ranking these laptops.
e.zh: 在给这些笔记本排名时，速度是关键的衡量特征。

e.en: The study identified three {criterial} attributes for diagnosis.
e.zh: 该研究确定了三个用于诊断的关键属性。

e.en: Cost is just one {criterion} we use to compare vendors.
e.zh: 成本只是我们比较供应商时使用的一个标准。

e.en: Originality was the main {criterion} for the writing prize.
e.zh: 原创性是这个写作奖项的主要评判标准。

e.en: The film {critic} praised the movie's bold visuals.
e.zh: 那位影评人称赞了这部电影大胆的视觉风格。

e.en: He's his own harshest {critic} when it comes to coding.
e.zh: 在编程方面，他对自己最为苛刻。

e.en: Backups are {critical} before upgrading the database.
e.zh: 在升级数据库之前备份至关重要。

e.en: Reviewers were {critical} of the app's confusing interface.
e.zh: 评测者对这款应用混乱的界面颇有微词。

e.en: Engineers ranked each bug by its {criticality} to launch.
e.zh: 工程师按每个漏洞对发布的紧要程度进行了排序。

e.en: The reactor reached {criticality} during the morning test.
e.zh: 反应堆在上午的测试中达到了临界状态。

e.en: Two passengers were {critically} injured in the crash.
e.zh: 事故中有两名乘客伤势危急。

e.en: Students learn to read sources {critically} in this course.
e.zh: 学生们在这门课上学会批判性地阅读资料。

criticise.t: v. 批评、评论（英式拼法）

e.en: It's easy to {criticise} a plan without offering alternatives.
e.zh: 批评一个方案容易，提出替代方案却很难。

e.en: Voters {criticise} the mayor for ignoring local concerns.
e.zh: 选民批评市长忽视了本地居民的诉求。

e.en: The journalist was {criticised} for publishing the leaked memo.
e.zh: 那位记者因发表泄露的备忘录而受到批评。

e.en: Critics {criticised} the sequel for lacking original ideas.
e.zh: 评论家批评续集缺乏新颖的创意。

e.en: My boss {criticises} every draft before approving it.
e.zh: 我老板在批准之前会挑剔每一份草稿。

e.en: The op-ed {criticises} the new policy for being too vague.
e.zh: 那篇评论文章批评新政策过于模糊。

e.en: Stop {criticising} the chef and try cooking yourself.
e.zh: 别再挑剔厨师了，自己来做做看吧。

e.en: She avoided {criticising} her teammate during the meeting.
e.zh: 她在会议上避免批评自己的队友。

e.en: He took the {criticism} well and improved his draft.
e.zh: 他坦然接受了批评并改进了草稿。

e.en: The proposal drew heavy {criticism} from local residents.
e.zh: 该提案招致了当地居民的强烈批评。

e.en: The report addressed several {criticisms} raised by users.
e.zh: 报告回应了用户提出的几项批评。

e.en: Her main {criticisms} focused on the messy code structure.
e.zh: 她的主要批评集中在混乱的代码结构上。

e.en: Don't {criticize} the design before reading the brief.
e.zh: 在阅读说明之前别急着批评这个设计。

e.en: Voters tend to {criticize} politicians for broken promises.
e.zh: 选民往往会批评政客违背承诺。

e.en: The CEO was {criticized} for laying off staff via email.
e.zh: CEO 因通过邮件裁员而受到批评。

e.en: Many readers {criticized} the ending of the novel online.
e.zh: 许多读者在网上批评了这部小说的结局。

e.en: The article {criticizes} the company's environmental record.
e.zh: 这篇文章批评了该公司的环保记录。

e.en: He rarely {criticizes} others without offering a solution.
e.zh: 他很少在不给出解决方案的情况下批评别人。

e.en: She kept {criticizing} the user interface during the demo.
e.zh: 演示过程中她一直在挑剔用户界面的问题。

e.en: Try giving feedback instead of just {criticizing} the team.
e.zh: 试着给出反馈，而不是一味地批评团队。

e.en: {Critics} loved the show's witty dialogue and pacing.
e.zh: 评论家们喜爱这部剧机智的对白和节奏。

e.en: The policy has its {critics} on both sides of the aisle.
e.zh: 这项政策在两党中都有反对者。

critique.t:
n. 评论、评析
v. 评论、评析

e.en: Could you {critique} my essay before I submit it?
e.zh: 你能在我提交前帮我点评一下论文吗？

e.en: His {critique} of the paper was thorough and fair.
e.zh: 他对那篇论文的评析既透彻又公允。

critiques.t:
n. 评论（复数）
v. 评论（三单）

e.en: The professor offered detailed {critiques} of every project.
e.zh: 教授对每个项目都给出了详细的点评。

e.en: This blog {critiques} new restaurants every Friday.
e.zh: 这个博客每周五都会评测新开的餐厅。

crouching.t: v. 蹲下；蹲伏（crouch 的现在分词）

e.en: A {crouching} tiger waited silently in the tall grass.
e.zh: 一只蹲伏的老虎静静地藏在高高的草丛中。

e.en: He noticed someone {crouching} near the fence at midnight.
e.zh: 半夜他注意到有人蹲在篱笆旁边。

croup.t:
n. 哮吼（儿童喉部疾病）
n. (马的) 臀部

e.en: Our toddler woke up with a barking {croup} cough.
e.zh: 我们家小孩半夜醒来,咳嗽声像哮吼一样。

e.en: Steam from a hot shower can ease {croup} symptoms.
e.zh: 热水淋浴产生的蒸汽能缓解哮吼症状。

e.en: The {croupier} dealt the cards with practiced speed.
e.zh: 荷官以娴熟的速度发着牌。

e.en: A polite {croupier} explained the rules to the new player.
e.zh: 一位礼貌的荷官向新玩家解释了规则。

crouton.t: n. 油煎面包丁（加在汤或沙拉上）

e.en: She topped the Caesar salad with a crispy garlic {crouton}.
e.zh: 她在凯撒沙拉上撒了一块香脆的蒜味面包丁。

e.en: Each {crouton} added a satisfying crunch to the soup.
e.zh: 每一块面包丁都为汤增添了令人满足的脆感。

crow.t:
n. 乌鸦
v. (公鸡) 啼叫；自夸

e.en: A noisy {crow} kept circling above the parking lot.
e.zh: 一只聒噪的乌鸦不停地在停车场上空盘旋。

e.en: Don't {crow} about your win until the season ends.
e.zh: 赛季结束前别急着炫耀你的胜利。

e.en: He used a {crowbar} to pry open the rusted crate.
e.zh: 他用撬棍把生锈的箱子撬开了。

e.en: Keep a small {crowbar} in the trunk for emergencies.
e.zh: 在后备箱里放一根小撬棍以备不时之需。

crowd.t:
n. 人群
v. 挤满；聚集

e.en: A huge {crowd} gathered outside the stadium before kickoff.
e.zh: 开球前一大群人聚集在体育场外。

e.en: Don't {crowd} the doorway when people are trying to exit.
e.zh: 别人要出去的时候,不要堵在门口。

e.en: The subway is always {crowded} during rush hour.
e.zh: 地铁在高峰时段总是挤得水泄不通。

e.en: We left the {crowded} café and found a quieter spot.
e.zh: 我们离开了拥挤的咖啡馆,找了个安静的地方。

crowding.t:
n. 拥挤；聚集
v. 挤 (crowd 的现在分词)

e.en: Fans were {crowding} around the singer for autographs.
e.zh: 粉丝们围在歌手身边索要签名。

e.en: Overpopulation is {crowding} the city's public transit system.
e.zh: 人口过剩让这座城市的公共交通系统不堪重负。

e.en: Huge {crowds} lined the streets to watch the parade.
e.zh: 大批人群挤在街道两旁观看游行。

e.en: This little café {crowds} up quickly on weekend mornings.
e.zh: 这家小咖啡馆周末早上很快就会挤满人。

crowing.t: v. (公鸡) 啼叫；得意地炫耀

e.en: A rooster's {crowing} woke me up before sunrise.
e.zh: 一只公鸡的啼叫在日出前把我吵醒了。

e.en: Stop {crowing} about the promotion and get back to work.
e.zh: 别再为升职得意了,回去干活吧。

crown.t:
n. 王冠；皇冠
v. 加冕；使圆满

e.en: The queen wore a jeweled gold {crown} at the ceremony.
e.zh: 女王在典礼上戴着一顶镶宝石的金王冠。

e.en: My dentist needs to put a {crown} on my back tooth.
e.zh: 牙医需要给我的后槽牙装一个牙冠。

crowned.t:
adj. 戴王冠的
v. 加冕 (crown 的过去式)

e.en: She was {crowned} champion after a thrilling final match.
e.zh: 在惊心动魄的决赛后,她被加冕为冠军。

e.en: Snow {crowned} the mountain peaks throughout the winter.
e.zh: 整个冬天,山峰都被白雪覆盖着。

crowning.t:
adj. 最高的；圆满的
n. 加冕

e.en: Winning the Nobel Prize was the {crowning} moment of her career.
e.zh: 获得诺贝尔奖是她职业生涯最辉煌的时刻。

e.en: The {crowning} ceremony was broadcast to millions worldwide.
e.zh: 加冕典礼向全球数百万人直播。

e.en: Several royal {crowns} are displayed at the Tower of London.
e.zh: 伦敦塔里展出着好几顶皇室王冠。

e.en: A skilled dentist {crowns} damaged teeth to restore their function.
e.zh: 熟练的牙医会给受损的牙齿装牙冠以恢复功能。

e.en: A flock of {crows} settled noisily on the rooftop.
e.zh: 一群乌鸦吵闹地落在屋顶上。

e.en: He {crows} about his fishing skills every chance he gets.
e.zh: 他一有机会就吹嘘自己的钓鱼技术。

croydon.t: n. 克罗伊登（伦敦南部地区）

e.en: The train from London Bridge to {Croydon} takes fifteen minutes.
e.zh: 从伦敦桥到克罗伊登的火车需要十五分钟。

e.en: She grew up in {Croydon} before moving to central London.
e.zh: 她在克罗伊登长大,后来搬到了伦敦市中心。

crozier.t: n. 主教牧杖（弯头手杖）

e.en: The bishop carried an ornate silver {crozier} during the procession.
e.zh: 主教在游行中手持一根华丽的银制权杖。

e.en: His ceremonial {crozier} symbolized his pastoral authority over the diocese.
e.zh: 他的礼仪权杖象征着他对教区的牧灵权威。

crp.t: n. C 反应蛋白（C-reactive protein 缩写）

e.en: The doctor ordered a {CRP} test to check for inflammation.
e.zh: 医生开了C反应蛋白检测以查看炎症情况。

e.en: His {CRP} levels dropped after a week of antibiotics.
e.zh: 服用一周抗生素后,他的C反应蛋白水平下降了。

crs.t: n. 共同申报准则（税务信息交换）

e.en: Banks must report foreign account holders under {CRS} regulations.
e.zh: 根据共同申报准则的规定,银行必须申报外国账户持有人信息。

e.en: The {CRS} framework helps governments combat international tax evasion.
e.zh: 共同申报准则框架帮助各国政府打击国际逃税行为。

crt.t: n. 阴极射线管（旧式显示器）

e.en: Old televisions used heavy {CRT} screens before LCDs took over.
e.zh: 在液晶屏取代之前,老电视用的是笨重的阴极射线管屏幕。

e.en: Retro gamers still prefer playing classics on a {CRT} monitor.
e.zh: 复古游戏玩家仍然喜欢在阴极射线管显示器上玩经典游戏。

cru.t: n. (法国) 葡萄园；酒庄等级

e.en: This bottle is from a famous Burgundy grand {cru} vineyard.
e.zh: 这瓶酒来自勃艮第一座著名的特级园。

e.en: Wine collectors pay premium prices for premier {cru} vintages.
e.zh: 酒类收藏家愿意为一级园年份酒支付高价。

crucial.t: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的

e.en: Sleep is {crucial} for memory and emotional health.
e.zh: 睡眠对记忆力和情绪健康至关重要。

e.en: Backing up your data is {crucial} before updating the system.
e.zh: 更新系统前备份数据是至关重要的。

crucially.t: adv. 至关重要地；关键地

e.en: The new policy, {crucially}, applies to all employees equally.
e.zh: 关键的是,新政策对所有员工一视同仁。

e.en: His decision will {crucially} affect the project's outcome.
e.zh: 他的决定将对项目结果产生关键性影响。

cruciate.t: adj. 十字形的（多用于韧带）

e.en: The athlete tore his anterior {cruciate} ligament during the match.
e.zh: 那位运动员在比赛中撕裂了前交叉韧带。

e.en: Recovery from {cruciate} surgery typically takes six to nine months.
e.zh: 交叉韧带手术后康复通常需要六到九个月。

crucible.t:
n. 坩埚
n. 严峻考验

e.en: War has often been called the {crucible} of national identity.
e.zh: 战争常被称为国家认同的熔炉。

e.en: The chemist heated the mixture in a ceramic {crucible}.
e.zh: 化学家在陶瓷坩埚里加热了混合物。

cruciferous.t: adj. 十字花科的（如花椰菜、西兰花）

e.en: Broccoli and kale are nutritious {cruciferous} vegetables.
e.zh: 西兰花和羽衣甘蓝都是营养丰富的十字花科蔬菜。

e.en: Doctors recommend eating {cruciferous} vegetables to lower cancer risk.
e.zh: 医生建议多吃十字花科蔬菜以降低患癌风险。

crucified.t: v. 钉死在十字架上 (crucify 的过去式)

e.en: The media {crucified} the politician for his careless remarks.
e.zh: 媒体因那位政客不当的言论对他大加抨击。

e.en: Romans {crucified} thousands of rebels along the ancient roads.
e.zh: 罗马人在古道沿线把数千名反叛者钉上十字架。

crucifix.t: n. 耶稣受难像；十字苦像

e.en: A small wooden {crucifix} hung above her bedroom door.
e.zh: 她卧室门上方挂着一个小小的木制十字架。

e.en: The priest blessed the silver {crucifix} before the ceremony.
e.zh: 神父在仪式前为银十字架祝圣。

crucifixion.t: n. 钉十字架刑；耶稣受难

e.en: The painting depicts the {crucifixion} in vivid, unsettling detail.
e.zh: 那幅画以生动而令人不安的细节描绘了耶稣受难。

e.en: Easter commemorates the {crucifixion} and resurrection of Jesus.
e.zh: 复活节是为了纪念耶稣的受难与复活。

e.en: The medieval cathedral has a classic {cruciform} floor plan.
e.zh: 这座中世纪大教堂有典型的十字形平面布局。

e.en: Archaeologists found a {cruciform} pendant in the old grave.
e.zh: 考古学家在古墓中发现了一枚十字形吊坠。

crucify.t: v. 把…钉在十字架上；严厉折磨

e.en: Critics will {crucify} the movie if the ending disappoints fans.
e.zh: 如果结局让粉丝失望,影评人会狠狠抨击这部电影。

e.en: Don't {crucify} yourself over one small mistake at work.
e.zh: 别为工作上一个小错误苛责自己。

e.en: Wipe the {crud} off the stove before cooking dinner.
e.zh: 做晚饭前把炉子上的污垢擦干净。

e.en: Most messages in my inbox are just marketing {crud}.
e.zh: 我邮箱里大多数邮件都是营销垃圾信息。

cruddy.t: adj. 肮脏的；糟糕的（俚语）

e.en: I felt {cruddy} all weekend because of a bad cold.
e.zh: 因为重感冒,我整个周末都觉得难受。

e.en: Don't buy that {cruddy} charger; it broke within a week.
e.zh: 别买那个劣质充电器,一周内就坏了。

crude.t:
adj. 粗糙的；粗鲁的
n. 原油

e.en: The price of {crude} oil rose sharply after the announcement.
e.zh: 消息公布后原油价格大幅上涨。

e.en: His {crude} jokes made everyone at the table uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他粗俗的玩笑让餐桌上每个人都不自在。

e.en: The map was {crudely} drawn on a napkin in pencil.
e.zh: 那张地图是用铅笔粗略地画在餐巾纸上的。

e.en: He {crudely} interrupted the speaker during her presentation.
e.zh: 他在演讲者讲话时粗鲁地打断了她。

e.en: The {crudeness} of his joke offended several guests.
e.zh: 他笑话的粗俗冒犯了好几位客人。

e.en: Critics noted the {crudeness} of the early prototype.
e.zh: 评论者指出了早期原型的粗糙。

crudites.t: n. 生蔬菜拼盘（法式开胃菜）

e.en: She served {crudites} with hummus before dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐前她端上了生菜拼盘配鹰嘴豆泥。

e.en: A platter of {crudites} sat in the middle of the table.
e.zh: 一盘生鲜蔬菜摆在桌子中央。

e.en: The film was criticized for its {crudity} and shallow humor.
e.zh: 这部电影因粗俗和肤浅的幽默而受到批评。

e.en: Despite its {crudity}, the sketch captured her likeness.
e.zh: 尽管粗糙,这幅速写还是捕捉到了她的神韵。

e.en: It is {cruel} to leave a dog tied up all day.
e.zh: 把狗整天拴着是很残忍的。

e.en: The job market has been {cruel} to new graduates.
e.zh: 就业市场对应届毕业生十分残酷。

e.en: He was {cruelly} mocked by his classmates online.
e.zh: 他在网上被同学们残忍地嘲笑。

e.en: Her hopes were {cruelly} dashed at the last moment.
e.zh: 她的希望在最后一刻被残酷地击碎。

cruelties.t: n. 残忍行径（cruelty 的复数）

e.en: The documentary exposed the {cruelties} of factory farming.
e.zh: 这部纪录片揭露了工厂化养殖的种种残忍行径。

e.en: History records the {cruelties} inflicted during the war.
e.zh: 史书记载了战争期间施加的种种暴行。

e.en: Animal {cruelty} is punishable by law in most countries.
e.zh: 虐待动物在大多数国家都要受到法律制裁。

e.en: She could not believe the {cruelty} of his words.
e.zh: 她无法相信他话里的那种残忍。

e.en: Pass me the {cruet} of olive oil, please.
e.zh: 请把那瓶橄榄油递给我。

e.en: A small glass {cruet} held the vinegar.
e.zh: 一只小玻璃调味瓶里装着醋。

crufts.t: n. 克鲁夫茨（英国知名犬展）

e.en: Their poodle won best in show at {Crufts}.
e.zh: 他们的贵宾犬在克鲁夫茨犬展上获得了全场总冠军。

e.en: Thousands of dog lovers attend {Crufts} each year.
e.zh: 每年都有成千上万的爱狗人士参加克鲁夫茨犬展。

cruise.t:
v. 巡航；乘船游览
n. 游轮旅行

e.en: They booked a {cruise} around the Mediterranean.
e.zh: 他们预订了一趟地中海邮轮之旅。

e.en: The car can {cruise} comfortably at highway speeds.
e.zh: 这辆车可以在高速路上轻松巡航。

cruised.t: v. 巡航；游弋 (cruise 的过去式)

e.en: We {cruised} along the coast for two weeks.
e.zh: 我们沿着海岸巡游了两周。

e.en: The team {cruised} to victory in the final.
e.zh: 球队在决赛中轻松取胜。

cruiser.t:
n. 巡洋舰
n. 游艇；巡逻车

e.en: A police {cruiser} pulled up behind us.
e.zh: 一辆警车停在了我们后面。

e.en: He restored an old motorcycle into a sleek {cruiser}.
e.zh: 他把一辆旧摩托车改装成了一辆流畅的巡航车。

cropped.t:
adj. 裁剪过的（图片、视频）
v. crop 的过去式

e.en: She {cropped} her hair short for the summer.
e.zh: 她为了过夏天把头发剪短了。

e.en: I {cropped} the screenshot before sharing it online.
e.zh: 我把截图裁剪了一下才分享到网上。

e.en: He came a {cropper} trying to ride the new bike.
e.zh: 他想骑那辆新车,结果摔了个大跟头。

e.en: The startup came a {cropper} after losing its main client.
e.zh: 那家初创公司失去主要客户后一败涂地。

cropping.t:
n. 裁剪（图像）
v. crop 的现在分词

e.en: The app makes {cropping} photos really easy.
e.zh: 这款应用让裁剪照片变得非常简单。

e.en: Crop rotation prevents soil exhaustion from continuous {cropping}.
e.zh: 轮作可以防止连作种植造成土壤贫瘠。

crops.t:
n. 农作物
v. 裁剪（第三人称单数）

e.en: Drought has devastated this year's {crops}.
e.zh: 干旱毁掉了今年的庄稼。

e.en: Farmers plant different {crops} to protect the soil.
e.zh: 农民们种植不同的作物以保护土壤。

e.en: They played {croquet} on the lawn all afternoon.
e.zh: 他们在草坪上玩了一下午槌球。

e.en: Grandpa keeps a vintage {croquet} set in the shed.
e.zh: 爷爷在棚子里收着一套老式的槌球用具。

e.en: I ordered a potato {croquette} as a side dish.
e.zh: 我点了一个土豆可乐饼当配菜。

e.en: Each crispy {croquette} was filled with melted cheese.
e.zh: 每一个酥脆的可乐饼里都包着融化的奶酪。

crosby.t: n. 克罗斯比（姓氏/地名）

e.en: Bing {Crosby} sang the most famous version of White Christmas.
e.zh: 宾·克罗斯比演唱了最著名的《白色圣诞》版本。

e.en: Sidney {Crosby} led the Penguins to multiple Stanley Cups.
e.zh: 西德尼·克罗斯比率领企鹅队多次夺得斯坦利杯。

e.en: The bishop carried an ornate {crosier} during the procession.
e.zh: 主教在游行中持着一根华丽的牧杖。

e.en: A golden {crosier} symbolizes pastoral authority in the church.
e.zh: 金色的牧杖象征着教会中的牧职权威。

cross.t:
v. 穿过，交叉
n. 十字，十字架

e.en: Look both ways before you {cross} the street.
e.zh: 过马路前要左右看看。

e.en: Mom got really {cross} when I came home late.
e.zh: 我回家晚了,妈妈非常生气。

e.en: His shot hit the {crossbar} and bounced out.
e.zh: 他的射门击中横梁后弹了出来。

e.en: She adjusted the {crossbar} on her bicycle frame.
e.zh: 她调整了一下自行车车架上的横梁。

e.en: A heavy oak {crossbeam} supported the cottage roof.
e.zh: 一根粗重的橡木横梁支撑着小屋的屋顶。

e.en: Workers replaced the rotting {crossbeam} in the barn.
e.zh: 工人们更换了谷仓里腐烂的横梁。

crossbones.t: n. 交叉骨（常与骷髅一起出现）

e.en: The pirate flag showed a skull and {crossbones}.
e.zh: 那面海盗旗上画着骷髅和交叉的骨头。

e.en: A skull and {crossbones} warned of poison inside.
e.zh: 骷髅交叉骨标志警示里面是毒物。

e.en: The hunter carried a modern {crossbow} into the woods.
e.zh: 猎人带着一把现代弩进了树林。

e.en: Medieval soldiers feared the deadly accuracy of the {crossbow}.
e.zh: 中世纪的士兵畏惧弩弓那种致命的精准度。

e.en: The {crossbowman} took aim from behind the castle wall.
e.zh: 那名弩手从城墙后瞄准目标。

e.en: A skilled {crossbowman} could pierce armor at a distance.
e.zh: 技艺高超的弩手能远距离穿透铠甲。

crossbreed.t:
v. 使杂交
n. 杂交品种

e.en: Farmers {crossbreed} cattle to improve milk yields.
e.zh: 农民通过杂交牛只来提高产奶量。

e.en: Her dog is a {crossbreed} of poodle and retriever.
e.zh: 她的狗是贵宾犬和寻回犬的杂交品种。

e.en: {Crossbreeding} has produced hardier varieties of wheat.
e.zh: 杂交育种培育出了更耐寒的小麦品种。

e.en: Selective {crossbreeding} can introduce new traits over generations.
e.zh: 选择性杂交可以经过几代培育出新性状。

e.en: A strong {crosscurrent} pulled the swimmer off course.
e.zh: 一股强劲的横流把游泳者冲离了航线。

e.en: There were political {crosscurrent} pressures shaping the debate.
e.zh: 各种政治逆流相互交织,影响着这场辩论。

crosscut.t:
v. 横切
n. 横切面；交叉剪辑

e.en: Use a {crosscut} saw to slice the log cleanly.
e.zh: 用横切锯把这段木头切得整整齐齐。

e.en: The director used a {crosscut} between two parallel scenes.
e.zh: 导演在两个平行场景之间使用了交叉剪辑。

crossed.t:
adj. 交叉的
v. cross 的过去式

e.en: She {crossed} her arms and refused to answer.
e.zh: 她抱起双臂,拒绝回答。

e.en: We {crossed} the border into France around midnight.
e.zh: 我们大约在午夜越过边境进入法国。

crosses.t:
n. 十字（复数）
v. 穿过（第三人称单数）

e.en: The bus {crosses} the bridge every fifteen minutes.
e.zh: 那班公交车每十五分钟过一次桥。

e.en: Wooden {crosses} marked the graves in the small cemetery.
e.zh: 小墓地里的坟墓上插着木制十字架。

crossfire.t: n. 交叉火力；激烈争辩

e.en: Civilians were caught in the {crossfire} between rival gangs.
e.zh: 平民被卷入了敌对帮派之间的交火中。

e.en: The new policy put teachers in the political {crossfire}.
e.zh: 这项新政策把教师们卷入了政治交锋的夹缝。

e.en: He centered the {crosshair} on the distant target.
e.zh: 他将十字准星对准了远处的目标。

e.en: Move the {crosshair} cursor to select your unit.
e.zh: 移动十字准星光标来选择你的单位。

e.en: The CEO has been in regulators' {crosshairs} for months.
e.zh: 那位首席执行官几个月来一直是监管机构的目标。

e.en: He lined the deer up in his rifle's {crosshairs}.
e.zh: 他把那只鹿对准在步枪的十字准星里。

crosshatch.t:
v. 画交叉阴影线
n. 交叉网格

e.en: Artists {crosshatch} pencil lines to create darker shadows.
e.zh: 画家用交叉影线来表现更深的阴影。

e.en: The tattoo featured a delicate {crosshatch} pattern.
e.zh: 那个纹身有着精致的交叉网纹图案。

crosshead.t: n. 十字头（机械）；小标题

e.en: Each section begins with a bold {crosshead} for clarity.
e.zh: 每个部分都以醒目的小标题开头,以便阅读。

e.en: The editor added a {crosshead} every few paragraphs.
e.zh: 编辑每隔几段就加上一个分节小标题。

crossing.t:
n. 交叉路口，横穿
v. 穿过（进行时）

e.en: Wait for the green light at the pedestrian {crossing}.
e.zh: 在人行横道处等绿灯再走。

e.en: The ferry {crossing} took about two hours.
e.zh: 渡轮横渡大约花了两个小时。

crossings.t: n. 交叉口，横穿处（复数）

e.en: There are several safe {crossings} along this highway.
e.zh: 这条公路沿线有几处安全的横道口。

e.en: Border {crossings} were closed during the emergency.
e.zh: 紧急状态期间各边境口岸都被关闭了。

e.en: "Stop interrupting me," she said {crossly}.
e.zh: “别打断我,”她生气地说道。

e.en: The teacher glared {crossly} at the noisy students.
e.zh: 老师怒气冲冲地瞪着吵闹的学生。

crossover.t:
n. 跨界，交叉（音乐、文化）
adj. 跨界的

e.en: The song became a huge {crossover} hit on pop charts.
e.zh: 这首歌在流行榜上跨界大热。

e.en: She drives a compact {crossover} SUV to work.
e.zh: 她开一辆紧凑型跨界SUV上班。

e.en: The chair's wooden {crosspiece} had cracked over time.
e.zh: 椅子的木制横档已经随着时间裂开了。

e.en: He nailed a {crosspiece} between the two posts.
e.zh: 他在两根柱子之间钉上了一根横档。

e.en: We met at a quiet country {crossroad} just past noon.
e.zh: 我们正午刚过在一个安静的乡村十字路口碰面。

e.en: The old {crossroad} has a small chapel on one corner.
e.zh: 那个老十字路口的一角有座小教堂。

crossroads.t: n. 十字路口；关键抉择时刻

e.en: Her career is at a {crossroads} after the company merger.
e.zh: 公司合并后,她的事业正处于十字路口。

e.en: Turn left at the {crossroads} and follow the river road.
e.zh: 在十字路口左转,然后沿着河边的路走。

crosstalk.t: n. 串扰（信号）；相声对白

e.en: There is too much {crosstalk} between the two audio channels.
e.zh: 两个音频通道之间的串音太严重了。

e.en: Witty {crosstalk} between the hosts kept the show entertaining.
e.zh: 主持人之间机智的对话让节目妙趣横生。

e.en: Always look both ways before stepping into the {crosswalk}.
e.zh: 踏上人行横道前,一定要左右看看。

e.en: The driver stopped to let kids use the {crosswalk}.
e.zh: 司机停下车让孩子们走人行横道。

e.en: The hikers paused at the {crossway} to check the map.
e.zh: 徒步者们在交叉路口停下来查看地图。

e.en: A weathered signpost stood at the village {crossway}.
e.zh: 村子的交叉口立着一块风化的路标。

e.en: The pilot landed safely despite a strong {crosswind}.
e.zh: 尽管侧风很强,飞行员还是安全降落了。

e.en: Cyclists struggled against the gusty {crosswind} on the bridge.
e.zh: 骑行者们在桥上与阵阵侧风奋力抗争。

e.en: Slice the carrots {crosswise} into thin rounds.
e.zh: 将胡萝卜横着切成薄圆片。

e.en: Lay the planks {crosswise} over the beams for support.
e.zh: 把木板横搭在梁上以作支撑。

e.en: Grandma does the Sunday {crossword} with her morning coffee.
e.zh: 奶奶喝着晨间咖啡做周日的填字游戏。

e.en: I'm stuck on a tricky {crossword} clue about Greek myths.
e.zh: 我被一道关于希腊神话的填字题难住了。

e.en: These jeans are too tight in the {crotch}.
e.zh: 这条牛仔裤裆部太紧了。

e.en: A nest sat in the {crotch} of the old oak.
e.zh: 老橡树的枝杈处搭着一个鸟窝。

e.en: The composer ended the bar with a single {crotchet}.
e.zh: 作曲家用一个四分音符结束了这一小节。

e.en: Refusing to fly is just one of his odd {crotchet}.
e.zh: 拒绝坐飞机只是他古怪癖好之一。

e.en: The {crotchety} old man yelled at kids on his lawn.
e.zh: 那个脾气古怪的老头冲着草坪上的孩子大喊。

e.en: My grandfather gets {crotchety} when he misses his afternoon nap.
e.zh: 我爷爷没睡午觉就会变得脾气暴躁。

e.en: A bright {croton} plant adds color to my living room.
e.zh: 一株鲜艳的变叶木为我的客厅增添了色彩。

e.en: The {croton} thrives in warm, humid climates with good light.
e.zh: 变叶木在温暖湿润且光照充足的气候里长得很好。

crouch.t:
v. 蹲伏，蜷缩
n. 蹲伏姿势

e.en: The cat began to {crouch} low before pouncing on the toy.
e.zh: 猫扑向玩具前先低身蹲伏起来。

e.en: You should {crouch} down to talk to small children.
e.zh: 和小孩说话时,你应该蹲下身来。

crouched.t:
adj. 蹲伏的
v. crouch 的过去式

e.en: The photographer {crouched} behind a rock to get the shot.
e.zh: 摄影师蹲在石头后面才拍到那张照片。

e.en: She {crouched} beside the puppy and stroked its ears.
e.zh: 她蹲在小狗旁边,抚摸着它的耳朵。

e.en: He won the {cruiserweight} title last weekend.
e.zh: 他上周末赢得了次重量级冠军腰带。

e.en: She trains hard to stay in the {cruiserweight} division.
e.zh: 她刻苦训练以保持在次重量级别参赛。

cruises.t:
v. 巡航；乘船游览
n. 游轮旅行

e.en: Luxury {cruises} have become popular among retirees.
e.zh: 豪华邮轮旅行在退休人群中越来越受欢迎。

e.en: The yacht {cruises} between the islands every summer.
e.zh: 每年夏天这艘游艇都在群岛之间巡游。

cruising.t:
v. 巡航；漫游
n. 乘船旅行

e.en: We spent the afternoon {cruising} down the river.
e.zh: 我们一下午都在沿着河顺流而下。

e.en: She is {cruising} through her exams this semester.
e.zh: 这学期她考试都轻松通过。

e.en: He grabbed a {cruller} and a coffee on the way to work.
e.zh: 上班途中他买了一个麻花甜甜圈和一杯咖啡。

e.en: The bakery's glazed {cruller} sells out by noon.
e.zh: 这家面包店的糖霜麻花圈到中午就卖光了。

e.en: She brushed a {crumb} off her shirt.
e.zh: 她把衬衫上的面包屑拂掉。

e.en: He gave her not even a {crumb} of useful advice.
e.zh: 他没给她一丁点有用的建议。

crumble.t:
v. 弄碎；崩塌
n. 酥皮水果点心

e.en: Old buildings start to {crumble} without maintenance.
e.zh: 老建筑无人维护就会开始崩塌。

e.en: Their relationship began to {crumble} under stress.
e.zh: 他们的感情在压力下开始瓦解。

e.en: The cookie {crumbled} the moment she touched it.
e.zh: 饼干一碰就碎了。

e.en: His confidence {crumbled} after the harsh review.
e.zh: 那篇尖锐的评论让他的自信崩塌了。

crumbles.t:
v. 弄碎；崩塌
n. 碎屑

e.en: This cheese {crumbles} nicely over a salad.
e.zh: 这种奶酪很容易碎着撒在沙拉上。

e.en: She baked apple {crumbles} for the whole family.
e.zh: 她为全家烤了苹果酥。

e.en: They are restoring the {crumbling} stone wall.
e.zh: 他们正在修复那堵摇摇欲坠的石墙。

e.en: The country's {crumbling} infrastructure needs investment.
e.zh: 该国日益破败的基础设施亟需投资。

e.en: The shortbread had a buttery, {crumbly} texture.
e.zh: 这种黄油酥饼口感酥松易碎。

e.en: The soil here is dry and {crumbly}.
e.zh: 这里的土壤干燥而松散。

e.en: Toast left {crumbs} all over the counter.
e.zh: 烤面包在台面上掉了一地碎屑。

e.en: The website uses breadcrumb {crumbs} for navigation.
e.zh: 这个网站用面包屑导航来指引路径。

e.en: I had a {crummy} day at work yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天我上班过得很糟糕。

e.en: They stayed in a {crummy} motel near the highway.
e.zh: 他们住在高速公路边一家很烂的汽车旅馆里。

crump.t:
n. 沉闷的爆炸声
v. 发出爆炸声

e.en: A loud {crump} echoed across the field as the shell landed.
e.zh: 炮弹落地时,一声沉闷的轰响在田野上回荡。

e.en: Boots made a soft {crump} in the fresh snow.
e.zh: 靴子在新雪上发出轻柔的咯吱声。

e.en: He toasted a {crumpet} and slathered it with butter.
e.zh: 他烤了一个英式松饼,涂上厚厚一层黄油。

e.en: Tea and a hot {crumpet} make a perfect afternoon.
e.zh: 一杯茶配一块热松饼就是完美的午后。

e.en: Don't {crumple} the paper before recycling it.
e.zh: 回收前不要把纸揉皱。

e.en: Modern cars {crumple} on impact to absorb energy.
e.zh: 现代汽车在碰撞时会溃缩以吸收能量。

crumpled.t:
adj. 皱巴巴的
v. 被揉皱

e.en: He pulled a {crumpled} receipt from his pocket.
e.zh: 他从口袋里掏出一张皱巴巴的收据。

e.en: She {crumpled} the letter and tossed it away.
e.zh: 她把信揉成一团扔掉了。

crunch.t:
v. 嘎吱咀嚼；紧缩
n. 关键时刻

e.en: The team is in a budget {crunch} this quarter.
e.zh: 本季度团队预算十分紧张。

e.en: I love the {crunch} of fresh apples.
e.zh: 我喜欢咬新鲜苹果时那种脆响。

crunched.t: v. 嘎吱咬碎；处理（数据）

e.en: Our analyst {crunched} the numbers overnight.
e.zh: 我们的分析师连夜处理了那些数据。

e.en: Leaves {crunched} under our boots in the forest.
e.zh: 森林里树叶在我们靴下嘎吱作响。

cruncher.t: n. 处理者；嘎吱咀嚼的东西

e.en: This laptop is a real number {cruncher}.
e.zh: 这台笔记本电脑算力很强,能处理大量数据。

e.en: He's the team's data {cruncher} for every report.
e.zh: 每份报告他都是团队的数据处理担当。

crunching.t: v. 嘎吱咀嚼；处理（大量数据）

e.en: The server is busy {crunching} millions of records.
e.zh: 服务器正忙着处理上百万条记录。

e.en: She kept {crunching} on celery during the meeting.
e.zh: 开会时她一直在咯吱咯吱地嚼芹菜。

e.en: I prefer my peanut butter {crunchy}, not smooth.
e.zh: 我喜欢颗粒口感的花生酱,不要顺滑的。

e.en: The salad had a satisfying {crunchy} topping.
e.zh: 沙拉上有一层口感酥脆的配料,非常满足。

e.en: The anatomy text labels the {crus} of the leg.
e.zh: 解剖学课本上标注出了小腿部位。

e.en: Doctors examined swelling around the patient's {crus}.
e.zh: 医生检查了病人小腿周围的肿胀。

crusade.t:
n. 运动；十字军东征
v. 发起运动

e.en: She launched a {crusade} against single-use plastics.
e.zh: 她发起了一场反对一次性塑料制品的运动。

e.en: The mayor's anti-corruption {crusade} won wide support.
e.zh: 市长的反腐运动赢得了广泛支持。

crusader.t: n. 改革斗士；十字军战士

e.en: He became a {crusader} for affordable housing.
e.zh: 他成了为可负担住房奔走的斗士。

e.en: The journalist was a tireless {crusader} for free speech.
e.zh: 这位记者是不知疲倦的言论自由斗士。

crusading.t:
adj. 讨伐的
v. 发起运动

e.en: She is a {crusading} lawyer who defends asylum seekers.
e.zh: 她是一位为寻求庇护者辩护的斗士律师。

e.en: His {crusading} journalism uncovered widespread fraud.
e.zh: 他充满斗志的新闻报道揭露了大规模欺诈。

crush.t:
n. 迷恋的对象
v. 压碎；压垮

e.en: Don't {crush} the strawberries when you wash them.
e.zh: 洗草莓时别把它们压坏了。

e.en: She had a huge {crush} on her math teacher.
e.zh: 她非常迷恋她的数学老师。

e.en: The recipe calls for two {crushed} garlic cloves.
e.zh: 这道菜需要两瓣压碎的大蒜。

e.en: He was {crushed} when his application was rejected.
e.zh: 申请被拒后他心都碎了。

e.en: The mine uses a giant rock {crusher} to process ore.
e.zh: 矿场用一台巨型碎石机来处理矿石。

e.en: That news was a real soul {crusher}.
e.zh: 那个消息真是让人心灰意冷。

crushes.t:
n. 迷恋
v. 压碎；击垮

e.en: The factory {crushes} aluminum cans for recycling.
e.zh: 这家工厂将铝罐压碎以便回收利用。

e.en: Most childhood {crushes} fade within a few months.
e.zh: 大多数儿时的暗恋几个月内就淡了。

crushing.t: adj. 毁灭性的；压倒性的

e.en: The team suffered a {crushing} defeat in the final.
e.zh: 球队在决赛中惨败。

e.en: Student loans are a {crushing} burden for many.
e.zh: 学生贷款对许多人来说是难以承受的负担。

crushingly.t: adv. 压倒性地；毁灭性地

e.en: The interview went {crushingly} badly for her.
e.zh: 那场面试对她来说糟糕得让人崩溃。

e.en: His memoir is {crushingly} honest about his addiction.
e.zh: 他的回忆录对自己的成瘾问题坦诚得令人心痛。

e.en: The novel reads like a modern Robinson {Crusoe}.
e.zh: 这部小说读起来像是现代版的鲁滨逊漂流记。

e.en: Stranded alone, he felt like {Crusoe} on the island.
e.zh: 独自被困时,他感觉自己就像岛上的鲁滨逊。

e.en: I prefer pizza with a thin, crispy {crust}.
e.zh: 我喜欢薄而脆的披萨饼底。

e.en: Earth's {crust} is constantly shifting beneath our feet.
e.zh: 我们脚下的地壳一直在不断移动。

e.en: Lobsters and crabs belong to the class {Crustacea}.
e.zh: 龙虾和螃蟹都属于甲壳纲。

e.en: Marine biologists study {Crustacea} along the reef.
e.zh: 海洋生物学家在礁石沿岸研究甲壳类动物。

crustacean.t:
n. 甲壳类动物
adj. 甲壳类的

e.en: A shrimp is a small saltwater {crustacean}.
e.zh: 虾是一种小型海水甲壳类动物。

e.en: She's allergic to every {crustacean}, including crab.
e.zh: 她对所有甲壳类动物都过敏,包括螃蟹。

e.en: Geologists measured recent {crustal} movement near the fault.
e.zh: 地质学家测量了断层附近近期的地壳运动。

e.en: Earthquakes release built-up {crustal} stress.
e.zh: 地震会释放积累已久的地壳应力。

crusted.t: adj. 结硬壳的；覆有外壳的

e.en: Snow {crusted} the windshield overnight.
e.zh: 一夜之间雪在挡风玻璃上结了一层硬壳。

e.en: The chef served pepper-{crusted} salmon.
e.zh: 主厨端上了一道黑胡椒脆皮三文鱼。

crustless.t: adj. 去面包皮的；无壳的

e.en: She made {crustless} sandwiches for the children's party.
e.zh: 她为孩子们的派对做了去边的三明治。

e.en: The cafe sells {crustless} quiche slices at lunch.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆午餐时卖无饼底的咸派切片。

crusty.t: adj. 硬皮的；脾气暴躁的

e.en: The bread had a {crusty} golden exterior and soft inside.
e.zh: 这面包外皮金黄酥脆,内里柔软。

e.en: My grandfather is a {crusty} old sailor with great stories.
e.zh: 我爷爷是个脾气倔的老水手,故事可多了。

e.en: He walked with a {crutch} after spraining his ankle.
e.zh: 他扭伤脚踝后拄着拐杖走路。

e.en: Coffee became a {crutch} for surviving long workdays.
e.zh: 咖啡成了他熬过漫长工作日的依赖。

e.en: The {crux} of the argument is whether AI can truly reason.
e.zh: 争论的关键在于 AI 是否真能推理。

e.en: Cost is the {crux} of the matter for most small businesses.
e.zh: 对大多数小企业来说,成本才是问题的核心。

e.en: Senator {Cruz} addressed reporters outside the Capitol.
e.zh: 克鲁兹参议员在国会大厦外回答记者提问。

e.en: We spent the weekend exploring Santa {Cruz} beaches.
e.zh: 我们周末在圣克鲁兹的海滩玩了一整天。

cruzado.t: n. 克鲁扎多（巴西旧货币）

e.en: Brazil introduced the {cruzado} as its currency in 1986.
e.zh: 巴西在 1986 年推出克鲁扎多作为流通货币。

e.en: Inflation quickly eroded the value of the {cruzado}.
e.zh: 通货膨胀很快侵蚀了克鲁扎多的购买力。

cry.t:
v. 哭泣；喊叫
n. 叫喊声

e.en: Don't {cry} over a spilled cup of coffee.
e.zh: 别为打翻一杯咖啡而哭。

e.en: We heard a sudden {cry} for help from the alley.
e.zh: 我们突然听到巷子里传来呼救声。

crybaby.t: n. 爱哭鬼；爱抱怨的人

e.en: Don't be such a {crybaby} about losing one game.
e.zh: 输了一场游戏而已,别这么爱哭。

e.en: His teammates teased him as a {crybaby} after the match.
e.zh: 赛后队友们都笑他是个爱哭鬼。

e.en: The town {cryer} announced the new laws in the square.
e.zh: 镇上的传报员在广场上宣布新法令。

e.en: She's a real {cryer} during sad movies.
e.zh: 看悲情电影时她特别爱哭。

crying.t:
v. 哭泣
adj. 急需的；迫切的

e.en: The baby was {crying} loudly through the night.
e.zh: 婴儿整夜大声啼哭。

e.en: It's a {crying} shame that the café finally closed.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆最终关门了,真是太可惜了。

cryogenic.t: adj. 低温学的；低温冷冻的

e.en: Vaccines are stored at {cryogenic} temperatures for stability.
e.zh: 疫苗在超低温下保存以维持稳定性。

e.en: The lab uses {cryogenic} liquid nitrogen for the experiments.
e.zh: 实验室使用低温液氮进行实验。

e.en: The samples are {cryogenically} frozen for long-term storage.
e.zh: 样本被超低温冷冻以长期保存。

e.en: Some billionaires hope to be {cryogenically} preserved after death.
e.zh: 一些亿万富翁希望死后能被冷冻保存。

cryogenics.t: n. 低温学；低温冷冻技术

e.en: Modern {cryogenics} enables breakthroughs in quantum computing.
e.zh: 现代低温学推动了量子计算的突破。

e.en: She studied {cryogenics} to work on rocket fuel systems.
e.zh: 她研究低温学,以便从事火箭燃料系统的工作。

e.en: The startup offers {cryonic} preservation for a steep fee.
e.zh: 那家初创公司以高昂费用提供人体冷冻保存服务。

e.en: Doubts about {cryonic} suspension remain widespread among scientists.
e.zh: 科学界对人体冷冻技术普遍仍持怀疑态度。

cryonics.t: n. 人体冷冻术（低温保存尸体以待复活）

e.en: {Cryonics} promises to revive frozen patients in the future.
e.zh: 人体冷冻学承诺将来能复活被冷冻的患者。

e.en: He signed up for {cryonics} long before he turned fifty.
e.zh: 他在五十岁之前就报名了人体冷冻服务。

cryopreservation.t: n. 低温保存（生物样本）

e.en: {Cryopreservation} of embryos has become routine in fertility clinics.
e.zh: 胚胎冷冻保存在生育诊所已是常规操作。

e.en: Researchers improved {cryopreservation} methods for rare plant seeds.
e.zh: 研究人员改进了珍稀植物种子的冷冻保存方法。

e.en: The quantum chip sits inside a giant {cryostat}.
e.zh: 量子芯片安装在一台巨大的低温恒温器内。

e.en: Engineers cooled the sample using a helium {cryostat}.
e.zh: 工程师们用氦低温恒温器冷却样品。

e.en: Tourists explored the dark {crypt} beneath the cathedral.
e.zh: 游客们参观了大教堂下方阴暗的地下墓室。

e.en: An old marble tomb sits in the church {crypt}.
e.zh: 教堂的地下墓室里安放着一座古老的大理石墓。

e.en: The {cryptanalyst} broke the enemy's code in just three days.
e.zh: 那位密码分析员仅用三天就破译了敌方密码。

e.en: She works as a {cryptanalyst} for a national security agency.
e.zh: 她在一家国家安全机构担任密码分析员。

cryptic.t: adj. 神秘的、含义隐晦的

e.en: He left a {cryptic} message before disappearing.
e.zh: 他失踪前留下一条令人费解的留言。

e.en: Her tweet was so {cryptic} that fans started guessing.
e.zh: 她的推文太隐晦了,粉丝们都开始猜起来。

e.en: The CEO {cryptically} hinted at major changes ahead.
e.zh: 首席执行官隐晦地暗示了即将到来的重大变化。

e.en: He answered {cryptically}, refusing to confirm any details.
e.zh: 他回答得含糊其辞,拒绝证实任何细节。

e.en: The puzzle book includes a tricky {cryptogram} on every page.
e.zh: 这本谜题书每一页都有一道棘手的密码谜题。

e.en: She solved the {cryptogram} hidden in the museum exhibit.
e.zh: 她破解了博物馆展品中隐藏的密码。

e.en: The {cryptographer} designed an algorithm resistant to quantum attacks.
e.zh: 那位密码学家设计了一种能抵御量子攻击的算法。

e.en: She trained as a {cryptographer} after studying pure mathematics.
e.zh: 她在学习纯数学之后成为了一名密码学家。

e.en: Modern messaging apps rely on strong {cryptographic} protocols.
e.zh: 现代聊天应用依赖强大的加密协议。

e.en: The wallet uses a {cryptographic} signature to verify transactions.
e.zh: 该钱包使用加密签名来验证交易。

e.en: Public-key {cryptography} secures most internet traffic today.
e.zh: 公钥密码学保护着当今大多数的互联网流量。

e.en: He took a course in {cryptography} during his master's program.
e.zh: 他在硕士课程中选修了一门密码学。

e.en: {Cryptology} combines mathematics, computer science, and linguistics.
e.zh: 密码学结合了数学、计算机科学和语言学。

e.en: She wrote her thesis on the history of {cryptology}.
e.zh: 她的论文写的是密码学的历史。

e.en: {Cryptosporidiosis} can spread quickly through contaminated drinking water.
e.zh: 隐孢子虫病可通过受污染的饮用水迅速传播。

e.en: The outbreak of {cryptosporidiosis} sickened hundreds of swimmers.
e.zh: 这次隐孢子虫病暴发使数百名游泳者感染发病。

e.en: Tests revealed {cryptosporidium} in the city's water supply.
e.zh: 检测在城市供水中发现了隐孢子虫。

e.en: {Cryptosporidium} is highly resistant to standard chlorine disinfection.
e.zh: 隐孢子虫对常规氯消毒具有很强的抵抗力。

crystal.t:
n. 水晶；晶体
adj. 清澈的

e.en: The instructions were {crystal} clear from the start.
e.zh: 说明从一开始就一清二楚。

e.en: She admired the snowflake's delicate {crystal} structure under the lens.
e.zh: 她在镜头下欣赏雪花精致的晶体结构。

crystalize.t: v. 结晶；使明确（crystallize 的异体）

e.en: Honey may {crystalize} after sitting in the pantry for months.
e.zh: 蜂蜜在储藏柜里放几个月后可能会结晶。

e.en: The discussion helped her ideas {crystalize} into a clear plan.
e.zh: 那次讨论让她的想法凝聚成一个清晰的计划。

crystalline.t: adj. 晶状的、清澈透明的

e.en: The mountain lake had {crystalline} water you could see through.
e.zh: 那座山间湖泊有着清澈见底的水。

e.en: Salt forms regular {crystalline} structures as it evaporates.
e.zh: 盐在蒸发时会形成规则的晶体结构。

e.en: The slow {crystallisation} produced unusually large sugar crystals.
e.zh: 缓慢的结晶过程产生了异常大颗的糖晶体。

e.en: Geologists studied the {crystallisation} of magma deep underground.
e.zh: 地质学家研究了地下深处岩浆的结晶过程。

e.en: Different {crystallisations} of the drug had varying solubility.
e.zh: 该药物不同的结晶形式具有不同的溶解度。

e.en: The lab compared several {crystallisations} of the same compound.
e.zh: 实验室比较了同一化合物的几种结晶形态。

crystallise.t: v. 结晶；（想法）变得清晰

e.en: Sugar will {crystallise} if you let the syrup cool too slowly.
e.zh: 糖浆冷却太慢的话糖就会结晶。

e.en: The team's vision began to {crystallise} during the workshop.
e.zh: 团队的愿景在研讨会上逐渐清晰成形。

e.en: Her opinions {crystallised} after reading the report.
e.zh: 读完那份报告后,她的观点变得明确起来。

e.en: The chef garnished the cake with {crystallised} ginger.
e.zh: 主厨用糖渍姜片装饰了蛋糕。

crystallises.t: v. 结晶（第三人称单数）

e.en: This essay nicely {crystallises} the author's main argument.
e.zh: 这篇文章很好地概括了作者的核心论点。

e.en: Honey {crystallises} faster when stored in the fridge.
e.zh: 蜂蜜放在冰箱里结晶得更快。

e.en: The debate is {crystallising} into two opposing camps.
e.zh: 这场辩论正逐渐形成两个对立的阵营。

e.en: He watched the salt slowly {crystallising} on the dish.
e.zh: 他看着盐在盘子上慢慢结晶。

e.en: Each {crystallite} in the metal affects its overall strength.
e.zh: 金属中每一颗微晶都会影响其整体强度。

e.en: Engineers measured the average {crystallite} size in the alloy.
e.zh: 工程师测量了合金中微晶的平均尺寸。

e.en: Slow cooling encouraged uniform {crystallization} of the compound.
e.zh: 缓慢冷却促使该化合物均匀结晶。

e.en: The workshop led to the {crystallization} of a new strategy.
e.zh: 那次研讨会促成了一项新战略的成形。

e.en: The chemist documented all {crystallizations} that occurred during testing.
e.zh: 化学家记录了测试中出现的所有结晶现象。

e.en: Different {crystallizations} of the molecule showed distinct properties.
e.zh: 该分子不同的结晶形式呈现出不同的性质。

e.en: A walk in the park helped her thoughts {crystallize}.
e.zh: 在公园里散步帮她理清了思路。

e.en: Pure water can {crystallize} into stunning ice patterns.
e.zh: 纯水可以结晶成令人惊叹的冰花图案。

e.en: The honey jar in the pantry has completely {crystallized}.
e.zh: 储藏柜里的那瓶蜂蜜已经完全结晶了。

e.en: His career goals finally {crystallized} after the internship.
e.zh: 实习之后,他的职业目标终于明确了。

crystallizes.t: v. 结晶（第三人称单数）

e.en: This single image {crystallizes} the spirit of the protest.
e.zh: 这张照片浓缩了这场抗议的精神。

e.en: Maple syrup {crystallizes} when boiled down too far.
e.zh: 枫糖浆熬得过头就会结晶。

e.en: The chemist watched the salt {crystallizing} at the bottom.
e.zh: 化学家看着盐在底部结晶。

e.en: Her plans for the company are slowly {crystallizing}.
e.zh: 她对公司的规划正在慢慢成形。

e.en: The {crystallographer} mapped the structure of a new protein.
e.zh: 那位晶体学家绘制出了一种新蛋白质的结构。

e.en: Rosalind Franklin was a brilliant {crystallographer} of her era.
e.zh: 罗莎琳·富兰克林是她那个时代杰出的晶体学家。

e.en: The team published detailed {crystallographic} data of the mineral.
e.zh: 团队发布了该矿物详细的晶体学数据。

e.en: X-rays revealed the {crystallographic} structure of the virus.
e.zh: X 射线揭示了该病毒的晶体结构。

e.en: X-ray {crystallography} helped scientists discover the DNA double helix.
e.zh: X 射线晶体学帮助科学家发现了 DNA 双螺旋结构。

e.en: She studies protein {crystallography} for drug discovery.
e.zh: 她研究蛋白质晶体学,用于药物发现。

e.en: Tiny ice {crystals} formed on the inside of the window.
e.zh: 窗户内侧结起了细小的冰晶。

e.en: She collects healing {crystals} from rock shops on her travels.
e.zh: 她旅行时会去矿石店收集疗愈水晶。

csa.t: n. 社区支持农业；儿童性侵（缩写，依语境）

e.en: We get fresh vegetables every week from a local {CSA}.
e.zh: 我们每周都从当地的社区支持农业获取新鲜蔬菜。

e.en: Joining a {CSA} supports nearby farmers throughout the season.
e.zh: 加入社区支持农业可以在整个季节支持当地农民。

csce.t: n. 欧洲安全与合作会议（缩写）

e.en: The {CSCE} eventually evolved into the modern OSCE in 1995.
e.zh: 欧洲安全与合作会议在 1995 年演变为如今的欧安组织。

e.en: Cold War diplomats negotiated security accords through the {CSCE}.
e.zh: 冷战时期外交官们通过欧洲安全与合作会议协商安全协议。

cse.t: n. 计算机科学与工程（缩写）

e.en: She's majoring in {CSE} with a focus on machine learning.
e.zh: 她主修计算机科学与工程,专注于机器学习方向。

e.en: The {CSE} department offers courses in algorithms and systems.
e.zh: 计算机科学与工程系开设算法和系统方面的课程。

csf.t: n. 脑脊液（cerebrospinal fluid 缩写）

e.en: Doctors test the {csf} to diagnose meningitis quickly.
e.zh: 医生检测脑脊液以快速诊断脑膜炎。

e.en: The lab sent the {csf} sample for analysis.
e.zh: 实验室把脑脊液样本送去化验。

csm.t: n. 客户成功经理；指挥服务舱（依语境）

e.en: Our {csm} guides the team through every sprint.
e.zh: 我们的Scrum认证主管在每个冲刺中指导团队。

e.en: She earned her {csm} certification last month.
e.zh: 她上个月考取了Scrum Master认证。

cso.t: n. 首席安全官（Chief Security Officer 缩写）

e.en: The {cso} reviews all data security policies quarterly.
e.zh: 首席安全官每季度审查所有数据安全政策。

e.en: Our new {cso} came from a major bank.
e.zh: 我们的新任首席安全官来自一家大型银行。

csu.t: n. 加州州立大学（缩写）

e.en: He transferred to {csu} for its engineering program.
e.zh: 他为了工程专业转学到加州州立大学。

e.en: The {csu} campus hosts a huge career fair.
e.zh: 加州州立大学校园举办了一场大型招聘会。

ctc.t: n. 反恐中心；联系（依语境缩写）

e.en: The recruiter quoted my {ctc} including bonuses and benefits.
e.zh: 招聘人员报出了包含奖金和福利的总薪酬。

e.en: Negotiate your {ctc} before signing the offer letter.
e.zh: 在签署聘书前先谈好你的总薪酬。

e.en: Press {ctl} plus C to copy the text.
e.zh: 按Ctrl加C键来复制文本。

e.en: The {ctl} key is stuck on my keyboard.
e.zh: 我键盘上的Ctrl键卡住了。

cuatro.t: n. 夸特罗（拉美四弦琴）

e.en: He strummed a lively tune on the {cuatro}.
e.zh: 他用四弦琴弹奏出一支欢快的曲子。

e.en: The {cuatro} is central to Venezuelan folk music.
e.zh: 四弦琴是委内瑞拉民间音乐的核心乐器。

e.en: The bear {cub} followed its mother into the woods.
e.zh: 小熊跟着妈妈走进了树林。

e.en: My nephew just joined the {cub} scouts.
e.zh: 我侄子刚加入了幼童军。

e.en: We spent two weeks exploring old Havana in {Cuba}.
e.zh: 我们在古巴的老哈瓦那游玩了两周。

e.en: {Cuba} is famous for its cigars and classic cars.
e.zh: 古巴以雪茄和老爷车闻名。

cuban.t:
adj. 古巴的
n. 古巴人

e.en: She ordered a classic {Cuban} sandwich for lunch.
e.zh: 她午餐点了一份经典的古巴三明治。

e.en: The band played upbeat {Cuban} salsa all night.
e.zh: 乐队整晚都在演奏欢快的古巴萨尔萨。

e.en: Each kid has a {cubby} for their backpack.
e.zh: 每个孩子都有一个放书包的小格子。

e.en: She tucked her keys into the entryway {cubby}.
e.zh: 她把钥匙放进门口的小格柜里。

cubbyhole.t: n. 狭小的空间；储物格

e.en: He found an old letter in the desk {cubbyhole}.
e.zh: 他在书桌的小格子里找到一封旧信。

e.en: The cafe has a cozy {cubbyhole} for reading.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆有个适合阅读的小角落。

cube.t:
n. 立方体；方块
v. 求立方

e.en: Drop an ice {cube} into your drink to cool it.
e.zh: 放一块冰块到你的饮料里降温。

e.en: The puzzle {cube} sat unsolved on his desk.
e.zh: 那个魔方还没解开,放在他桌上。

cubed.t: adj. 切成小方块的；三次方的

e.en: Three {cubed} equals twenty-seven in basic math.
e.zh: 在基础数学中,三的立方等于二十七。

e.en: She {cubed} the potatoes before roasting them.
e.zh: 她把土豆切成方块后再烤。

cubes.t:
n. 立方体（复数）
v. 切成方块

e.en: Add two ice {cubes} to chill the cocktail.
e.zh: 加两块冰块让鸡尾酒冷一些。
